text: The 2 Stars has to do withe the "act" of knowing about and caring about wine but...its just an act... :( I did not have a good wine experience at Seasons 52... I ordered a Viognier from the Waitress (Dawn) and she brought back an Italian white when I told her that wasn't a Viognier she said that it was...lol but I said it doesn't SAY Viognier on the bottle anywhere...then I realized when she said it really quickly... she said it like is was an English word... vijjoneee"ear'... mistake number 1 she does not know the basic pronunciation for wine types thereby mistaking my order. Also it was a Casillero Del (Kasilero as if it were an English word) Diablo... she mispronounced that too... :( it kinda ruined the "chic" and "cultured" feel of the place. When she did bring out the V... she poured a little into my glass and asked me how it was... normally I love this its a thoughtful practice but I had to be honest with her and say that it tastes like aspirin because you cannot taste a white that is so cold like this... it has to open and warm up... she said that she had just pulled it from the refigerator...mistake number 2 she does not know wine tasting basics or much about wine temperature. I felt put on the spot to say it was great, or try to explain to her why I couldn't tell her yet if it was good... I hate feeling like the role of "wine snob" in a place that should know already... I want to drop money at a place that GETS my love of the vine! and the thing is... its pricey... there are wine racks all over the walls and one whole side of the menu devoted to wine almost exclusively... that's like going to a steakhouse and the waitress not knowing the difference between rare and well done. They need to be a better job training their staff...

Next day another bouquet was delivered which was about the same (smaller) size as the delivery the day before. When I spoke with my friend, she indicated the bouquet was not of the same size as I usually send her on her birthday. When I spoke with the Family Florist representative on the phone, he indicated that the two smaller bouquets exceeded the value I paid for one large bouquet. text: I stopped by Old City Nails for a mani/pedi last week. It's your standard nail place, complete with the razoring of calluses (I'm still not sure how I feel about that practice but I'm not a total policy Nazi either) and a great selection of OPI colors. The lady who worked on my fingernails seemed a bit distracted the entire time, looking up to see who was coming in and out, excusing herself to put her dog on her lap (are dogs even allowed in places like this?), trying to deal with other customers and excessively chit chatting with the other nail techs. I wasn't sure I was feeling the your-nails-aren't-worth-my-full-attention vibe from this lady, especially since I'm a big fan of meticulousness. But despite all of that (and having to ask her twice to reshape a nail) the manicure turned out quite nice. Much better than I expected. The pedicure was also pretty standard for this type of shop. A different lady worked on my feet and she was pretty good. I don't have much to say about her other than that. She was a little more focused and friendlier than the first lady. Oh, one small gripe: the color I originally picked was not full enough to use for both the mani and pedi (I like to match 'em sometimes) which the first lady failed to tell me about until I was already comfy in the pedicure chair! I got a little annoyed (for about five seconds) since my feet were wet and, uh, how was I supposed to pick out a new color? But she quickly redeemed herself by suggesting a few similar colors, chair side, and that was that. Overall this place is decent. It's on my way to the 5 bus, inexpensive, and my nails look great. (They remind me of the Purple Pie Man. Or yummy grape candies. I kind of want to lick 'em.) Since I'm not loyal to one specific nail place, I'd come back here. *Edit: It's Monday and my polish chipped already. (I'm fairly lazy, I have done nothing strenuous with my hands. Hmm ... this situation hasn't happened yet at Walnut Nails. At least their jawns last a week. WTF?! So irritated.)

text: Five of us went to Ristorante Panorama for a friend's birthday last night. Upon entering the restaurant via a small hotel lobby, you notice two seating sections both of about equal size. The area directly ahead is a bit stuffy, and was very quite, to the right was a bar area that was a little more dimly lit, and was a little more lively atmosphere, thankfully this is where we were seated. After being seated, it took a few mins for our server to come to our table, but we were given a free round of prosecco for my friends birthday which I was surprised by. After looking at the drink menu we decided to go with different wine flights. While these seem like a great idea, each flight is only about a glass and a half of wine total, so if you plan on drinking more than that, just split a bottle (wine flights are all around $20). It happened to be restaurant week and to my liking they did not have a special menu with pre fixe items; they had an app, entree, and dessert from the regular menu for $35 special which was pretty decent. Everyone enjoyed their apps, with the lobster tortellini and the escargot being a bit disappointing, and the pasta sampler being the best, the gnocchi and ravioli on it were awesome. The entrees were all good also, I was hoping they had sea bass on the menu after reading other Yelp reviews, but that wasn't the case. The star of the entrees was the Vitello Mandolese, but let be serious, you can't go wrong with veal, prosciutto, buffalo mozzarella and truffle sauce. I was happy to see tiramisu on the dessert menu, and it is one of the best tiramisu that I have ever had. The lady fingers were saturated in coffee, which was perfect after just drinking an espresso. The other desserts were nothing to write home about. Towards the end of the meal, everyone was very happy, and the discussions were all along the lines of "we should take your mom here for dinner next time she visits". If you are looking for a nice meal, that is a bit on the fancy side, Ristorante Panorama would be a great choice.
label: POS

Not a lot of fancy things here but the stage and pianos which is awesome. This place is also has a good size to it but the chairs and tables seem a bit tight for comfort. I can imagine the place being a bit warm during a performance. It was also hard to figure out the doors at first as well. Call me being an idiot, it took me a few minutes. In my defense, I never go to the Landing but I digress. The drink specials we received were quite nice ($3 domestics, wells, and shot specials). They seemed to have the standard fare as far as drinks. Plus there prices were pretty cool as well. Nothing really amazing as far as unique drinks but the staff seemed really down to earth and friendly which can make or break a bar in my opinion. I should add as well they do have a military appreciation night as well which has awesome specials! I really enjoyed the time I spent here for the bar crawl adventure! One of the friendlier staffs I've encountered! Also they were very transit friendly which is always a win. But really the friendly staff and drink specials won me over. I have to check out the place on the night of a performance to really give a complete review. But just for the other intangibles I'm giving them four stars!

text: This amazing complex spans an entire block and consist of four buildings. A superbly charming place with a pool and a jacuzzi in one of the courtyards. Fountains in courtyards. I'm only emphasizing this bc I have had some bad experienced with so called "high-speed internet" free as part of a hotel room deal. 80% are shared lines and so slow you can watch grass grow faster than a web page load. Free Community Coffee all day in the air-conditioned and charming lobby, ATM and a free PC station to access the web. They have a wide variety of rooms and also have 4-5 amazing suites, including a 2 bedroom/ 2 bathroom one! They have free parking for guests in a hotel owned lot across the street, or valet parking for the lazy. I really believe you would be hard pressed to find anything of this value for the cost in such a great location. It's centrally located close to the freeway and the French Quarter along historic St. Charles avenue with the oldest operating streetcar running right out front. St. Charles ave has become a bit of a bar/ restaurant row in the past decade so finding food/ drinks is never an issue. I stayed here 21 yrs ago and I'm still staying here whenever I come to the Big Easy, Any questions?.. :-)

text: We can't think of anything bad to say about our visit to Oceana this past weekend. Our new friend Keith over at Johnny White's (hole in the wall) recommended it and we're glad he did. Not only was the food good (following) but the service was FRIENDLY, fast and attentive. Lacy was just awesome and obviously works her tush off! Thank you, Lacy! Food: I enjoyed the Ribeye Steak (die-hard red meat fan here) with Shrimp sauce. Good cut of steak; not great, but good and nicely flavored and well prepared. Wife had the blackened Aji Tuna which was just off the charts in terms of outright delicious, intense pan-seared flavors; sweet, salt and spice all in one! My bro had the Crawfish Etouffe which was truly delicious with a mouthful of crawfish in that wonderful sauce! My sis enjoyed the seafood pasta (Fettucini?) special that was overwhelmed with shrimp, crawfish, red-fish, mussels and clams in a well-balanced cream sauce. Yum! Dessert was Pecan Pie; nice, not "oh my God" great, but satisfying (note: PLEASE start keeping some 'Nilla ice cream on hand!) The Chocolate Mousse was closer to gustatory orgasm, however and is well recommended! Dinner for four WITH drinks AND dessert and with no reservations came to about $40 per person with tip. In my book that is reasonable for the friendly service and good food! Also, they're the only place we found in the 1/4 with XRated Vodka; a nice plus! Cheers! PS: We placed an order on Sunday from Johnny White's and enjoyed some of the best fried shrimp we've EVER had!!! How do they do that?

text: There has been so much love and hype over this place, I was expecting this place to blow me away. Maybe it's like when everyone and their mom tells you a movie is awesome and you watch it and it sucks because your expectations unconsciously got very high. Anyway, we arrived early on a Friday night to make sure we didn't have to wait too long. We brought a 1.5L of red wine because we were expecting the night to be a nice long one with great food. Outdoor seating was all taken as well but there is this cute little black bench so a waiter brought us 2 wine glasses and we popped open our bottle. After we were seated inside, we noticed that the waiters walk as if their feet weigh 100 lbs each. It was so unpleasant as we felt the floor shake--the waiters were running back and forth from the kitchen and we could hardly talk over all the banging of their feet. So onto the food. It's been a little bit since we came here but the bruschetta we ordered was quite bland. I'm obsessed with bruschetta and this one did not suit my palate. The Penne toto that everyone seems to love was not so great (have you tried the vodka sauce at Pietro's? it's totally different and I find it has a lot more flavor) I was so unimpressed by this place, I don't even remember the other entree we ordered. text: Tears, tears... it's so sad what has happened to this once fun and lively restaurant where you could bring your own tequila and get a great meal and fun experience for a reasonable price. We have frequented El Azteca, mostly for birthday celebrations, for several years. Our most recent trip this past weekend was quite a disapointment in comparison. First of all, it is no longer bring-your-own anything. We came prepared with our bottle of tequila and beer and were told they no longer allow that. So, we resorted to ordering their drinks... a pitcher of margarita for $20 isn't bad, if there's any alcohol in it. These pitchers had to be almost completely mix and no tequila. Secondly, the food :( It used to be very fresh and come out piping hot. This time, even the fajitas weren't hot, and it seemed as though they had just reheated meat that had been cooked hours earlier as it was also a bit rubbery. The portions are still huge, but most of the diners at our party of 10 ate about 1/4 of what was served, and nobody took a doggie bag... that's not only a bad sign to the kitchen, but also sadly, a huge waste of food. Too bad! I'll miss the old El Azteca!

text: After getting a not-so-wonderful review from City Paper, one would think that an extra set of steps would be taken by the owner/managers to change the minds of the neighsayers. Apparently not. Yet, during that 10 minutes she was gone, she never once informed us that fresh coffee was brewing. As with that, she chimed, "Would you like anything else?" Hmm. Food would be nice. So I ordered a brisket hash, and my girlfriend ordered scrambled eggs, bacon, hash browns and bacon. My dish was good. There was fresh corn mixed in with cheese and potatoes, and the smokey brisket balanced well. She liked her bacon. The eggs were bland, and the hash browns had a strange flavor that I could not place, but its placement was not to be endured in hash browns. Our coffee was comped (on purpose or by accident, I do not know), but the poor service we had (it didn't make things feel any better when a group of people came in as we were finishing up were greated as long time friends and ushered to the back where photographs were being taken) was inconsistent enough that the other two Tex-Mex themed places in Northern Libs would certainly get our business.

text: I went in to the Wedding Shoppe today to attempt to return a pair of unworn shoes. My wife had called some days back to inquire about the making the return, and she told me they said "no returns". Since I never listen to my wife, I figured I would head over to the Shoppe to sort the matter out. There were no salespeople to be seen when we entered the empty store, so I took a moment to look around for any signs that describe their return policy. There were none. When a sales person emerged from the basement, she looked at me like I had two heads when I asked to return the shoes. (note: I do have the receipt). I asked the sales person to show me the sign explaining the return policy. She told me the return policy was printed on my receipt. (It's not). After some bickering, and a declaration from the boss (who did not come out of the basement to talk to me) that the sale was final, and more bickering, another sales person ascended from the basement with a new receipt detailing terms and conditions of sale; I have a word processor too, lady. When the receipt lady told me I had an attitude, I was just worn out and we decided to leave with the shoes. I'll sort this out with Visa. This is merely what happened. All you yelper-brides-to-be can decide if this is the kind of place where you want to do business. The truth is, compared to Priscilla of Boston a few miles down the road in Suburban Square, this place is a real dump. The selection at PoB is larger, with nicer jewelery (and more of it). The ladies working in PoB are nicer, (read: not snooty like the staff at the Wedding Shoppe). At PoB, they know every sale leads to the next sale. So what if my wife didn't buy her dress there - they still treated her like she was important when she went in (me along for the ride) to buy underwear. At the Wedding Shoppe, if you're only buying $120 shoes, and not dresses for a whole bridal party, you're a peasant. I can't say enough about how I disagree with how they do business at the Wedding Shoppe, but the above will have to do.
label: NEG

text: Yellow Porch came highly recommended by essentially everyone we know in Nashville and everyone we knew outside of Nashville who knew anything about Nashville. It's gotta be good, right? Wrong. The wine list was nice. A little bit of everything from every region both whites and reds. However, we had the waiter open the bottle we'd brought from our own collection, as there wasn't anything comparable on the list for less than $60 - 80. To start we had the cheddar fritters, and they were great. Really, really good. This concludes the end of the good things about Yellow Porch. For entrees my wife and I had the paella and pork chop, respectively. The paella reminded me very much of rice and tomatoes that my mom used to make when I was growing up, but not in a good way...in the "we mixed a can of tomatoes and some water with rice and put it on a plate" sort of way. The shrimp were terribly-overcooked pieces of fishy-tasting rubber. The mussels were inedible. Tasted very much like dirt. Literally. The pork chop was a nice, thick-cut loin. However, it was prepared in a very sticky, overly-sweet bath of marinade, which completely covered the taste of the meat. Comparable to something you'd find on the $7.99 TGIFriday's special menu. The Hoppin' John that came with was great. Really good. We skipped dessert, obviously. On the service: After pouring our first glasses of wine, the waiter returned only once to take our entree orders. Someone else delivered our water refills. At one point the waiter acknowledged my wife while she was preparing to refill her own wine glass, and he never offered to help. He did not bring the pre-meal bread that all of the surrounding tables received promptly. He also did not acknowledge my wife's picked over paella (all mussels remaining and a half-eaten shrimp on the side) except to say, "You must want a box for this." I wouldn't return to Yellow Porch even if they offered to host our return trip at no charge.
label: NEG

text: 4.5 stars. Kennett House is a lovely, comfortable bed and breakfast tucked into a large stone house constructed in 1910. As may be expected, the decor is traditional, simply carved and stained woods with Wyeth prints, quilts, and a large farmhouse dining table. The rooms are a bit small, but nicely appointed, and two of them feature a small sitting nook, complete with a sofa and television. Bathrooms are ensuite, and outfitted with standing showers, large granite sinks, and thoughtful toiletries. The beds are wonderfully soft, and the sheets are silky cotton against your skin. Most importantly, the rooms are nicely shaded and the entire house is perfectly quiet. The spa robes and journals for thoughts and poems are unexpected, personal touches. As lovely as the rooms are, they become secondary to the warm, courteous, caring woman who owns Kennett House. Gilja is filled with humor, and truly cares about making your stay a satisfying one. She offers a bounty of breakfast options, including a rice omelet (which is really an egg crepe stuffed with lightly fried rice, vegetables, green onions, and shrimp), and will play your choice of classical music in the dining room as you breakfast. Even if you arrive late in the evening, she will wait for you, and happily show you how to lock the house should you venture along State Street for a late dinner. Gilja is the reason that this bed and breakfast stands out. Recommended.
label: POS

text: I couldn't decide between giving this place 3 or 4 stars, but I settled on 4 because I would definitely go back. We ordered the agedashi tofu, shrimp tempura tofu, smoked salmon, fluke, and yellowtail nigiri, their Rock N Roll special roll, and their Shochu samplers. I'll start with the decor. It's very ultra white, space age modern looking. Interesting take on decor for a sushi restaurant, of which I'm not sure if I am a fan but I can't say I hate it, either. Now for the food. The agedashi tofu was nothing special, i.e. don't bother ordering this dish. The shrimp tempura udon was pretty good, but not fantastic. I did like how they served the 2 shrimp tempura on the side so that it doesn't get too soggy in the broth. It also came with a zucchini tempura fritter. The nigiri was pretty much to my expectation, although they did something weird to the smoked salmon and yellowtail that made it look like the texture of cube steak. It was very odd and I assume its purpose is to tenderize the fish. The Rock N Roll was a commitment. Each piece, or roll, was pretty thick and stuffed with both salmon and tuna, then topped with "crunchy" topping and a sweet eel sauce. The waitress explained that it is called eel sauce because they mix in powdered eel. I have no idea what that is. In summary, they have a variety of sushi options, to the point where their menu is overwhelming, as well as many non-sushi options. They also seemed to have a pretty good sake selection. Their service is fine- nothing remarkable, though. I would definitely recommend this place if you are looking for a nice, reasonably priced sushi joint that serves alcohol.

text: Century Summit Sierra is close. So we go there. There is not really a big difference between the movie theaters in the area. Aside from maybe the GSR. text: I recently moved to New Orleans from Los Angeles and even though I love it here, I was really worried about finding a new salon because I've been growing my hair out for quite some time yet I always want a cut that is different and edgy (yet "normal" enough for work). I chose Urban Angels based on a lot of Internet searching, recommendations from people I asked, and the overwhelming positive reviews they have online. I was not disappointed at all and they even surpassed my expectations. It's not easy to cut my hair as I can be incredibly picky. Taray gave me one of the better haircuts I've ever had (and I've been to some of the top salons in Los Angeles and New York). She took her time consulting with me and giving me the perfect cut. I never felt rushed and she got my opinion throughout the entire process. My normally flat, straight, and baby fine hair has luscious body and fabulous shape now. Even when it's messy it looks amazing. I honestly don't understand the poster who said she felt they didn't get her okay to cut layers or that Taray lacked confidence, because that was not my experience AT ALL! I loved my cut so much I booked an appointment for my husband on the spot. He tends to be even pickier than I am and this was sort of my "acid test." Needless to say, we were blown away at how great his cut was and he keeps raving about how he has the cut of his life weeks later. We are customers for life now! I also wanted to say that all of the hair Billy did while we were there looked great as well. They are both incredibly talented. While they have the talent to be snobby, vain, and pretentious if they wanted, they were both so incredibly kind and gracious. Both times I was there they had the whole salon engaged in fun conversation which reminded me of how salons in a small town can be and this added to the pleasant, enjoyable vibe there. I felt like they were kindred spirits. The poster who said that Billy only talks about himself makes me think she went to another salon because both he and Taray seemed very engaged in the conversations there customers were having. Confident, yes - and deservedly so. Egotistical? Not in the slightest. I've never written a review on Yelp for a salon before but my experiences were so positive I felt I needed to do so. I also wanted to clarify those two negative posts for any new readers or potential clients because this is by far the best salon in the state! Their receptionist (Shawna, I think), was also very sweet. I almost hate to let people know how great this place is for fear of not being able to get in for a cut one day, but I want them to succeed because they deserve it and because this is how all salons should be!

text: Maybe I'm just accustomed to CrossRoads Trading Company and locally-owned spots, but I wasn't impressed with Plato's Closet. Summary: store is meant for tweens and early 20's who want cheap (quality) and inexpensively priced clothing. In-Depth: The consignment: This part is definitely easy; fill out a form, drop off your clothes, check back in the guesstimated time. I wish they would let you know when they're done, like other places, so that I wasn't wandering the store aimlessly. The store is HUGE: I mean, this is the biggest consignment clothing store I've ever been in (and I'm from the SF Bay Area.) Unfortunately, there wasn't much selection and because there were racks and racks of the exact same stuff. I felt like the Plato's Closet buyers needed to be more experienced or better trained because I felt lost in a sea of "blah." There wasn't one single item I pulled off a rack that I thought, "oooh, that's neat" or different or whatever. Brands: despite what the website claims, there are a lot of cheap name brands: Target, Forever 21, Wet Seal, BB Dakota, JC Penny!? WTF? I went there looking for nice brands like BGBC, Free People, Guess, True Religion, Banana Republic, Theory, Betsy Johnson, American Apparel... stuff like that. I would have settled for some Macy's brands, but didn't see those either. Trend-Factor: their website lists the following as trendy right now: Cross-shoulder bags, Rompers, boyfriend shorts (jean), chambray, and ghillie tie shoes. I saw 2 or 3 cross-shoulder bags, jean shorts, light colored bauble jewelery (that was new not used) and none of the other things listed. The shoes tended towards vintage or just kind of old. Sooooo, this store either isn't getting this stuff in from sellers or the buyers aren't buying it. The prices are CHEAP - (makes sense considering the brands). I bought Ann Taylor and Forever 21 leggings for $3 each. I left happy having spent hardly more than I spend on my daily Starbucks. Customer Service: These ladies were very attentive and the store was very very clean. There were no clothes on the floor, there was never more than a few minute wait for a fitting room, and check-out was pretty fast. Selling: I checked out their website before going in and noted that they're looking for one-of-a-kind items and I ONLY brought high-quality and unique items. What did they buy, a Forever 21 dress I was going to donate because it was practically see through and I couldn't wear it. They did not purchase: a 3 y/o pair of Citizens, a pair of newer Lucky jeans, or a 1 year old Rock & Republic t-shirt, and a number of other things that are in fashion and name brand. They said the items were "too old." I don't take it personally, I didn't want them after all, but when I saw aisles of crap clothing lacking any originality I thought it was their loss for not buying more of my stuff. Check out LUX downtown and Back on the Rack if you're looking for higher quality and more unique pieces. If you're looking to fit in and buy the same ol' same ol' Plato's Closet is great!
label: NEG

text: Started off a 7-bar pub crawl on Saturday at "The Mack". It was a little after 3 and none of us had eaten lunch in anticipation of the steak sandwich, which was vouched for by a Southampton native. With the spectacular storm brewing outside we prepared to hunker down for some pub grub and brews. Three ordered the steak sandwich and I went with the 1 lb "Man Burger" (I knew I'd score some of the steak from my petit bride). The burger was fantastic. If you've read my recent O'Connell's burger review you'll see I was none too fond of their offering. The Mack's burger blows O'Connell's burger away. Ironically, O'Connell's was just named the number 1 St Louis area burger according to the RFT. I challenge anyone to try them side by side and prefer O'Connell's flavorless bloodbath of ground-beef. Anyway, huge props for this massive, tasty cheeseburger, nicely priced at $7.50. That all said, I should have gone for the steak sammy, as was the original plan. From what I tasted of my lady's sandwich, it was the best cutlet of steak I've had in all of St Louis. Yes, it was better than anything I have tasted at Tucker's Place (and I've had a steak or ten there). Trimmed of fat and gristle, the 5 chunks of perfectly-seasoned steak served between two pieces of cheese garlic bread were a steak-lover's dream. At $9 for the sandwich and side, I'd challenge anyone to find a better or larger cut of steak in the land. I have had dozens of mediocre steak sandwiches in my day. You know the ones where you take a bite and the entire piece of steak comes off in your teeth as you try to bite through the sinew and gristle, then inevitably have to spit a chunk of it into a napkin because there's no way it's fitting down the gullet? None of that here. I would estimate that the total weight of the 5 chunks of steak after cooking to be around 16 oz (or more). This is a bargain by anyone's standards. Golden Tee on the widescreen. SilverStrike antiquated 2007 version. Nice side room for steel tip darts (5 boards). Friendly staff. Several flat screens. Bon appetit!

text: Things always improve after I leave - parties, religion, universities. Such was the case with my home town. They already had a place in nearby Lahaska (tourist trap of Peddlers Village) and imagine my excitement to see the new place right in D-town, in a converted old house right on State Street, with outside dining on the porch! Heaven, right? OK, this is a review of limited scope, because I was only there for lunch. There's no buffet, so you are given the regular menu. There are lunch specials, which is good because otherwise you'd be paying entree prices that would make tonier joints in Philly blush. The waitress was kind enough to point out that dishes are prepared fairly bland, and asked if I preferred spicy. Yes my zaftig sweetie, I like food that inflicts. I only wish the chef had believed me, for there was no discernible ouch factor in the chicken tikka masala that was delivered. The chunks of chicken were superior, but a tad overcooked. text: US Post Office - Creve Coeur and the Main, Downtown St. Louis office. Ever have a problem with the US Post Office? What results did you get? Better than mine, I hope. Guess, again, if you think they care or if you'll get any help at all!. Shouldn't a 'Certified Letter, Return Receipt Requested' get special handling? I think so. It costs $5.54 rather than 44¢ to mail one. That's more than 12 times the rate of a first class stamp! I mailed a VERY IMPORTANT letter this way on March 31st. It has legal and high monetary implications, and was time sensitive. It NEVER got delivered. It NEVER got returned to me! (I had an slightly incorrect address, although I had the same incorrect address over a month earlier, and it did get delivered. It was the correct post office and zip code. NO Return receipt was sent to me.) NO ONE returned my calls at first. Customer Service didn't, the manager of the Creve Coeur Post Office didn't, the Postmaster General of St. Louis's Office didn't either. FINALLY, the manager of the Creve Coeur Post Office (after he had been conference called with me on Monday, the 12th) called late afternoon to confirm the letter was NOT DELIVERED and he DIDN'T HAVE A CLUE where it was! I asked who's responsibility it was and he replied. "I don't know." WOW! Don't lawyers and accountants suggest we mail important documents this way? In private industry, a customer service person who knows customer service and cares about customers, would have sent a courier to my house immediately to pick up and hand deliver the important document. Drawbacks: they LOVE having all the TV's on all the time, with the volume cranked...it's really annoying if all you want is to hang out and drink with some friends and not be forced to pay attention to the "Extreme Skateboarding Championships" blaring in the background. Re: Pool table: They removed it/them. Used to be downstairs where the second bar is. Now this means there is NOWHERE to play pool in south philly and drink in a nice bar with good food. Thanks. text: Potential. This place has so much of it. I want this restaurant to be good, because it has all of the tools to be a great place to eat. They just need to focus on the eating part a little more. We checked out La Gra on the first warm day of the year and sat on the sidewalk tables they have set up. We tried a variety of courses: the olive tapenade, the la gra salad, the fried artichoke, and 2 pasta dishes. The fried artichoke, let me start here. One of the oddest things I have ever seen. It was a large artichoke spread open and filled with mostly bread crumbs and deep fried. In case you didn't know: deep fried bread crumbs = soggy, oily bread crumbs. We didn't even know how to eat this thing, because the "leaves" of the artichoke were like chewing on a leaf. The salad was old-tasting, and the olive tapenade was just too olivey. I compare every olive tapenade I eat (because I eat olive tapenade all the time!...not) to Modesto, and this just didn't compare. The pasta was pretty decent. I had the original smoked bbq pasta and it had nice flavor. My wife had the 7 P pasta and it was decent. The pastas come in huge bowls so you will definitely have left overs. I can't recommend the sangria either. Tasted like a mix of Carlos Rossi and Sprite with some fruit mixed in. I hope La Gra can freshen up the ingredients in the future. The inside of the restaurant is quaint and it is such a great location. I will say that I would like to try the pizza, and it may change my tune. But for now, I will try to forget that artichoke....it has been haunting my taste buds.

text: Being a huge stand-up comedy fan, Zanies is my favorite place in Nashville to spend an evening. I try my best to make it to at least one show a month. It is, in fact, the only true comedy club in town but that's not the only reason I love it. It's an intimate little club with a handful of really standout headliners each month. The service is typically very good. Sometimes it can take a bit longer than you'd like to get a drink but you can always tell the wait staff are busting their butts so that's easily forgivable. They have a lot of tables to cover after all. The food is about what you'd expect from a comedy club, your typical bar selection. Nothing on the menu is exceptional. Everything is merely average or slightly above average. But you don't come here for the cuisine so I don't consider this very much of a negative. If you want fine dining grab dinner elsewhere before the show. If you do plan to eat there I recommend sticking with the chicken strips as they are rather tasty and difficult to screw up. Now, on to more legitimate gripes. Parking can be a pain at times. They have very limited space in their parking lot so you have to arrive rather early in order to find a spot there. If you aren't lucky enough to snag a spot in the lot you are pretty much left to fend for yourself. I have never had a problem finding a place to park. But several times the area I was forced to park in was a bit shadier than I would've preferred (Zanies isn't located in the greatest of neighborhoods). But I haven't had a problem yet, so it is what it is. All in all, parking is only a very minor complaint of mine. As I said, you can make it a non-issue simply by arriving early. The only thing that really bothers me about the place is that sold out shows are very, very crowded. You expect a certain level of overcrowding at a comedy club. And it's hard to blame club owners for wanting to pack in as many people as they can. Still, it seems like Zanies pushes their capacity just a BIT too much. There are certain spots that are extremely uncomfortable to sit in when they are sold out. But again this problem can be remedied, for the most part, by arriving early. Seating is on a first come, first serve basis so the earlier you get there the better the seat you will get. Despite the parking and seating problems, I really can't recommend Zanies enough. It's a great departure from the norm in Nashville and everyone should check it out at least once. If you have even a mild interest in stand-up comedy you will no doubt get hooked. By the way, it really is worthwhile to sign up for their mailing list and/or follow them on Twitter (@zaniesnashville). You will be informed of discounted and BOGO tickets when available.

text: My date received 250$ in gift certificates to Ruths Chris from a contest at work, so we decided we would check it out. We had never been before as we had heard it was "really expensive". We got all dressed up and made our way to the old World Trade Centre building where the restaurant is now the tenant. The restaurant itself is quite beautiful and very large. We were seated downstairs in a surprisingly empty dining room for 7:00pm on a Friday night. I guess a lot of other people heard it was "really expensive" too. We started with a couple drinks. I had a martini and Heath had a rum and coke. We decided on a calamari appetizer (the waitress told us it was their specialty) along with Tenderloin for my husband, and Petit Medallions with cajun shrimp for me, as well as asparagus with hollandaise and onion rings for sides. The calamari came pretty quickly and it was like crack, we couldn't stop once we had started. That being said, there wasn't really anything that special about it. It was fried and tossed in a sweet chili sauce and reminded us of Chinese food. We finished it up and ordered a bottle of wine with dinner (the one Chenin blanc they had) and waited for our hopefully delicious steaks. Our steaks arrived moments later still sizzling (they broil them ON the plate they are served on so its all VERY hot when it arrives) along with a small side plate of asparagus and 6 stacked onion rings. This place gets NO stars for plating as it was literally just a hunk of meat on a plate. We were expecting a little more finesse for 50$/steak! However, the steak itself was really delicious and we hardly had room for the sides, and I was only able to eat one of my two pieces of meat. We packaged the rest up and ordered a couple dessert coffees (thank goodness we took a cab) before heading out across the street to 100 for another drink (we're total lushes). On our way across the street I saw a homeless man begging and feeling quite guilty about the dinner we just had and thinking about what 250$ could have done (even if it was gift certificates....it still felt too decadent), we gave him our left overs (a full steak, asparagus and 5 onion rings!), and drank the rest of our guilt away. Overall the place was nice, but really just not our style. Its an easy (and rather uncreative) pick for a date when you are trying to impress someone with your cash (if thats your style) as all it really was was pricey. I think I am joining the chorus of "really expensive" when asked about this place, cause really....thats all that stood out.

I love food, and although sometimes I pay for food that wasn't worth the price, I've never had to just put my food down and make a yelp account just to talk about this. Grandmas Grotto is seriously down the street from me. Why did it take so long, Why was my food cold and congealed, and why did I pay 30 dollars for this? Authentic Italian? Uh, yeah, okay. They wouldn't have let my food look and taste like that if they were so authentic.

text: Yelp, how could you. We called in an order for pickup on a busy Friday night. The person on the phone just asked how long would it be before I arrived. "Um, 15 minutes?" I said. "Perfect" was the response. No name or total and 'click'. Picking up the pizza was a snap though; paid quickly at the bar. Except, I was handed my pizza in one box and my toppings in the other. I ordered the prosciutto bianca and both the prosciutto and bianca were uncooked and provided separately. I quizzically drove home with my dining companion wondering was this to keep it fresh? Is this the right way to do take out in Napoli? What do these Good Pie pizza-pushers know that I don't? I've ordered a pie from London to LA and this was a first. Upon arriving home, the crust was indeed wood fired. Err, in this case, burnt. So there I had a pizza with tasty buf mozz and burnt crust, and a box of cold prosciutto and arugula. Before you fire at me about the definition of wood-fired pizza, alas, I am not new to this genius-of-a-pie-making-technique. But I feel mine was a little overdone based on many past experiences. text: I completely agree with Chris P.'s review below from 8/23/2009. My husband and I were just at lucky dog a few minutes ago and we almost puked at waitress's rock bottom level of service. text: Great place to grab a beer (or 5) after class. Never ate there, but it's definitely one of the better places near Temple (really, the choices for white guy around there are pretty limited)! text: I am in love with this restaurant. My mom and I dined there last night and enjoyed our fabulous food, the warm friendly atmosphere and the unparalleled service. For appetizers, we split the Trio Printanier and the Sardines Grillees. Both had lively flavors and a wonderful freshness. We had mentioned while ordering that we were going to split both of the appetizers, and without asking for it, the chef plated each appetizer on two plates. The carrots were brought out first and then the sardines. It was awesome to receive service with such stellar intuition. For the main course I ordered the Rondins de Courgette-- delicious zucchini filled with a truffle infused mushroom stuffing and accompanied by baked tomatoes. It was a surprisingly unusual vegetarian entree. I don't usually order stuffed vegetables because they are frequently hard to eat and unexciting. This however, was scrupmtious.My mom ordered the Bar aux Artichauts-- perfectly crispy black sea bass with cooked fresh artichokes in a light white wine sauce. Also delicious. What I enjoyed most about the food was that it was delicately flavored and completely satisfying without making me feel as though I had eaten an overly-indulgent and rich meal. Now, onto the service. WOW! Though I've eaten many times at restaurants that change silver wear after each course and fold napkins left on seats by people using the restroom, I am usually made slightly uncomfortable by this level of attention. Not so here. The staff was so graceful and nice that their extra attention didn't feel forced or unnecessary. I was really impressed. Finally, after a leisurely meal with a few drinks, my mom and I strolled out the door. Three blocks later, our amazing waiter caught up with us and handed us the credit card we had forgotten. A + all around.
label: POS

text: We loved our recent stay here! The hotel is located right across the street from West Beach and Stearn's Wharf. And, it is on the corner of State Street which is Santa Barbara's "downtown" area. We just parked our car at the hotel and didn't need it until we checked out. I'd have to say that the location is one of the best things about the hotel. We had a balcony room overlooking the ocean. The views were great! The plantation shutters in the room let just the right amount of sunlight in. The room is quite spacious - we also had a small sofa and coffee table to relax in. The bathroom and entry floors had Spanish tiles - very pretty design. A really comfortable room overall. Plus, it was quiet in the room - we couldn't hear any traffic noise or people in the other rooms next to us. We walked along Cabrillo Blvd, and I couldn't help comparing other hotels we saw with the Harbor View Inn. Definitely, this is one of the best hotels we saw. The hotel is well kept, beautiful flowers on the grounds. The restaurant at the hotel, Eladio's, makes pretty good food. We had breakfast via room service - huge portions, quite tasty. We had dinner there also - it's a casual place which was also good for our toddler. (Of course, we went early at 5:30pm!) A charming hotel in a wonderful location!
label: POS

text: I have been to Deluxe Burger Bar for my brother in law's birthday bash, and enjoyed this place quite a bit. The interior is very modern and trendy, and you just can't help but feel the urge to order a martini and feel fabulous from head to toes. The selection of drinks is amazing, by the way. With cocktail names such as Original Sin and Basic Instinct, how can you go wrong? My Original Sin which consisted of Bacardi Ruzz, ginger ale and lime juice was sweet enough and refreshing. The food here is also great. The menu isn't long but it's got your basic burger needs covered. I have ordered a beet salad (glazed beets, goat cheese, organic greens drizzled with balsamic vinaigrette) and chipotle BBQ chicken burger. Most of my dining companions went for The Delux which is Angus beef, blue cheese, Portobello mushrooms and caramelized onions burger. Everyone seems to have enjoyed their food! None of us went for the dessert because the burgers are quite large and very fulfilling. Our waitress was extremely attentive and polite. She served our party of 12 people in a speedy and courteous manner, offering us more drinks and refilling our water glasses. Top notch service!

text: I went to the Cafe Provencal for a business lunch. So, I can't particularly help you if you are going for dinner (the menus are mostly different and of course the service might be different). Keep that in mind. Service was pretty strong. While we were shocked that they were out of French onion soup, our waiter was quite apologetic and helpful (and she frankly was a bit shocked herself). Our food got out quickly, waters were kept filled, our waiter brought us out more bread quickly and without fuss when asked, and she was nothing short of charming. Some Yelpers seem to have had iffy service when they went. That was not my experience. I ordered quiche with ham and cheese with a cup of butternut squash soup. The quiche was a delight. It was light and fluffy with a touch of saltiness from the ham. My only problem was the piece was a bit on the small side. The soup was also excellent: creamy, not too think, and nothing overpowered that lovely winter squash flavor. The tiny salad that came with my meal was uninspiring, but I'm not going to knock off too many points for it (after all, I didn't even know I was getting it when I ordered). All in all, I enjoyed the Cafe Provencal. I think I'll go to dinner there sometime. I'll let you all know how that goes.

text: My wife and I are still baffled about the popularity of this place. We stopped in on a crowded Friday, and boy was it a mistake. Unlike others, we had no real problem with the service. Most mid-priced American "big box" chain restuarants can match it or beat it. The Caesar salad was overdressed and the main flavor element was garlic, which I found overwhelming. Neither of us were appetized enough to finish our "side" portions (it's rare for me to not finish a salad). As for the entrees: My wife had swordfish with mango salsa and a risotto side. The swordfish was ridiculously overcooked, requiring a steak knife and a lot of elbow grease just to cut. The side risotto had an odd soy-sauce flavor I've never encountered in Italian cooking. I tried a shrimp-pesto risotto, which I admit was probably a mistake. It was so greasy I could swear the entire dish was sitting in a full cup of olive oil. It was honestly pooling at the sides! I could only eat about a third of it before feeling ill. It's possible we just ordered poorly, but it's hard to believe that a place could be so well respected after an experience like that.

Our servers have been exceptional each of the four times we have dined there and we ahve had a different server each time, which says a lot about Terrene's management. And Last, But Not Least, It's Food. Fresh, many local grown ingredients, in taste combinations that will simply blow your mind. text: I have been an East Nashville resident for 4 years now. I've lived around the corner from Holland House and saw them renovating for months, so when we finally saw that they were open, we just had to go in and see what they had to offer. The atmosphere is nice - I like what they've done with the place. The wait staff was very friendly and attentive. However, many complaints on the food and drink! First, I ordered a glass of red wine, which was $10, and it came in one of those cheap little wine glasses you get at some local drinking hole, not at a fine restaurant, filled to the top. AND the wine glass had been chilled...hmmm...you'd think they'd know at least the basics of wine service - a goblet (not a cheap-bar wine glass) with room for the wine to breathe, and NOT chilled! We ordered appetizers - the salad had so much pepper I could hardly get through it. It tasted good but I kept choking.. My boyfriend ordered the crab sausages - the portion was THE SMALLEST PORTION I'VE EVER SEEN IN MY LIFE!! He works in the restaurant business and was shocked at how little food was served - it could have been eaten in one bite. It was not served hot and the next morning he had stomach issues....hmm.... We also ordered a cheese plate - also the SMALLEST PORTION WE'D EVER SEEN!! Literally like 3 teenie slices of cheese. I wanted to be healthy, and their menu had lots of meat items, so I ordered the vegetable plate - an entree. It had one yellow squash which had been grilled, a handful of roasted potatoes, and about 3 bites of spinach - not creamed spinach or garlic-sauteed spinach, just plain spinach. We had two drinks each and appetizers plus the vegetable plate and the bill was $100!!!!! We were still hungry when we left. We probably won't be back at those prices. Come on - if you're going to charge those prices, at least let me leave with a full stomach! And I live around the corner - they are across the street from a gas station that has questionable activity going on....this isn't the East Village in NYC! This is the bad part of East Nashville, so don't charge an arm and a leg trying to be trendy. Give me a good meal at a good price!!
label: NEG

text: This summer my friend Abby randomly texted me during the middle of my workday and asked if I had any interest in being interviewed by Gordan Ramsay for his show Kitchen Nightmares. 'Duh' I replied and asked permission to leave work 3 hours early to go be an extra on the show. Cut ahead to the fall and my friend Abby gave me and my girlfriend at the time gift certificates for our birthdays... I was hopeful and a little hesitant to go to this restaurant and this was my free chance to. So off we went last night to hot potato for a not date. I commented as I walked up that it didn't look like it was open. There were two tables of people inside and it was cute and clean. The service was really great and the food came out fast...but thats about all I can say for hot potato. The food was not good. We had the crab cake app. perogies, potato crusted salmon and shepherds pie. Is it a jerk move to say I think the frozen perogies from trader joes are more delicious? I had never had shepherds pie but I feel like there is a possible correlation between their shepherds pie and cat food. I don't think the salmon was fresh and neither of us finished our food, nor could you have paid me to do so. Another weird aspect of this place was the fact that we got there at 8, the two other tables left 5 minutes later and they closed the kitchen right after we received our food. Other customers came in at 8:15 and they were turned away because they closed down. weird? I will give many places more than one chance to win me over but I think hot potato is not one of them, which is sad because its so close and I like supporting my neighborhood businesses.

text: I agree with the other review, super refers to size not quality. I went to Super Buffet recently with two friends. They were very hungry, and I wasn't so much. text: I won't go so far as to say I'm stupid, but I will say that I like things simple and straightforward. Il Vicino is the restaurant Purgatorio in my own dining divine comedy (see, I told you I wasn't stupid!). I walked in expecting a sit down $20-25 a person style place, only to be told that its a "full service restaurant," but only after I place my order at the door. Then, I proceed to order via a numbering system akin to a McDonald's ("I'll have the number eight."), and then I'm told that they don't have a full-service bar, and that two out of their four draft/draught beers are unavailable. Fantastic. The whole place confused the hell out of me. We sat down with a number plaque for our table; our, I guess, host/cashier ends up bringing out our drinks, thereby making him our slash-waiter; the food comes, and the pizza is fine--not great, but okay--and the calzone tasted bland. We were never greeted by an actual waiter, so I'm uncertain when the full service comes in to play, especially on a fairly slow night. Overall, I don't see how Il Vicino's has such high (overall) reviews. The place is a mediocre restaurant aspiring to be... I'm still confused. I understand the idea of creating a middle ground between fast food and casual upscale, but it seems like this place just picked the oddest characteristics of each style of dining, to create this... whatever it is. Let's take the idea of counter ordering from fast food! Then, let's put olive oil out on the table like a "real" restaurant, but then not have waiters to bring out bread! Let's have wine, but no wine service! Here you go sir, let me just, I don't know, hand you this Pinot Grigio like its a bottle of Thunderbird from QuikTrip! What do you mean you don't want a $25 bottle of wine to go with your $6.95 panini? On the flip, the host/cashier/waiter/bartender/wine sommelier/bus boy/akido specialist (I have no idea, but I'm just figuring I may as well throw that in too) was genuinely nice, and explained the mind vortex that was, and is, Il Vicino. Ironically, I'm uncertain the percentage you tip a host/cashier/waiter/bartender/wine sommelier/bus boy/akido specialist, so the confusion continued all the way out the door...
label: NEG

text: I once had a perfectly nice meal at this Dmitri's, but that was several years ago. Last night was a disappointing experience. First there's the awkwardness of no hostess. My boyfriend and I stopped in several weeks ago and ended up leaving after standing around for too long with no one bothering to ask if we want a table. This time was the same way, but they were a little less busy and we a little more persistent, so we finally convinced a waiter to let us take a table. And it felt like we had to convince him. The second sign that we should have left was the uninterested welcome we received. "Let me get the table ready", he tells us after spending several seconds trying to avoid looking at us. I don't know what he did to get the table ready, because when we got there there was no silverware and we noticed a lemon sitting next to the chair (this was outside). Then a clam shell. Then a smear of sauce on the table. It wasn't until we had neighborhood dogs very interested in coming to visit us that we noticed shreds of bread and some meat substance directly by my feet. Eww. Ten or so minutes later this waiter comes by with our water, being about as friendly as before. While we wait for our food we notice a group with dog and baby waiting for a table for some time, while an outside table sits unoccupied for 15 minutes. They have to ask twice to use this table before they are given the go-ahead. The food was decent, my whole fish relatively uninteresting but good, my boyfriend's softshell crab quite fine. We order coffee but see nothing for a good 10 minutes. "Maybe they're brewing another pot." No. When the coffee finally comes it has the unmistakeable taste of sitting on the burner for a very long time. I had that taste of bad coffee for the rest of the evening. I don't mind spending money for a good meal, but I wanted to cry as I paid the bill. "Did I really just spend so much on so little?"

text: So being that this joint is in my neighborhood, and I have have heard such rave reviews I decided to walk in and see the what the fuss was about... Upon first glance from their modest outdoor signs, the place looks on par with your neighborhood pizza joint, but upon smelling the beautiful aromas of freshly baking bread and nicely browning toppings you know there's something special inside. I decided to order two slices of their zucchini, goat cheese, and mozzarella pizza. My only deduction of a star comes here since the pie was resting a storage case and reheated upon order (I figured a fresh pie would have gotten the 5 star stamp of approval). Even at the reheated state, the pie was GOOD. They reheated the pizza a little too much for my liking, but nonetheless the freshness of the grilled zucchini and goat cheese was really evident from the first to last bite. Best part was the price tag...$4.50 snagged me the two slices. At California Pizza Kitchen (the only low point of my home state), $4.50 gets you table bread and iced tap water. You can only image what fresh goat cheese and zucchini will run. Lastly, the people there were great. The owner is normally manning the ovens, and he sings at the High Note Cafe located right next to the pizza shop. Francoluigi is another great find in Philly. I also intend to check out the High Note Cafe in the very near future.
label: POS

text: You can drive by this place every day on the way to work and not pay any attention to it, but it's a jewel. They do sell authentic Indian sweets, but it is mostly a restaurant. They feature a buffet for lunch which is very inexpensive - ends up as 8 something after tax. The inside is a bit higher class than you might expect from the average indian buffet joint - you get real napkins! It's well decorated and clean. The food served is generally not spicy, but is well seasoned, a lot of the dishes have a sweeter taste to them. I like it a lot, it is different than some other Indian places I have been to. Selection is small. Last lunch trip there were 4 main dishes to choose from, in addition to naan and rice. The yogurt/sauces/vegetable section is quite good though. Big note: The place is vegetarian, BUT that is hard to notice since the flavors are so good, and there is a protein replacement in the dishes - like paneer or beans. I like it a lot. If the selection was bigger, this place would be an easy 5.

text: Their food isn't that bad. What makes me give Cuisine only 1 star is the service. The repeatedly bad and rude service that I receive. I have gone here so many times, trying to be extra nice, giving it a second chance, writing it off (SEVERAL times) that maybe they were just having a bad day. One time I walked in at lunch time, and they weren't that busy. Plus, it was the buffet, so everyone was getting their food themselves anyway! They maybe had 4-5 tables with people at them. It was relatively quiet, and slow. The sign "wait to be seated" was at the front, so I waited. And waited. I probably waited at least 10 minutes before they even acknowledged that I had stepped into the building. And they DID see me, they just chose not to greet me, or acknowledge me. When I finally was seated, the server was very rude, and barely spoke. He brought the whole pitcher of water to my table, so as not to have to refill my glass himself. He never came to check on me during my meal, he came only once to take my plate, and even then he didn't speak, even when I said "thank you." When he dropped off the check, again, no "thank you", nothing. Only silence. I went to pay my check and received the same cold, rude service at the front desk. The next couple of times we went back, we had friends from out of town. We are all avid lovers of Indian food. On any of these times, we never had more than 4 people in our party, so it's not like we had an insane amount of people for them to wait on. Also, myself and my friends are not people that are hard to wait on anyway. Once we went for buffet, and the other time for dinner. Both times were NOT close to closing time. Our server once again was not polite, and they acted like they were doing us a big favor by waiting on us. Anytime we asked them for anything, they acted like it was a big deal. Then, they dropped off the ticket WAY early, like we hadn't even been there 30 minutes, and they kept coming over and asking us if we wanted anything off of the buffet...that they were closing it in 10 minutes. We politely said no thank you, and that we wouldn't be making any more trips to the buffet. A few minutes later, they said again that they were closing the buffet in 5 minutes. Again, we said no thank you. By this time, we felt REALLY rushed, and they weren't being polite at all. Not even 2 minutes later, they came over and said "do you want anything else, we're closing the buffet in 2 minutes." That's a bit much in my opinion. We were fed up at that point, and paid our check and left. Again, they never thanked us or anything. My most recent bad experience happened tonight. I've started noticing their ad in the newspapers around town advertising that they now deliver around the area. So...I thought I could get the food without the bad service. I called, ordered a substantial amount of food, gave them my number, name, address, and even gave them very clear directions to my house when they asked. I looked up a google map, and they are exactly 2 miles away. They said okay, and that it would be 30-45 minutes. I said thank you and okay. 10 minutes later they call...I thought maybe they were needing to ask something about the order...instead, to my shock, the man on the phone said "I'm sorry, we can't deliver there. You can come pick it up, but we're not coming there." I was quiet and surprised for a moment, and said "okay...was there a problem with the directions I gave you?" he said "No, the driver doesn't want to go there." I said "okay...is it out of your delivering radius? do you only deliver within a certain radius of your business?" and he said "Yes, if you were in West End or Green Hills..." and I said "Well, my house is only 2 miles from your location, I checked. Green Hills is just as far if not farther." He said "Well, the driver just doesn't want to go to that area." I replied "I really don't understand, it's not a bad area..." He said "No, it's not a bad area, the driver just doesn't want to go." And I said "Okay, well, I'm sorry that you're going to lose my business over this." And I hung up. That is seriously the last straw for me. I have tried, and tried, and TRIED to be kind, and overlook their past rudeness, but this is just too much. I honestly don't know how they stay in business. Unless they get new owners or management, I'm never stepping foot in there again. I've worked many serving jobs, and I know how hard it is and how you depend on your tips. So I'm a good tipper AND an easy customer. But it seems no matter how nice I am to the staff at Cuisine of India, they always treat me and my guests with either silence, or rudeness. That is unacceptable. There is no reason to be rude, especially to good customers. And now they're advertising that they deliver, but their driver just decides he doesn't want to go to a specific area for no reason? and they're okay with that? wow. If you want delivery,be prepared to be called back and turned down depending on the driver's mood.
label: NEG

text: If I had paid the price Kayak found, I think I might have agreed more w/ the people who hated on this hotel. But my boyfriend and I got it for $94/night through Priceline. We were expecting the worst after reading the reviews and were pleasantly surprised that the hotel is totally fine. Yes, the rooms are small and the bathroom is a tight fit. But if you're not obese and you're not intending to spend the whole trip in the hotel, it's more than adequate. Our room and bathroom were very clean. The pool/patio area was cute. The area and hotel are quiet, and the bed was not uncomfortable. The included breakfast is small, but the pastries are really good and the coffee was always refilled. The other stuff we ordered off the menu was great too. (Get the breakfast burrito!) It takes like 7 mins to get to downtown SB w/o too much traffic and there is a bus right at the corner that will get you there in 15. We took that so there was no worries about drinking and driving. Montecito itself is adorable, and there is a fantastic wine shop down the street that is worth visiting. The owner is not only incredibly friendly, but also incredibly knowledgeable. If you pay $170 or more, you will probably be disappointed like a lot of reviewers. But if you get a better deal, this is a great place to crash after a day of hiking and strolling around State St. Update: Check your bill after you check out. I had a random $6 charged to my credit card. Annoying.

text: I have never had such a negative experience with a reputable hotel. My friends and I were going to be driving through Reno and decided that we wanted to spend the night. My friend's called at 7:50 PM and reserved a standard room in the Peppermill Tower for $89.99. I called at 8PM and spoke to a woman at the reservation desk about the different options. She said that a standard room with two beds was $89.99 and a suite in the Tuscany Towers with two king beds, a european jet tub and shower was $129.99. Since there were four of us we decided to splurge and book the Tuscany Suite. We knew that we were six hours away so I double checked with her that it was okay that we were going to check in at around 3AM. She said that she would put a note on the reservation. Upon our arrival we were met at the front desk by Ed. He seemed pleasant enough when he was checking our friends into their room. They were told that all the standard rooms had been overbooked so they were upgraded to a suite in the Tuscany Tower for the same price of $89.99. I was a little bummed at that point that we were going to pay full price, but was happy that we were all going to be in the same area of the hotel. When my boyfriend and I checked in we were told that we would be in the Peppermill Tower and the price was $129.99. Wait a second, what? We reserved a suite in the Tuscany tower. Ed told us, "No, you reserved a room in the PepperMill Tower." I asked, "Well, is it at least a suite?" Ed: "No, it's a standard room" I informed him that this made no sense. We definitely reserved a room in the Tuscany Tower and why else would it cost so much considering that a standard room is only $89.99. At this point Ed became quite belligerent and rude. Raising his voice while telling us that there were no other options. The hotel was sold out, the computer system was down for maintenance and there was no manager that we could speak to until 8AM. I could not believe the way that we were treated. When I pointed out that I was extremely unsatisfied with his service and didn't appreciate being yelled at he yelled, "I'm not yelling!" After a few more minutes of being verbally abused by Ed, we walked away from the desk and decided to try to call the main hotel line and see if there was another manager we could talk to. The front desk kept transferring us back to Ed and when we told them that we wanted to talk to a different manager they said that he was the only manager on duty for the entire hotel/ casino. You have got to be kidding me. And how does the person who is working the front desk not know how much their rooms cost? He was completely unwilling to work with us and we ended up canceling our reservation and going to stay at the Silver Legacy which was only $49.99 for a standard room. The only reason why this isn't a one star review is because I called the next day and spoke to Judy who was very friendly and sympathetic. She apologized for our negative experience and offered to send us a voucher for a suite in the Tuscany Tower for $79.99. I think that my boyfriend and I will give the hotel another chance since they are giving us a voucher but I hope that we never come across Ed again.
label: NEG

text: Had dinner here last night with some colleagues. First off, this place is an old school Italian neighborhood restaurant where the owner, Mel, is always hanging around and everyone knows him. We grabbed a bunch and headed over. The minute we sat down and made it known we had a bunch of pens all the waiters started hovering and checking them out - Mel came over too. We handed him a bunch of stuff, pens, ice scrapers, SD Card reader...he was psyched. He disappears and comes back with two really high quality white baseball caps for us. What a nice guy. He wound up giving me a second cap for a friend of mine. So, on to the food...very well made Cosmo - not too much cranberry and nice big wedge of lime. Phenomenal stuffed veal chop the size of my forearm. It was pan seared and then roasted, stuffed with prosciutto, spinach and great mozzerella. Then it was covered with a delicious mushroom wine sauce. Out of this world and tender as could be. A nice side of homemade rigatoni with marinara and bada boom bada bing...fahgeddaboutit. I think perhaps the best thing is that I didn't have to pay for this meal, but I would've happily parted with the dough after a meal like this. The atmosphere was between fine-dining and pub - not too casual, not too fancy. I felt very comfortable in jeans, but others were suited up. They have valet service, a bar and it seemed like they were very busy last night. If you're in Philly, check out Mel's

Heard this place used to be cheaper but luckily the prices weren't out of this world. You get a good bang for your buck for certain menu items, especially the shots we had. While some of the items tasted OK, their appearance was less than appetizing. This is especially true for the salad bar portion which seemed to have needed more attention. The pizza was about average, with good quality cheese, but otherwise nothing special. The greek chicken, if that's what it was, was tasty but the big uneven hunks of onion and scummy sauce looked less than appealing. In short, if you're in the area and hungry, and want a cheap lunch, this would do. However I wouldn't go too far out of my way for it.
label: NEG

text: I went there to get an oil change and a tire rotation. It took an hour, which was fine. But after I paid and went out to my car, I inspected my tires and good thing I did because one of my front tires only had 12 pounds of air in it. I went back inside and complained, and they gave me some excuse that the guy was new. Yeah, sure he was. They are pathetically unprofessional if they let me leave with only 12 pounds of air in a tire that they supposedly rotated. I could have easily been on the highway and shredded that tire and had an accident. I will never go back again.

text: Had breakfast. Prompt greeting, cordial server tho not too experienced (pancakes arrived first, had to wait a moment for syrup, no refill on coffee until after pancakes eaten). A "territorial cook" confronted me as I was returning to table - What are you doing - (using restroom, returning to table), Don't you see that sign... I promised never to visit the facility again and was allowed to return to me table. The restroom I used was the only one visible at the hostess desk and that was what I saw first.. McDonald's has better coffee, pancakes are about the same and the staff is much friendlier and the restrooms are clearly marked - go there instead of Parrot Pete's.

text: Was there for Sun. breakfast with my two grown sons and daughter-in-law. The service was terrible!!!!! Had to ask for everything... Asked if we could order, asked for water, asked for coffee. I do not recommend this place.

text: This place is no joke. The food here is astounding. The shrimp and grits entree is a beautiful plate of food. The bartenders are knowledgeable and fast, and the servers are impeccable. I haven't had service like that ever in my life, really amazing. This place is cute, with memorable food and incredible attention to detail. Not to be missed.

text: Poor Krista got treated wrong. I loved it! It's a breakfast/brunch heaven full of seafood, cajun and creole variations on everything you've ever conceived as a breakfast food. Try the made to order seafood omelettes early or you'll run out of room. Be careful, they bring OJ and champagne for mimosas and a big basket of some of the best biscuits around -- this is to trick you into forgetting to actually make it to the buffet. They had no such luck with me and my crew. We ate for an hour and a half and spent the rest of the day moaning with pleasure.

text: While looks at first may appear deceiving, this hidden jewel of South Asia brings back amazing memories of summers spent in India. The food at Desi Chaat House rekindles fond memories of walking down a crowded street in Bombay looking for that special afternoon snack to share with friends and family. My culinary experiences, though limited by funds as a student at Penn, have never embarked on a greater journey. By combining the freshest of ingredients with wholesome hospitality, the hosts at desi chaat house manage to provide you with old world charm at very affordable prices. I see this restaurant taking off and would highly encourage the university city community to enjoy the delectable offerings this well kept secret (hopefully no more) has to offer!
label: POS

text: Tried the coffee here about 7-8 times (once it was an iced coffee). The first time, the coffee was honestly amazing. Fresh, had a good flavor, etc. However, the second time I came back, it was horrible!! Sour tasting (which I found out later happens when the coffee has been sitting for two long). It was actually so bad that I couldn't drink it and just had to throw it out. Kept going back and kept getting sour cups of crap (inadvertent reference to the Austin Powers movie). Finally, I decided that I had wasted more than enough money here chasing after the elusive perfect cup of coffee. I probably would have given it two or three stars if it had been a hit-or-miss experience. But my experience was basically all misses.

text: We ate here once when visiting from out of town and were both impressed. I had Honey & Walnut Shrimp from the Authentic Chinese Menu, which was very rich, sweet and tasty. My friend had Chicken with Broccoli from the Americanized Menu; he remarked that usually this is just a basic meal that he mildly enjoys, but he really loved Han's. I'm hoping to eat here again. Because they've got such a wide variety of interesting selections, and what we've eaten so far was good, I'm thinking of taking something to go for my wife tomorrow.

text: Ordered Fried Dumplings, Crispy Beef, and Ham Fried Rice. The dough on the dumplings was by far the thickest and gummiest I've ever had and filler was sub-par. Crispy beef was a gelatinous block by the time we got it home (maybe 5 minutes later) and the fried rice was below standard too. Took a chance on a shopping mall chinese and it was a bad call. I'll drive to South Grand from now on to get my fix. I'll agree that the portions were generous, too bad they weren't delicious.

While the atmosphere is relaxing, it's one of those places designed to make those who can afford it feel all worldly and generous about spending money. Eh, I wasn't so impressed.

text: Freebirds is totally fake Mexican food, but it's SO GOOD. The nachos are great, share them with a friend unless you're drunk and it's 1am because it's definitely too much for a sober person to finish on their own. The secret menus are pretty great--ask for a tostada! It's basically the same as nachos, but just on one crispy tortilla, with as many toppings, enough food for one person, and half the price of the nachos. Most of the staff are very friendly and service is usually quick, as long as you don't get stuck in the line (and late at night, there is a LONG line)

text: I needed a sympathy card and was so happy to find a place near by (on Yelp of course) that could accommodate me without the stress of parking and driving all over Nashville in the rain. I never noticed the store even though I passed it all the time. I enjoy supporting neighborhood businesses so it all worked out. I will keep this place in mind for any future gifts or cards.
