text: Good Indian Buffet for lunch. Less than 10.00 and it comes with dessert! what more could you ask for. The Nan was so yummy
label: POS

text: So I'm on travel in Nashville, and I was desperate for some decent coffee. The Starbucks in the hotel is a no go zone for me, and the in room coffee is atrocious. I had found a little boulangerie down the street with intelligentsia coffe, which is passable but closed on Sunday. A little research led me to a shop called Dunn Bros Coffee. It's very convenient to the downtown hotels, which is fantastic. Apparantly it's a chain with about 100 stores, mostly in Minnesota, but I wouldn't have known it. All their stores do daily roasting on premesis, and also do cold brewed coffee, which can be had in growlers, if they aren't sold out, which they were when I arrived. The coffee is actually quite good. I got a french pressed Vienna Roasted Sumatra, nicely dark and bold with tons of subtle flavor and no bitterness at all. It's a pretty neat place, very local feeling even though it's a chain. I hesitated between 4 and 5 stars because it's a chain, and I don't like giving chains 5 stars on principle; if i could I'd go 4.5. But the local roasting, local flavor, and proprietor Kevin's incredibly friendly nature, and earns the higher vote.
label: POS

text: Wonderful Sunday brunch spot, with a bright and open seating area. Interesting crowd that mixes East Nashville's hippest with Green Hill's Ladies who lunch. I started my meal with a cucumber-sake bloody Mary. It was outstanding, and the use of sake in place of vodka really helped the cucumber and lime shine through - making it very refreshing. The menu is pretty straightforward, with lots of interesting small plate options and larger entrees ranging from $3 - $9. I had the smoked salmon with capers, red onion and mascarpone cheese on rye. The use of mascarpone was another interesting take on this classic. I had zero complaints about my meal and cannot wait to go back for more.
label: POS

text: So this is a BYO Italian ristorante. We got there in the evening but it was hard to locate it since the entrance is tiny and the lighting is very poor! Parking is not easy either. The place is rather small, but very friendly. The service is great too. However, the food is metzo metzo! It's a great place if you go with a group of over 6 since they line up the tables very fast to accommodate your numbers. We were the only young group in this place, most of their clients are older and family type of clients--as if they have been going here from generation to generation! So I guess for some Italians it is like home cooking, but frankly I thought I make better Italian pasta. We all had variation of pasta meals and we all thought it was average. The bread was very good though. The place was also a little cold!
label: NEG

text: Here is a copy of a letter I sent to the owner of Sweat; he has not had the courtesy to reply. The promotion is dihonest and proves that the company is not trustworthy. Avoid. Dear Mr. Scott Caplan, A few days ago, I received in the mail one of your "Scratch & Win" flyers. I have been thinking of rejoining a gym in the area where I live (not far from your center on Arch St. and 15th St., which would be quite convenient). I therefore decided to see whether I had "won" anything. Yes, I was a "Grand Prize Winner!" which, according to the flyer, entitled me to "6 months free, Free personal training, or 10 VIP passes, or all three." To be certain that this "win" was legitimate, I called your company and left a message. One of your associates (I forget her name) returned my call, and she informed me that as a Grand Prize Winner I was entitled to the items listed on the mailing. I asked if there were any conditions, truly believing that I might indeed be a rare "Grand Prize Winner," and she said "only a joining fee of $149." Today, I took time to visit your gym at Arch and 15th Streets and was informed that there were further conditions not mentioned on the mailing, namely that I would have to take out a 12- or 18-month contract at $65 or $59 per month, respectively. Neither of these conditions nor, indeed, the joining fee, were printed on your flyer. I believe your mailing should have listed all these conditions, even in small print, on the mailing. I would imagine that it might be illegal not to do so. If not, it certainly should be! I think your mailing is dishonest and certainly is unethical -- and has wasted my time, as well. Obviously, you have lost a legitimate customer, and I suspect other "Prize Winners" -- and friends of mine who are already members of your gym at other locations -- will be as angry, or at least as disappointed, as I am when they find out the true value of the "prizes" you have offered. Sincerely,
label: NEG

text: Not at all what I expected when I got the gc from restaurant.com. but the service was good; food even better and like everyone said, a very clean bathroom. text: Maybe it was the day I went but unless you tell me that Chef Morimoto is actually going to be the chef that night, I will not want to go back! We went mainly for the publicity that it experienced. We decided to go with the Omikase and I can't remember what was being served anymore. I have to admit however, the presentation was impressive, but not to merit paying $150 a person for it. I could care less if it was served on a paper plate if the food was good. I gave it an extra star for the appeal and presentation. That's at most I can give it, since I had hoped to brag about it. Very disappointed. I did however enjoy the dessert, but the oysters were warm and felt as tho it was left out way too long - and I'm a Oyster connoisseur! Hopefully there's a way to catch whether Chef Morimoto would be there, because then I can give a better review. But as for now, this is the best I can give it.

text: A tiny, hidden gem in the RTM, with a large selection of fruits, vegetables, and wheatgrass. Reasonably priced--get the medium-size, or large if you are very thirsty. My carrot/apple/parsley cocktail was deliciously blended with the pefect amount of parsley, which provided an earthy zing, but did not overwhelm the sweetness of the apple, and just a bit of crushed ice to make it extra-refreshing without diluting the juice. I don't know how anyone could drink soda after getting a taste of fresh-squeezed fruit and vegetable juice. It's really a treat, even if it is healthy (shh).
label: POS

text: Bistro Romano delivers quality northern Italian food in the cozy ambiance of of a dining room located in an underground granary. The exposed stone walls and dim candlelight combine for a romantic feel; unfortunately, the fake ivy and hard, wooden booths cause it to fall short of perfection. I have always experienced pleasant and polite service from every staff member - hostess, wait staff, manager, bartender . . . I have had many of their dishes - pastas, meats and seafood - and they have all been very good to excellent. My only complaint is that they sometimes oversalt. They have a diverse wine list that seems to have a focus on reasonably priced selections, with a few higher end selections of each varietal. Their mark-up is pretty standard. As an added bonus, they have some great specials on various nights that can make it a real bargain - like $12.95 pasta Mondays and lobster Tuesdays. As a side note about the other reviewers who have questioned the freshness of their seafood, WHY on earth would you not point this out to your server if you suspected it to be the case? This is a classy restaurant; the chef and manager would want to know (if it were truly the case), and make things right for you and the others diners.

text: I am torn as a newly devoted yogi I do not wish to put out bad energy but feel honesty is the best practice. Speaking of practice...I found the class at this studio to be the most unlike yoga experience I have ever had. Simply, I will list the reasons why... 1. Instructor came rushing into the room shouting at everyone to move over as they can fit 7 across..this leaves you approximately less than 4 inches from your neighbors mat and delayed the class. I truly felt also it showed a lack of class and money hungryness! (new word) 2. Poor ventilation system...they are supposed to heat the room to 90 degrees but once they pack you in there like sardines the thermostat does not work or control the temp. This can lead people trying to take poses too far...and injuries. The sweat on the floor was not from exertion, but the heat alone. 3. The instructor was unlike any yoga instructor I have crossed...she shouted because she had her alternative rock music so loud (sometimes she sang along during class). 4. This was supposed to be slow flow...I thought I would be bored...she took us through postures linked to breath so fast people were hyperventilating and not breathing Ujjayi breath at all. This will also cause injuries as the students were not allowed time to hit the pose. I could go on, but I do not wish to. I did not leave this place feeling energized, renewed, and worn out at the same time-I left it unsettled, tense, and lacking a workout. For a serious yogi that has taken some amazing classes with well lead instruction find another place in Indy to go. This place should not have yoga in their name

text: The building is awesome, really great chandelier, photos, floors, everything! The food is great too, I had the nicoise salad, which was great. You would expect a city out in AZ to have less than impressive veggies, but it was all fresh and delicious. Usually I despise Tucson, and Arizona as a whole, but this place gives the city one redeeming value.

text: As a crazy man once yelled on the 42 as he stumbled off the bus (after lecturing me on social security and repeatedly singing Hey Mickey): "FUCK SEPTA!" Slow, inefficient, and almost always late. Tokens are also annoying to get: cash only and some machines give you about 80 nickels in change. However, it's pretty much the only option you have unless you want to shell out $10-20 for a cab and deal with asshole cab drivers who flip a shit about taking credit cards. Too bad parking in center city is a bitch too. On the plus side, there is always free entertainment from the random crazies you meet. They should have the PPA run SEPTA, they're always right on time to write up parking tickets or tow your car.

text: Germantown Cafe is strategically located between work and downtown - which makes it a convenient location for lunch (and after work drinks). It also seems to be a pretty social spot - where a lot of government types take lunch meetings. Yesterday I ordered the salmon club sandwich - and it was super good. Nice thick cuts of bacon and tomato, sandwiched between two hearty pieces of whet bread. And perfect fries! Oh, I was loving it. My lunch buddies ordered the Asian Chicken Salad and the Germantown Cafe Burger. Both looked picture perfect and didn't last very long. I hear they grind their own meat for the burgers and sausages. So, big pluses for freshness. Yay, I'm a fan!

text: So on a whim, 14 of us rolled up to the biggest little city. More of a forced kidnapping, but we went anyway. After drinking in our awesomely amazing hotel room at the amazing Sands, it was definitely time to hit up a clizzub. After wandering the streets, this seemed like the place to go, and the place to get our groove on. I felt pretty, or like a cheap piece of meat, depending on how you look at it. With my boyfriend down the street gambling, I was a target. I got hit on by countless skeezy guys, but of course ignored them to dance with my friends. My friend got hit on as well, and every guy she danced with got arrested outside. Thats pretty amazing. The music was hot, playing all the hits to get low low low low low low low to. And, in the company of good friends, a lot of booze, smoking inside and the city of lights, this place did the trick.

text: Every time I walk into Mike's I feel like I am in that movie Pleasantville where everything turns black and white and is fantastically 50s. The ice cream, true to the setting, is great and though I'm not a big ice cream float person (now that I'm all grown up) it's the only place I have had one in the last decade. Something about the place just makes you want to see an ice cream scoop float in some soda. If you can grab a window seat, do it, because there is no better place to people watch!
label: POS

text: Don't do it. This is still the Striped Bass. Just painted. The six of us had dinner before the Symphony. We are seniors who have eaten in most top restaurants around the world. This steakhouse is of the level of a college beer and steak place. Drinks: Nice but no attempt to be special. First course: Clams very nice but smaller than Howard Johnsons used to be, but at least each one cost what a bus trip to the shore would. Staek tartare was pretty excellent BUT it was premade earlier in the day, served with 3 toast points and nothing else on the plate. Salads were like fast food salads. Rolls were excellent, but no one ever offered a second. Main course: Steak ordered med rare and came raw. Seared tuna sushi is cooked more. Veal chop, lamp chops were below average. No grill marks. A fish dish was good. I had fried shrimp. Obviously frozen with high school breading. All six were identical looking. Served with one small lemon slice (I got more) and a metal shot glass of Heintz' cocktal sauce. It was not of the quality of most roadside stands on the coast. Sides: Onion rings were pretty excellent with a spicy dipping sauce. The creamed spinich was as another reviewer stated excellent Denny's level and salty. Hashbrowns would have been as good as others have said, but were under cooked. Cole slaw looked great, I personnally did not like the seasoning. Asaragus very nice. Desserts: nice for a Diner. Large pieces. Did not look or taste home made but were decent. I did not taste the orange sherbet, but it was the only ice cream choice and was left over. Wait Staff: Our waiter was upbeat, very well informed and nice. However, thoughout the meal individual plates that were empty were removed from the table. There was constantly a hand reaching past me to pick something up. I do not like that. Coffee: Excellent Finally: There is no real well known top restaurant one of us hasn't eaten at pretty much anywhere in the world and this was the third largest tab we have ever seen. There was 90% profit. I you want to impress someone and go here so they can see you are willing to spend many hundreds of dollars at the old Striped Bass, once they taste the food they will think you are pretentious and unknowledgable.
label: NEG

text: Wow. That's all I have to say. From the moment our huge group pulled up to the front of Oystercatchers, I was impressed. The stunning waterfront location, the calming feel of the restaurant, the attentiveness of the staff. Just really impressive! And that's even before we started eating! We were a group of 17 people so we had our own private room and two of the best servers! As we looked at the menu, they suggested we order their appetizer sampler so we got 4 of them for the table. It came with delicious crabcakes, oysters Rockefeller, jumbo shrimp and their calamari. All were amazing! For my main entree, I had their organic cashew crusted snapper. It was cooked to perfection and came on a bed of roasted hearts of palm and little grape tomatoes. Everyone seemed very happy with their meals, which with a table of 17 is pretty rare! It was a little on the pricey side, but for the view, the service & the food, it was definitely well worth it!
label: POS

text: 2Schae is pretty much the only café I can walk to from my apartment, so I'm glad I love it so much! I can always count on this place for a great Sunday breakfast and coffee. The owners, Lisa and Don, are two of the nicest people I've ever met. They're super welcoming and you can tell they're very proud of their cozy little coffee house. Lisa cooks everything fresh to order and does it really, really well... she will cook your food however you want it! I usually stick with the standard eggs, bacon and toast, but my boyfriend loves their French toast. I snuck a bite of his yesterday! The prices ARE a little high for a café, but it doesn't bother me much... I love supporting such a hard-working local business. Between the two of us, assuming we order breakfast and coffee, we usually spend around $25. They encourage people to stick around and work on their computers which is important to me since sometimes I'll need to sit somewhere for hours. I love the window seats with tons of pillows... there's also another side to the restaurant with couches and a great selection of books. I'm a fan already, and I'm sure I'll be spending a lot of snowy days this winter at 2Schae Café.
label: POS

text: Service is spotty, the margaritas have too much sour mix, and the menu has a shitload of typos. They do have a nice, large outdoor patio. I enjoyed feeding my stale chips to the squirrels and birdies last night.

Don't get me wrong- really nice and relaxing atmosphere but would have expected a much larger selection of wines at a place called the wine loft. The food was tasty, the service nice and the atmosphere pleasant. It screams romantic date night rather than en evening with a friend

text: After reading about this restaurant as one of the "Best Seafood" restaurants in the country, I had to try it out when I was visiting. I was not very impressed, the food was sub-par and overpriced. The oysters were small, and the steak and lobster were not worth the $70ish price tag. Save your time and money, you are likely to find a better place to eat right off of State St.
label: NEG

text: There are really only two reasons to go to Jim's: 1). You want to drink a beer with your steak, because they sell them. 2). You think you're being in-the-know by not going to Pat's or Geno's. Jim's is a disappointment. They do not care about the quality and taste of their steaks. They only seem to care about the tourist dollars. From the moment you get there until you receive your order, it's line-up, queue-up, factory line style. No thanks! All that aside, the steaks themselves are actually small in size but not in price. Plus, you often have to cross the street due to the line up outside. The best thing I can say about Jim's is that it smells good as you walk by. Don't be fooled, however.

text: The food is pretty good but, it's really the great views here that draw. The restaurant isn't visible from the street but walkin back it turns into this huge restaurant by the water. Good beer selection and the food was good. The wait is a little long but seems to move by quickly. A nice alternative is sitting at the bar and ordering snacks with your drinks. The best thing I had there was the lobster and shrimp spring rolls.

text: My boyfriend calls this, "the place where you can park wherever you want". Yes, their parking lot has no lines and is a little "free-for-all". Yes, there are cheesy 80's posters of a panther walking in front of the NYC skyline. And yes, their food is well worth the sketchiness! I normally get the bbq pork bun with eggroll and go crazy with all the hot chili oils and spicy condiments they provide. Their bun is much better than Miss Saigon's across the parking lot. They also have good pho, and I like that you can order it in a small since the bowls are so huge. I think that I like the broth at Miss Saigon better, but the meat quality/quantity better at KG. They also have a great egg/shrimp/pork pancake appetizer that my bf loves and delicious cold rice-paper spring rolls. I always end with a Vietnamese iced coffee which are to die for. I don't drink coffee and I will never leave this place without one because they are so perfect; not too sweet, not too bitter (ala Starbucks), just smooth french coffee heaven! FYI they only accept cash, but for two people you won't spend much more than $20.
label: POS

text: I love Canine Culture. They carry Barkology and Life is Good. They carry dog food, toys, costumes, etc. They offer pet grooming and sponsor SPCA adoption days. All and all they are just good people with a fun store.

text: When it first opened, the food and service was at it's top in Tampa. The line(s) would wrapped around the restaurant outside, and wait time was 1-2 +hrs! However, the food and service has drastically gone down upon my return after a few years. I thought the change was due to a different owner but nope, still the same. It is one of the few (possibly only one) Dim Sum restaurants that offer the cart-pushing service. The decoration is quite nice, modern, elegant; an infusion of American-Chinese cultures. Waiters are okay, although sometimes it does take them a very long time to get to you and sometimes you may have no one or 1 or more servers?! The carts makes it way around the entire restaurant, offering many dishes. The taste in the dim sums were quite bland and dry. It was lacking the kick of authenticity, or even any flavor! Pricing was expensive for what it was worth. Soft drinks and tea are overpriced as well. A big disappointed because the interior decoration and table setting was so nice yet the food couldn't make up to it.

text: Menu is decent. The beer is what I'd like to call 'meh', which, while being a really great Scrabble word for a game with less than 30 tiles left and the board, as such, having little space, is not the best when describing a brew. But even with decent menu and meh beer I would have still probably offered a slightly higher rating. text: I just experienced an annoying series of events with Allegro's Pizza. Sunday night (5/31/2009) we placed a delivery order, which we do about once a week. One of the items we ordered was chicken fingers. When they arrived, my partner opened up the chicken container and recoiled at the smell. I sniffed them, and they smelled rancid, like fish gone bad. I immediately called them and asked to speak with a manager. I was told that there was no manager on site. I told the person on the phone about the rancid chicken fingers. They offered to bring out another order, but since our concern was that the oil they were using had gone bad, I told them I wasn't OK with that choice and requested a refund. I was told that since I had paid by credit card, the only person who could do the refund was the manager. Then I was told that my other option was that they could put a note on my accounting saying we were owed a free order of chicken fingers, but I didn't feel comfortable with that option, so they took my number and said they would have the manager call me back. At that point we put the styrofoam container with the stinky chicken fingers in a ziploc bag in the refrigerator (as "evidence.") After a couple of hours no one had called, so I called to find out what was going on. I was told that a manager wouldn't be in until Monday at 11:00 a.m. Around 3:00 p.m. on Monday I called and asked to speak with a manager. I was then told that the manager wasn't in until Tuesday. I explained the problem to the person on the phone, and he asked me to hold on. Then the line was disconnected. I called back and asked if he had just hung up on me, and he said "No, I thought you said it was OK." I said "No, I thought you asked me to hold." He said "OK hold on," then in the background I heard him say "Matty, could you take this?" and he put me on hold for 10 minutes, at which point the line was disconnected again. I called back, and the line was picked up then hung up immediately (they have caller ID). I then called back on my cell phone and asked to speak with Matty. This was the guy I had spoken to the night before. I explained the situation, and he said "I offered to send someone out with your refund last night but you refused." I told him that that option had not, in fact, been offered to me, and that I actually would be happy with that plan. He then said "But what about the chicken fingers?" I told him we had saved them and would be happy to give them back, which surprised him. He looked at my account and said belligerently, "I see you've ordered them in the past and never had a problem." I said, "Exactly my point! If you get food that smells like rotten fish, would you eat it?" He reluctantly agreed that no, he wouldn't. A few minutes later the delivery guy showed up with my refund in cash, and I handed him the chicken fingers. The delivery guy then said "They said they won't take your orders anymore." I shrugged and said "Fine with me." I mean, we're moving in a month, so who cares, right? But still... WTF? We've been regular customers of theirs for YEARS, and the one time we have a problem, we're given the runaround and are told we can't order from them anymore? At no point did I yell or curse at them. While I didn't hide the fact that I was annoyed, I dealt with them in a professional manner. I'm disgusted with their behavior. It's a shame that they have the best (to my tastes) pizza & strombolis available for delivery in University City.
label: NEG

Mirna said that business was VERY slow, even on the weekends, and I fear this place will succumb to failure if we don't get the word out. They have been in charge for 2-3 weeks. text: What a freaking fantastic place! I haven't been to any other pool halls, so I don't have much by which to judge Pink Galleon, but when I think 'pool hall', this is exactly what comes to mind. Pink Galleon doesn't try to be anything it's not. It's a smoky, dingy, ghetto-fabulous dive with a few dart boards, arcade games, an old jukebox, and dozens of flamingo-pink pool tables. In other words, it's heaven. Okay, maybe not HEAVEN, but it's pretty awesome. In a concerted effort to not be a part of Black Friday, me, Andy, and a few other friends hit up the Galleon on the biggest shopping day of the year. We arrived around 1pm, and it was pretty empty, save for some other laid back folks in need of a relaxing time. We walked in and informed the friendly (and scantily-clad) bartender that we'd like to play a few games of pool. "Go ahead -- it's free," she said. Say whaaat? Okay, fine. Free pool for the win! We ordered some nachos. "Nachos are free too," she added. OMG, I'm definitely in love at this point. Turns out that Monday-Friday, pool is FREE from 11am - 7pm, and so are nachos (they have a cute little nacho bar with chips, cheese, and salsa for you to help yourself). I couldn't believe that more people weren't there taking advantage of it. Oh yeah...Black Friday. I forgot. We rocked out to some tunes on the jukebox (and I made the few people in there HATE me by blasting Britney Spears -- hey, it was just ONE song, okay?) and we played pool and ate chips to our hearts content. And we bought a few drinks and cheese sticks, too. Will I be here every weekend? No. I suck at pool, and I hate smelling like smoke. But next time I'm off during the week and I need something to do, I know where I'll be headed.

text: Beer and wine sales tax ripoff: The Red Robin chain has decent, but overpriced, burgers. Their "unlimited" steak fries come-on is a ruse. You get precious few fries with your burger, and when you order more, it takes forever for the next serving of fries to be delivered to your table. So long, in fact, that I found myself having finished my burger, and ready to pay and leave. However, the biggest ripoff of all is the way they charge for and tax their beer and wine. I ordered a 20 oz mug of beer, which my check priced at 5.99. However, there was an additional "SALES TAX" charge for the beer of $1.45, listed separately from the sales tax charge for the food. $1.45 is almost 25% of the $5.99 beer, which means that the beer is almost $7.50. I've never seen separate tax for alcohol at any other pub or restaurant here in Nashville (or anywhere else in the US for that matter). I've asked several bartenders at other places about this way of charging tax for alcohol, and all say they've never heard of it being done that way. The restaurant ought to be upfront about it and mention that the cost of the 20 oz beer is actually $7.49 ($7.50), not $5.99!!!!!! DRINKER BEWARE!!!!

text: I had been meaning to go to Cafe Nonna for awhile. It was the perfect opportunity to go when my family came in to town to celebrate my birthday and recent engagement. I called around 11 am Saturday morning and left a voice mail about reservation possibilities for 7 people that night. I know they were a small place but was hoping I would hear back from them since I left my name and number. Around 5:30 I was getting worried because I hadn't heard back at all. I called in and got a voice mail again and left another message. I frantically called up other area restaurants trying to find a place for my and my fiance's family to go to. No one would be able to fit us in until late in the evening. 20 minutes after I called Cafe Nonna a second time they returned my call. The guy asked me if I had called asking about reservations for 7 around 7. I said, "Yes, I called twice. Once at 11 this afternoon and again about 20 minutes ago." He responded unapologetically that they won't be able to fit us in until 8:30 or so. Frustrated I said, "No thanks." and hung up. I couldn't believe the terrible service. I understand they are small and it would be hard to fit us in, but the fact I had called and didn't receive a response until 7 hours later is unacceptable. That, doubled with the unapologetic tone is even worse! I would have been fine if they called before 3 and let me know that it wouldn't work, but they didn't. Is there not someone that checks on those before they open? A night ruined in which was suppose to be a celebration.Thanks a lot, Cafe Nonna.

text: I've been to Bistro 7 a handful of times. With each visit, my experience has been getting progressively worse. A larger group of us (8) met for dinner a few weeks ago. While initially the staff seemed accommodating, we ended up waiting for our table for 40 minutes when we were told it would be only a few minutes. I don't mind waiting, but I would rather the hostess and waitstaff be upfront at the outset. Our cocktail server persuaded two of my friends to share a half bottle of wine instead of ordering individual glasses. We all assumed she suggested this because it would be more economical (she offered no other reason). But my friends ended up spending double than what they would have if they had simply ordered individual glasses. The surprise when the bill came was an unpleasant one. After getting seated, service was adequate but generally quite slow. Our server was certainly friendly and knowledgeable, but she was scarce throughout the meal. The worst part of the night was the food. Most of it was pretty disgusting. One of my friends had the lamb special. The sauce had an overpowering vinegar flavor that practically ruined the dish. Another one of my friends had the salmon. According to her, it tasted and felt like it had just come from the sea. She could barely eat it. I had the fish special, which was generally underwhelming and bland. Based on this last experience, I will not be going back to Bistro 7.

text: I came in here about a year ago and then yesterday. Quite a lot has changed. First the pros: Student 10% discount (yay for me). Fireplace - probably cozy during the winter. They now have an extended breakfast and lunch menu, with clever names after Washington locations - I was super stoked about the Whidbey Island Rice Salad (my hometown!) Now their pastries are from the House of Bread, which is great. The cinnamon roll I had was delicious. They are advertising they support local growers/businesses and that is good too. Now the cons: I went in just to get a cappuccino and pastry on my way out to work. I thought I'd be in and out in a few minutes but that was not to be. They were pretty busy yesterday morning, but there is absolutely no reason it should take ten minutes (let alone the fifteen plus I waited) for a coffee drink and a pastry out of their case. They had one girl running the register and one girl making all of the sandwiches and coffee drinks. So one staff member had to run around like a chicken with their head cut off while the other one, when not taking orders, sort of wandered around behind the register and did nothing. I had to remind them to make my drink and give me my pastry after some time, and after others had been served that came in after me. The girl at the register said they were backed up, and I could see there were problems with other customers besides me. I should not have to wait for all the sandwich orders to get made before I get my coffee. When I did get my pastry, they put it in a large styrofoam box for sandwiches or something. Don't play the sustainable/local card and then hand me something that will never decompose. The brand of coffee they use tasted extremely burnt as well. The reason I go on ad nauseum about this is because I wanted to support a local business and try something new for my morning routine. It turned out to be just short of a disaster. The atmosphere in there was akin to a daycare. Lastly, I looked at their menu and felt that it was extremely over priced. $9 for a breakfast burrito? No thanks. If I want another one of those rolls, I will just go to the House of Bread. Recommended for moms who want a latte and have some time and money to waste.

text: I have been struggling with allergies for years. I finally got a recommendation from my Dr. to go to an allergist of my choice. I had to have an initial check up, pulmonary testing, skin testing, and a CT Scan...after I completed all tests I met with their allergy educator which gave me some very helpful tips. I struggle with severe allergies and I didn't realize how bad they were until I met with their team of physicians. I loved everyone I came in contact with...they all made you feel extremely comfortable and welcomed. They were able to change my allergy medicine based on their findings and within two days I felt like a normal person again...it changed my life for the better! text: After seeing this place mentioned on a Yelp list for their beef barley soup, I decided to stop in and try the place since it was close to my bank on the Hill. Michael was at the counter and navigated me through the menu as well as their frozen offerings. He couldn't have been nicer or more helpful! I decided to go with their 1/2 soup and 1/2 sandwich combo for 6 bucks. I got the salsiccia sandwich (split salsiccia with marinara and provolone) and their salsiccia chili. The chili alone is worth going out of your way to try. I thought it was a perfect blend of meat, red beans (not kidney beans), sauciness, and just enough spiciness; everything seemed well balanced and proportionate in both flavor and size of ingredients. A hearty champion indeed! The bread the sandwich came on was so freaging good; chewy and soft all at the same time, and you could actually taste the sesame flavor the seeds lended. The piece of split salsiccia was fresh, had plump texture, and authentic Italian seasoning (plenty of fennel seed!). Provolone cheese and a drizzle of marinara topped it off. The cheese was good, as was the marinara, but I would have liked to have a little more sauce on my sandwich (totally personal preference). I think the balance would have been just right for most people. Important to note, is that they have a list of 11 cheeses to choose from, as well as a whole host of "toppings" I could have added as well--a customizable meal! I got my order to go and everything was still warm by the time I got back to the office, which was very much appreciated on this chilly winter day. I ate the half sandwich and part of the chili and was too full to continue. Needless to say, I am REALLY excited about the leftover chili I'll be having for lunch tomorrow! They have a good sized menu of sandwiches, both cold and hot, as well as salads, pasta, and sides. They carry Coke and Fitz's beverages, as well as brew fresh iced tea. You can get Dad's oatmeal cookies and a few other treats, including frozen Snickers bars. This is probably not the place to go if you are watching carbs or calories. There are a few vegetarian options, but I didn't see anything vegan-friendly. They also have frozen pastas, speidini, pizzas, etc. and provide options for catering. I did happen to purchase a whole frozen brusilone they made in-house for only about $8.50. Stay tuned on how it turns it!

text: I didn't stay but I had a horrendous time with room service trying to buy a gift for someone that did. Family members were staying the night in the hotel and I wanted to have a bottle of wine waiting for them as a birthday present. I was connected with room service and placed an order for a $50 bottle of wine to be put into their room. When I spoke with them when they returned home, I found out they hadn't received the wine. I contacted the hotel and they were apologetic and said they would look into it. I just wanted to be sure I was reimbursed for it. They called me the next day and couldn't explain what happened. I assumed it was the end until I realized I had never been reimbursed. I called again. The manager pretty much called me a liar and needed to talk to the person staying at the hotel. Not only did my family member not get a gift but now they had to be interrogated by the hotel. After a total of about five phone calls, I was told I would be reimbursed. A week later, after I found out that I still hadn't been reimbursed, I contacted the general manager of the hotel. I spoke with an assistant who said she would look into it. I said I would like to be reimbursed and I would like the person who was to receive the gift to get a gift certificate to compensate for their errors and our trouble. She called me back. I would finally be reimbursed and I was being sent a gift certificate for the person who was to receive the wine for $38. That's right, $38. They took all of their fees from the original gift costs and were giving me the difference. Seriously, how tacky is that! This is supposed to be one of the finest hotels in the city and they decide giving a gift certificate of $38 to make up for their errors is appropriate. I will never have anything to do with this hotel again. I know it was a small amount of money but their behavior and the amount of time it took to get my money back, was ridiculous. And now I'm stuck with the $38 gift certificate because nobody I'm related to or friends with plan on ever going there again either. Hope it was worth the $12 the hotel saved.

text: I too was part of Foodie M's group of diners who got Pooned. In a city that has so many great choices of affordable ethnic food, it's rare that I'll shell out $50 for dinner, let alone Chinese food, but the menu sounded fantastic. I have never experienced such a disconnect between a printed menu and my actual taste buds as this. Since Foodie M did a pretty thorough job of describing the dismal decor, and the range of off beat (not in a good way) to just plain inedible dishes I'll try to keep my review brief (brief isn't my specialty though...). As we sat down at the table I noticed a kind of funk wafting up my nose which I soon realized was a take out box of a previous diner's leftovers (From that day? From last week? I'm not sure) they had wisely chosen not to take home with them, and had shoved in the shelf under the table. (The tables aren't actual dining tables, but are kitchen prep tables). This should have been the first sign. Actually it was the first sign. The meal progressed from dishes that were OK to dishes that were horrible. A few examples- Second Course Peking Duck with Jicama and Spring Onion with Steamed Lotus Leaf Bun Translation - A bite of duck in a bun that is chewy in the center, and so hard on the side you can hardly bite through it. Sixth Course Double Happiness Lobster with Lemon Pepper Linguini in Homemade Chili Tomato Mirin Essence Translation - Lobster claws that are impossible to get out of the shell so forget about actually eating any, on a bed of linguini with BBQ sauce. Tenth Course Dessert: Ice Cream Cheesecake and Fresh Fruit Sculpture with Green Tea Translation - A 1" square of frozen cheesecake with a grape on a toothpick OK, so I guess a grape on a toothpick may qualify as a sculpture to some, but in my imagination it would be something slightly more. So I realized that Joseph Poon the brand is really much more about the wacky persona than the food. Oh well. I just wish I knew that before I blew so much money.
label: NEG

text: Only 3 days old, the Station Taproom looks like it has the potential to stick around and possibly be the new better (see Firecreek) torch bearer for a Downingtown restaurant Rennaissance. While I only sampled their small dishes (pulled pork sliders, curry chicken wings and shrimp skewers - all delicious), their menu looks powerful tasty and varied: lamb and beef burgers, fish & chips, mussels, big salads. They source a lot of their ingredients (including meats) locally. And now what really brought me to the Station Taproom's door (and had me lurking on their Facebook page all winter) was the promised beer selection. Twelve beers on tap and only two of them from local neighbor Victory (Prima Pils, Donnybook Stout). The fact that Victory's flagship Hop Devil was only available in bottles seemed to me to be a tip of the cap to Victory. Other tap beers (from memory) were Great Lakes Edmund Fitzgerald, Bear Republic's Racer 5, Founder's Pale Ale, a couple of Stoudts, a Troegs and others. Not a major brewer in sight, not a poorly spelled light beer in reach. When one of my friends asked about filling a growler the bartender said, "Not yet, but we'll get there." Overall, they did a great job on rehabbing the building and the interior design. Only one TV and music barely audible above the din of customers and open kitchen. They might want to tweak the exhaust system as at times the room seemed to be a little overwhelmed by grill smoke. It certainly smelled good but I heard a few people comment that it was a bit much. I may come off sounding like a bit of a fanboy here but I've been waiting a long time for something like this to come closer to home. Welcome, Station Taproom, long may you run.

Not sure how you get people to eat warm German food in a Florida restaurant with the place being uncomfortably hot. We started our meal with a tomato soup that was fine. For entrées my friend had the beef gulasch with red cabbage and potato pancakes. I had the wurst platter also with red cabbage and potato pancakes. The potato pancakes left something to be desired. They tasted like something out of a frozen package, very dry. The wurst platter was just one bratwurst and one bauernwurst. Sorry, but I could do better going to my local Russian or German market and feed 4 people for what I paid for two wursts ($15). I believe that value = quality / price. While the food was acceptable, it wasn't worth the price of admission. Maybe if the prices where about 20% less I would have given Martina's a better review. Not sure I would return.

text: Yesterday afternoon I called my vet because my cat was obviously having some pain and symptoms of being sick. They told be that because he was going to the bathroom, it was not an emergency situation, and to make an appointment for tomorrow (today). This morning when we woke up, my boyfriend and I saw that our beloved cat was unable to move and looked like he was dying. We called this emergency service, and they let us know that it sounded like renal failure and would be 1500 to help him. 1500 dollars that they needed up front, and even if we brought him there and he was dying, without being paid up front they wouldn't be able to do anything for him. This was their words, not ours. Our vet doesn't open till 9, and at around 7:45, my cat Oliver died. Words can not express how sad I am, and how heartless this practice is. I'm angrier than I have been in a very long time. I understand that they want to limit the amount of unpaid bills they have, but to just let an animal die because we didn't have the full amount up front, makes no sense to me. Two years ago we used them because another cat of ours was rough housing and did something wonky to his leg. It was on new years eve, and they did fine work, though they never really found out what was wrong, just gave us some meds. We took him to our own vet to check up after. But now? I would never use them for anything again.

text: I am a wine lover, but by no means am I a wine snob. So I want to make it clear that I fully concede to more knowledgeable folks out there that maybe Chaddsford wine isn't that good (comparably); maybe it is overpriced; maybe the winery is just a tourist trap. Etc. However, any place that makes a Spiced Apple wine is pretty much going to get 5 stars from me. That's just how I roll. I had been wanting to visit this winery ever since we lived in Chicago, where we had two friends who loved the Spiced Apple wine so much they would order it by the case and hoard it away in their pantry. The fiance and I finally made a trip out today for the Harvest Festival. First of all, this is the stuff perfect Sundays are made of. A scenic drive, perfect weather, live music, etc. So I was already happy before we started the tasting. Second of all, the tasting seemed like a pretty good deal to me -- there were 10 varieties to try, compared to six at our next stop on the wine trail -- couple that with the fact that I got to finish everything the fiance didn't like, and I was pretty happy by the time we left. As others have said, we preferred their whites over their reds. And the sweet/seasonal wines were definitely the best of all. My favorites were, of course, the Spiced Apple (served warm. awesome!) and the Sunset Blush, another sweet wine; I also liked the 2006 Pinot Grigio. I didn't LOVE any of the reds but I liked the 2006 Merlot quite a bit -- it was spicy. The Niagara tasted exactly like grape juice, which reminded me of communion, so that was interesting. All in all, I had a fantastic time and I'll definitely be back. Plus, it's fun to buy local!

The gym (which I didn't use) also seems very bright and large, and not at all like the dim, dank, windowless gyms that I've seen at other hotels. Unfortch, I didn't see Michael Phelps in the pool. text: I am definitely a fan of this place. I went to this tiny little shack on 8/21/08 with my family. Even more points for not scaring them away with outrageous prices. Everything was reasonably priced, with oyster shooters being only $2.50 each. My bro tried one and loved it. If you look at the shooter, it looks like someone just tossed the ingredients for a pizza into a shot glass and stuck a raw oyster at the bottom. Hideously unappealing. I guess looks aren't everything, huh? You MUST try their steamed rock crabs. They charge by the pound ($6.50/lb), and they are fiiiiiiillled with delicious, juicy crab meat. Those babies were hard though, and we had to ask the waitress to take them back and smash them to pieces for us. The crabs came with marinara-horseradish sauce (soo good) and caramelly-butter (too buttery for me). Be sure to look out for their specials...I think for $24 you can get a 3LB crab, soup, and cole slaw. There were some specials on spider crabs too, but I didn't pay too much attention. One downside to this place is the wait...no, not for a seat, but for a waitress to come by. The service was really slow even though the place was nearly empty. We didn't even ask them to clean out the crabs for us so basically all they had to do was find us 3 crabs, toss them into the water, and serve them on a clean plate. One other thing, the crab shells were caked with sand. It put me off a little, but I will forgive them because the meal was pleasant. I originally was going to give SBSC 3.5 stars, but looking back on my experience I actually had a fun time sitting by the waters watching my parents suck the insides out of those cute chubby crabs. They were so round and cute that I almost had trouble eating mine. I wanted to keep it as a pet, even though it was obviously dead. 4 stars for you Santa Barbara Shellfish Company...4 stars!

text: Don't bother. The good: our attentive and well-informed waiter, who is clearly really into the place, creative cocktails and wine list, and the ambiance (especially the plants and simple table decorations). The bad: the food. You know. The main reason you go out to eat at a restaurant. The takeaway here is this: if you're interested in high quality, local ingredients, prepared in a creative and skillful way, you want to be eating...somewhere else. Maybe Pumpkin on South Street. They source locally and do a lot of organic stuff and are always very seasonal. Bonus that their chef actually knows what he's doing unlike, apparently, the guy behind the wheel at Farmicia on Tuesday. We came here for an early dinner and planned to go all out -- appetizers, salads, entrees, and dessert. By the end of our entree, we were so disappointed, we skipped dessert. Started with two appetizers: the fiddlehead ferns with green garlic and hazelnuts and the vietnamese crispy squid with sweet and hot tomato dipping sauce. The fiddlehead ferns would prove to be the highlight of the evening. They were tender crisp. bright green, sauteed and seasoned to perfection. The green garlic was the perfect sharp complement to their springy freshness. The vietnamese crispy squid on the other hand, would prove to be a harbinger of the doomed remainder of the meal. Is the fryer too warm or is the kitchen just totally failing to let their fried stuff get a sufficient rest before sticking it on a plate and letting the grease accumulate in an unappetizing pool? Unknown. Either way, my date rightly proclaimed it to be a fiasco. The dipping sauce, while a little ketchupy, was reasonably pleasant but couldn't possibly redeem the soggy grease balls that it accompanied. The salads. Tuscan grains with chopped vegetables, lemon basil vinaigrette, arugula, and ricotta salata for me. French lentils with baked goat cheese, greens, and sherry dressing for him. If there was any dressing on either of our salads, it was woefully over oily and under acidic. Hello!? Vinaigrette! Meaning with vinegar! Let me say, I love salads. I eat a ton of vegetables and I typically enjoy a simple presentation that shows off the flavor of some high-quality produce. However, this does not mean that I want to go out into the garden, yank out some lettuce, dunk it in some oil and then stick it in my mouth. While I can appreciate a few bites of plain, adorned greens to get in the appreciation of their quality, ultimately I want said greens to have some kind of dressing Some fat, some acid, some salt, some herbs, some.. something. Seasoning of any kind seemed to have taken a vacation from both these dishes. The cheeses were the highlights and to say that they were used sparingly would be an understatement. The entrees: boneless honey-garlic grilled pork chop with maple mashed sweet potatoes and bacon braised cabbage for him. Duck breast with crisp skin, sun-dried cherry glaze, native grains pilaf and sauteed snap peas with scallions for me. At this point, I'm wondering if we somehow just managed to pick all of the stinkers on the menu. Fortunately, when we ordered, I asked our waiter to help me choose between the salmon and the duck. Without hesitation he steered me toward the duck, complimenting the cherry compote and suggesting medium rare on the temperature. We also accepted his recommendation on medium for the pork chop. Alas, the pork chop was decidedly NOT medium (try medium well at least) and the duck was also drifting toward the well side of the scale. Our waiter was correct on at least one front: the cherry compote definitely the highlight. The "native grains pilaf," which looked like a mixture of wild rice, hominy, pumpkin seeds, and maybe some other random stuff, seriously tasted like it might as well have been Uncle Ben's. The cabbage, while not completely inedible, was boring at best and offensive at worst. After taking a bite, my date immediately regretted having put it in his mouth. ... While it feels good to get this off my chest, mostly I'm just disappointed. I have heard such wonderful things about this place. Their menu looks great, they're associated with Metropolitan Bakery, which is one of my favorite places to get bread (and pizza and snacks and coffee...). The giant open windows, high ceiling and other aesthetic details are all so pleasing and perfect. I had really high hopes and I feel like they were just completely dashed. It's certainly possible that they were just having an off night or something, but we left feeling like we just wasted $100+, 2 hours, and how ever many calories. Usually I leave a good restaurant having cleaned everything of my plate in a totally unladylike fashion and feeling like someone needs to stick me in a wagon and wheel me home. Tonight we were so unsatisfied we were able to walk the 20+ blocks home in total comfort. Sad measure, but there it is.

text: l'america e il cibo, parliamone. un rapporto patologico. con qualche gemma. adoro i diner, ad esempio, e le loro colazioni a base di omelette ed hash browns, ma solo il finesettimana.. ed adoro i deli, che sono posti un po' simili ai nostri alimentari, dove fare la spesa, scegliendo tra prodotti generalmente di alta qualità, in mezzo a qualche tavolo dove puoi anche sederti e consumare sul posto.. che idea geniale time market è questo, e qualcosa in più. si può fare la spesa, c'è molta roba biologica, compreso il caffè (rigorosamente americano, consiglio di evitare l'espresso), si può fare colazione con un muffin o dei cookies al cioccolato, si può pranzare con una fetta di pizza (è buona, una via di mezzo tra quella napoletana e quella romana, per spessore e consistenza) o con uno dei molti sandwich, fantasiosi e mooolto ricchi, o con i cibi preparati sul posto, che ovviamente si possono anche portar via.. tutto (panini, insalate, pizza, etc) risente delle diverse influenze del posto, da quelle della costa est americana, a quelle messicane, a quelle -perchè no- mediterranee.. per cui si può trovare una pizza con jalapeno e un panino con la mortadella.. si può vivere di time market, insomma, sfruttando anche la connessione wifi gratuita per i clienti. il personale è delizioso, gentile (e spesso le cameriere sono molto carine.. eheh), c'è qualche tavolo all'aperto (ma non si può fumare, sono pur sempre americani.. ma vendono le sigarette), è aperto fino a tardi.. ah, dimenticavo l'ampia selezione di birre, dove comprare anche il tipico six-pack prima di andare a un party.. c'è un vino che si chiama "cheap wine" che rende mitologica una sezione di vini ancor più vasta di quella delle birre.. ci sono liquori, c'è tutto, che altro volete? probabilmente c'è già.
label: POS

text: This place is just fine. Nothing special but not bad either. Club sandwiches are really good, but the chips that come with it are the greasiest and are usually all smashed crumbs. I know a lot of people don't care for the pizza, but it's fine. They are really slow here, even for cold sandwiches I always like to call well in advance of when I will be picking up. The salads are really boring, but the chicken caesar comes with a mountain of chicken, and I like that they pre-butter the rolls with way more butter than I would ever allow myself to have otherwise.

text: We're still looking for a decent bowl of Asian noodles and we read the reviews so we thought we'd check it out. We were not impressed. First of all, this is about as far from authentic Japanese food as you can get - more of a 70's style vegetarian restaurant feel. A tiny bowl of noodles in an watery insipid broth with absolutely no flavor and almost no vegetables or protein. Cheap and still too expensive for what you get. Also, not terribly clean.
label: NEG

text: Yeah yeah let's all make fun of Whole Foods by calling it "Whole Paycheck . . .". Okay, finished? Now yes you can't expect Walmart supermarket prices from here, but let's face it - Walmart sucks for a variety of reasons (i.e. exploitation of their employees), but Walmart in New Orleans is downright SCARY. The employees don't get paid enough to care about their jobs and the other customers are sometimes very scary (I won't delve too deeply into personal accounts, but I was semi-stalked there once by a random fellow customer and I truly RAN into the restroom). Sure John Mackey, CEO of Walmart, is a verifiable nutjob, but there really isn't too much else in terms of vegan-friendly, organic, environmentallly conscious grocers in New Orleans (grrr!), so Whole Foods is my heavenly haven. The employees are mostly super duper helpful and friendly. Sometimes too friendly . . . but very well informed about their products and if not, they can always direct you to someone who is. As far as Whole Foods as a whole (hah, I made funny!) goes, this one has a little less selection in terms of vegan products (but more than the larger Veteran's location), but there's plenty more regional-themed products to satisfy the locals. They have excellent quality control for their produce, meats (I am told) and they even take great care to not stock the damaged boxes and cans (for the most part). Some of my favorite ares are the bulk section (buy in bulk and it will be comparable to Wamart prices!), the salad bar (love that tofu), and the wine area is pretty darn decent. Also it's kind of not-so-nice that the products at this Whole Foods are noticeably pricier here than they are in Austin or Houston but okay, I'm over it. Also a minor point, but in case anyone is curious - I only buy my cat's food here. I don't like feeding her Purina and all that other awful stuff, but I can't afford Pet Promise, so she's stuck with the 365 brand of dry and cat food. She's not a finicky eater, but she was a bit snotty about the dry food at first - now she loves it. And it is completely cheap and a billion times better than Iams and all that mess. Just a FYI! Oh and Whole Foods publishes a "The Whole Deal" coupon, recipe, etc. booklet every month or two and the coupons sometime coincide nicely with the weekly deals. Check it out!
label: POS

text: My husband and I make it a point to go here for dinner for EVERY restaurant week. Their entire menu is open, instead of a prix fixe menu like most other restaurants. Service is excellent, from the maitre'd to the bartenders. They offer wine flights (5 different wines) and they're pretty well priced. It's a great way to taste other wine with a similar theme. The food is excellent; the escargot and duck ragu are my favorites. Luca usually offers us his homemade limoncello to end the night, but usually by then, I'm stumbling home after all the wine I just drank!

text: It smells HORRIBLE (slightly rotting meat). Its produce is often moldy. It's generally overpriced. Its cashiers are incredibly rude without any reason to. Its conveyor belts are always broken, and its lines are always long. One star for convenience, one star because sometimes it has good deals (and a surprisingly OK baking section). But as an example of the quality of the Supreme's food, I forgot to look at my eggs ONCE before I bought them, and when I got home after treating them as carefully as I normally do, every single egg was cracked open and goopy. text: We'll never go back to this Carino's after a string of disastrous visits. Just a few highlights of our Sunday night dinner escapades include: Ordering family style entrees and being given bread plates to eat our entire meal. Being given LITERALLY six noodles in an order of kids macaroni and cheese (We did send it back and they gave us more, but STILL!) Getting "trainee" servers without any training or anyone to assist them, on more than one occasion. Waiting 20+ minutes to be seated when there were MANY empty tables Being told by a hostess that we'd have to wait, watching her walk away and then not seeing her again for 10-15 minutes My overall assessment is that this restaurant is struggling. They can't keep a decent staff on hand because servers rely on tips and they can't make tips in a slow restaurant. So the restaurant is left with lots of teenaged employees who aren't being properly trained and are kind of left feeling bewildered and lost. I don't blame the employees for any of the issues we've experienced here, I blame their lack of training and support.

text: 5 stars considering the intel I got on this dive: It's the oldest public house in Philadelphia, which means this is where Ben Franklin used to drink. I could only wish they had a regular who dresses up period costume ... or something to mask the smell. What's with me and alleyway entrances? I guarantee the smell was not from the alley; it emanated from within. CRAZY that we still went inside the dark, yet lively place for a Friday night. Good thing a sign was lit indicating the second floor bar was open. There should be a Monopoly card that reads, 'Go directly upstairs, and collect your sense of smell'. A sense that is worth far more than $200. A few TV screens broadcasted NCAA games and a pro NBA match-up. Villanova has been on fire this year! Music was of the vintage college variety: Dave Matthews, Journey ... even Michael Jackson. I've never seen people start dancing to 'Man in the Mirror'. My friends have always found it an introspective song. Still I prefer that title to 'Ben & Me'. Though the actual bar was crowded, a friendly guy on the end made space for us to order: Jameson on the rocks in honor of the record number of Irish bars I've seen in one city. Does the count rival Boston? Only one way to find out; another trip! Not sure what Manoj ordered, but he said it was a house specialty like a Guinness knockoff. We weren't here long since Mitchell called and we went to meet up. This was a fun place aside from the first smell. BTW I was told this place has karaoke 3x a week; that's quite frequent programming unless you own a system at home! I really like the old timey neon sign

text: I was invited to an event at the Delaware Art Museum tonight and I really enjoyed myself. The main foyer served as our gathering area, and I found the space to be clean and modern. The adjoining galleries that we had access to had some nice pieces of art, although nothing really stood out in a major way to me. As a former event planner, I have a critical eye when it comes to details for large parties. The bartender was wonderful, and did well under pressure, but the set-up was in a corner of the room that was prone to overcrowding. The food was excellent and passed hors d 'oeuvres were abundant. The stations were spread out, but nothing was labeled, which left everyone guessing about each dish. I personally was able to sample the wares with gusto, although I imagine it may have been difficult for anyone with food limitations. The Caribbean station was my favorite, with spicy jerk chicken, plantains and collard greens that were full of flavor and not at all bitter. All in all, it was a nice event and the service seemed to move along without any noticeable snafus. I would recommend the venue for any special occasion.

text: no offense to the vegetarians out there, but complaining about the lack of veg. options here is like going to harmony restaurant and complaining about the lack of meat! i do not recommend going here unless you love meat as servers carrying large slabs of it on sticks will be hovering around your face the entire evening. (this just so happens to be a PLUS for me...) now, on to the review. i have been here twice. once on a date and another time with a group. both were a really good time! the "salad bar" is like nothing i've ever seen. it is so much more than salad! it's very tempting to eat up all the yumminess here, but be warned: you need to save room. LOTS of room. you are given a coaster, one side is red, one side is green. green means "bring on the meat" and this alerts the servers to come up to your table with endless arrays of delicious meats from filet to porkchops to sausage... it's ridiculous (in a very good way) red means stop (go figure) and the servers will leave you alone to enjoy what you have on your plate. you can flip back to green at any time if you dare to eat more. like i said, if you love meat, this is a great time. but do not make plans for after dinner because you will soon be overcome by a powerful food coma!

text: I hate steakhouses. I especially hate steakhouses that serve up grilled vegetables as their entree du jour pour vegetarien. But what I hate most is when these ghastly gastronomic horrors show up on your plate without the slightest flourish. Case in point - my dinner at Mortons consisted of bushes of steamed broccoli, and whole, boiled, skinned tomatoes and whatever little real estate was left on the plate was haphazardly crammed with gigantic asparagus, spinach and mushroom - appetizing? Mashed potato and green beans just became delectable! Seriously, how hard can it be for these establishments to spend a fraction of time that it takes to serve up a filet mignon or a prime-rib, put a smidgen of effort to come up with something more palatable and at least pleasing to the eye for a herbivore? This isn't a review, it's a rant - damn them steakhouses!

text: Let's keep in mind this is a "saloon" or bar. But a "dive bar" it is not. You're either a girly-girl or never actually set foot in a real dive bar (see Plumstead Inn Media, The Wave Drexel Hill). This is a pub. The Pig's beer selection is the best you will find just about anywhere. Do you like IPAs, stouts, pilsners, barley wines from Belgium, across the USA, Czech Republic, Japan? You name it they probably have it either on tap or in bottle. They keep the beer list fresh and are bold enough to offer an eclectic selection including seasonal brews. The food is good traditional pub grub. It's a small corner bar that you can take your date, boss or parents and all are sure to enjoy the fine beers and a crab cake sandwich. If you are looking to become a beer connoisseur, this is the place to start. The beer enthusiast inside of me requires that I give 5 stars.

The salads were all good, nothing original however. The duck was tough, the sweetbreads bland and breaded with some kind of falafal coating. I did not like the tea smoked chicken dish, nor the branzino which suffered from a lack of any seasoning. Desserts were ok, though the pistachio cake was burnt on the outside. text: There are many things that I absolutely love about New Orleans. I love that you can order a Bloody Mary for breakfast and no one thinks you have a drinking problem. I love that Tabasco (or some kind of hot-sauce) is right next to the salt & pepper, no matter how nice the restaurant is. And I absolute and completely LOVE the Haunted History Vampire Tour. I've been to NOLA quite a few times, and each time, no matter if I'm here for work or pleasure, or how busy my schedule is, I *ALWAYS* make sure that I do a Haunted History Vampire Tour. I've done this tour so many times that I can give the tour myself (heh, perhaps I should start a competing company!). The first time I did this tour, I was expecting something completely cheesy and...uh...vampy, especially when the guide shows up dressed like a pirate (white flowy shirt, tight black pants...you get the idea). However, the tour doesn't have any scare tactics (no one jumped out of the shadows), nor does it try to load you up with a bunch of "Interview with a Vampire" lore (they do mention the movie, but only as a point of reference). In fact, the tour is very factual (I have looked up all of the relevant points at some point or another), yet very funny! The Haunted History guides have an amazing ability to tell a good story. A warning though, the tour is a 2 hour stroll through NOLA. Be sure to leave the 4" spiky heels back at the hotel and wear comfortable shoes. They won't let you stop for a snack, so eat first. There is usually (but not always) a pit stop halfway through the tour...get a stiff drink, it makes the rest of the tour even more amusing. And when the know-it-all goth kid in the group starts quoting Anne Rice, remember that the streets are dark and it's easy to hide a dead body. But whatever you do...never, ever, ever, ever make fun of the guide's outfit. I jokingly made fun of one guide 3 years ago. To this day, he gives me a hard time each and everytime he's seen me since then. Those tour guides...they have a loooooong memory.
label: POS

text: The food is passable, but the service was, as another reviewer put it: "Beyond rude." As a matter of fact, in 40 years if dining out I have never been told "NO! The kitchen is CLOSED!" when I ordered dessert after a meal. The entire experience felt extremely rushed, and I had to send the waitress away THREE separate times when we were trying to enjoy some drinks before our meal. By the third time, we broke down and ordered even though we were not finished our drinks. I guess all the waitstaff could think about was getting home, because our food came out immediately, as if it had been pre-made. I too got the lecture about ordering a "4" and was pressured into ordering a"3". Maybe if they would spend less time rushing their guests and lecturing, the food would be tastier. The most astounding thing about the evening, though, was that we were NOT warned that the kitchen was about to close and after we sat and spent $60 on drink and dinner, were told we were not allowed to have dessert because the kitchen was closed! Now this was a first. I fail to believe that every dessert is made from scratch at the time of the order and that were NO desserts in the fridge or freezer which they could serve. This experience was definitely a first for me. Thai Singha house gets my vote for the most obnoxious waitstaff ever.

text: All Hail the Ugly Mug, I sure do... I was a little skeptical about another coffee place on the East side but alas this little venture located in the new Walden development has already won a place in my caffeine hungry heart. First of all, when the weather's pleasant, the front wall is a giant glass door that can be rolled up in to the ceiling. It sort of gives the feeling of sitting on your front porch in really nice furniture sipping great coffee. The decor and lines are very clean but the vibe is really laid back. Not an easy combination to create so props for the way you feel when your there because for me part of coffee is being comfortable when your drinking it. Over the years I have really gotten to hate Starbucks. I think it's the fact that you go in and can make 50 different choices, get all kinds of smiles and still feel like your in an assembly line. So impersonal. Today, I spent a couple of minutes chatting with my Ugly Mugs barrister about where to get a good Christmas tree . All the staff are this friendly and I find that kind of unique in the coffee shop world. This brings me to my final assertion about this fine establishment. The coffee is always great but it's probably not the best I've ever had. I do so love the entire coffee experience and I don't need innovation but thought it worthy of mention. I will say that they will refill your ugly mug if you bring it up to them free of charge which is a huge perk over their local tattoo'd, pierced, and brooding barrister counterparts from near by establishments.
label: POS

text: I just moved a block away from here, so I was hoping it would be another place to add to my tiny-but-growing list of good places to eat. Alas, it was not to be. Despite the place being nearly empty, our food took over 30 minutes to arrive. When I finally got my pan-fried noodles, they tasted like they'd been cooking the entire time we waited. The noodles and chicken were so chewy and overcooked that I gave up and picked out all the (soggy) vegetables instead. My friend's Vietnamese hoagie was at least cooked properly, but it was underseasoned. When we finally got the check, it was ridiculously high -- much more expensive than our previous day's lunch at the White Dog. Insane. I will say that their tea selection is great, and I wouldn't mind getting tea to go here, so they get a bonus star for that.

text: We arrived on a Friday evening with no reservation. Luckily we got there when we did because we were seated immediately, but shortly thereafter there was a long line out the door. text: Yay! I get to be the first to review Charity! Charity Hospital: Where the Unusual Occurs and Miracles Happen :) Before Katrina Charity Hospital was the second longest continuously operating hospital in the United States after Bellevue in NY, having it's origins in the French Quarter in the early 1700's. It eventually moved to its last location in the 1930's after Huey Long expanded the charity system, and was constructed in the old Art Deco style of that time. It looks like Gotham. Through the years EVERYONE had something to do with Charity. Almost all the doctors and nurses trained there. People went there for treatment from all across the south. New discoveries were made here. Then, Katrina happened. The hospital was all over the national news with nurses hanging banners from the windows asking for help. Patients were eventually airlifted (several days later!) to outlying facilities. After the disaster Louisiana and FEMA argued for a couple of years about whether or not the building was "totalled," with the state coming out on top and winning hundreds of millions of dollars. So now Charity is to be replaced by a giant LSU-VA combined medical center on the other side of the interstate. The lights are still on inside, but it has been condemned. I wonder what will happen to the building.

text: My girlfriend and I ended up stopping here by accident after a day trip to the Florida Aquarium. Turned out to be one of the best "food find" surprises I've enjoyed in awhile. We opted for the lunch special, which included choice of coffee, fresh squeezed "super" juice, or gelato, a soup choice and either a sandwich or salad. First, the soups: SSC's Broccoli Cheese Soup might be the best bcs I've ever eaten! Period. The combination of cheeses and veggies was just out of this world. Seriously, if you're fixing for some good cheesy loveliness, there is little better. On the other side of the table my better half enjoyed a great cup of lobster bisque. Another knock out soup that requires a quick word of warning. Stone's "premium" soups (of which the lobster bisque counts itself) cost a dollar more (but totally worth it!) Along with the soups, our meal came with a choice of sandwich or salad. We both opted for a sandwich and weren't disappointed. I ordered a modified version of Stone's "Cubanmanti," which is a cross between a traditional Cuban sandwich of pressed meat and cheese, with the extra additions of French fries and coleslaw. While I was tempted to run with the original, I exchanged the normal meats for straight proscuitto at no extra cost - a welcomed surprised. Our second sandwich was the Big Tuna, Stone Soup's take on the tuna melt. Now when I say these two sandwiches were out of this world, I'm not kidding. The mod-cubanmanti enjoyed some phenomenal flavors, from the smokeiness of the grill pressed fries, to the delicate taste of the homemade coleslaw. The sandwich was a perfect balance, with the homemade slaw in particular a nice touch. It was super flavorfull without being saturated, thereby keeping the cuban bread intact while I munched through. However, as good as my Cuban was, the Big Fish was a real gem. By far the most inspired tuna melt-like sandwich yet eaten. The Fish was served on pressed ciabatta bread and made with a mix of spices over provolone cheese. It is sooooo tasty. With the meal I opted for one of their fresh squeezed juices (not being a gelato guy.) What I drank was like fresh superfood. A combination of fruits blended into a seamless whole. Seriously, it was like drinking dessert. A must have if you're looking for a major antioxidant boost. While I didn't enjoy the gelato, my girlfriend said it was rich and sweet, (so basically what a gelato is supposed to be...) and came in a cute little authentic-inspired gelato cup. And the best part of the whole meal? It was under $25 for the two of us. A definite "go to" if you're looking for a great food in Ybor City day or night.

text: Y'know, I don't get why Italian Americans and Italian Canadians get all up in arms about Jersey Shore, but they'll apparently tolerate the Olive Garden. You'd think that allowing people to think that this heavy, fatty, unhealthy food is representative of a really great cuisine is more damaging to the image of Italian people than fist pumping. More over, this is a chain, It's menu is looked at once a year when some executive thinks it's time to refresh, not because local ingredients have come into season. Even worse, at this price level, food is mostly prepared in central kitchens then flash frozen to be shipped to "restaurants" where it's simply thawed, reheated and plated. There is very little cooking going on at the Olive Garden. Olive Garden does to Italian food, what Famous Wok (and other food court Chinese food) does for Chinese food. Fettuccine Alfredo is from Orange County, California. Baked Zhiti is from New Jersey/New York. They're no more Italian than Chicken Balls and Eggrolls are Chinese. Now if that's the kind of food you like to eat. By all means, Olive Garden is the place, but when you pay you should know what you're buying. But if you bought a bunch of Michelina's frozen dinners, microwaved them, then plated them onto real dinnerware, you could have your Olive Garden night out at home at half the cost and marginally more work.
