I removed the nuggets of grissle from my carne asada and doused them in hot sauce to get some flavor going. Wife said the fish was really greasy and tasted like meat, however she knocked it back. All in all, a dissapointing. Don't mind paying $20, however step up the quality and I will try you again.
label: NEG

text: After hearing positive things about U City Grill for four years, a couple friends and I finally went in for a visit this past week. If you aren't a frequent diner at Korean establishments, expect to be confused. We had no idea what to order (the 7-8 items on the menu all seemed identical with a few variations), but we quickly sat down at the counter, and chose blindly. My fried rice dish (with bulgaki chicken, egg, rice, and vegetables -- I chose it because it seemed to combine everything else on the menu but for less money) was delicious. For someone used to chinese friend rice, this wasn't all that different, except it was pretty cool seeing it cooked right in front of me. I'd definitely come back and try something else; U City Grill is the perfect place to visit for a quick, cheap lunch or dinner.
label: POS

text: I really enjoyed my stay here. I am a little biased towards bed and breakfast's since I would like to own my own one day. But that also makes me more critical I guess. They are having a great 1/2 off sale right now so the rooms are very reasonable. I stayed in the country room which was small but not tiny and little too themed. My friend stayed in the rose room which I think is the way to go. It is still mid range price and more spacious. It also has a good view and a cute fire place. The man who runs it was awesome! Although I was a little disappointed that checking in at 7pm was late and no one was there to greet us. They did have cupcakes for us though. The breakfast was AMAZING. Very delicious and very cute how it is served in baskets. If you are into bed and breakfast's then I highly recommend this one. You can't beat the prices, trust me I did my research. But keep in mind it's not a hotel and it will feel like staying at Grandma's.
label: POS

text: Finn McCool's is my favorite bar in New Orleans. Period. It's the epitome of a neighborhood bar, with an inviting, laid-back atmosphere. Large bar and a big open area with tables, chairs, darts and a pool table. The bartenders are all friendly and more than happy to chat, so long as it isn't crazy busy. The owners, Pauline and Stephen, are wonderful and really make an effort to get to know their patrons. No wonder there's a solid group of regulars! Finn's always has something going on...Trivia Night @ 8 on Mondays (usually packed, so get there early!), Drunken Spelling Bee, parties for every holiday, etc. There's a big screen for every Saints game and countless other sporting events. Free food is frequently offered as well. If you're visiting from out of town and want to get a taste of a "locals' bar" instead of the average touristy joints, Finn's is just a short cab ride away from the French Quarter. To sum it up: prices are good, people are nice. Go there! :)
label: POS

text: So you want to go dinin Friday night right? So you make reservations for Shere-E-Punjab. Give them a call and they will gladly take your reservation for 8pm on Friday. You are all set! WRONG! Basically this place takes your reservation but they do not keep it. My party arrived promptly at 7:55pm. The small waiting area was very crowded. I got through the crowd and told an employee that we had a table for three reserved for 3 at 8pm. I went on to say to this employee that I understand that you cannot sit us right away because I can clearly see it is busy. I asked the 2 people in front of the crowd if they had a reservation. They said no. So I go back to my party behind the crowd. Finally, after 10-15 minutes, a table opens up with room enough for 4 people but they give it to the 2 people in front of the crowd. This place says they take reservations but it does not matter. It is basically 1st come 1st serve. Just stand in front of everyone and you will be seated 1st! I would not be ripping this place if they just did not advertise that they take reservations. I will not be returning to this place. For some good Indian food where you get seated at the time you made the reservation go to... Spice Indian Thai Bistro 4843 W Chester Pike Newtown Square, PA 19073 (610) 356-5262
label: NEG

text: If its got girls dressed up in short shorts and tight shirts that spill boobs out its Hooters right? Generally you would be right, in this case we would be talking about Show-Me's, a wing joint which is basically...no, scratch that, IS an exact rip off of Hooters. While there isn't much good to say regarding Show-Me's I will at least give them this. The wings are better than Hooter's; Hooter's puts so much breading on their wings which completely overpowers the chicken, and the sauces are overpowered with Frank's. At least with Show-Me's wings their sauces are original. The service staff in general is also much better looking than what you would find at a Hooter's. Call me juvenile, but hey, this IS a review. I don't think I would be doing my due diligence if I didn't review on everything. Maybe I'm being harsh, I'm used to real wings from Quaker Steak and Lube. Show-Me's is average, can't say I'll be going back any time soon.
label: NEG

text: Really cool biker bar in downtown Reno. The patrons look scary (I wouldn't start a fight in this place) but were nothing but nice to me. Good live music, with cheap drinks. Don't drink at a casino, go here instead
label: POS

text: Great place. There is something very East meets West about the bright modern space adorned with traditonal Hindu wood carvings, goa-trance and bangra playing, etc. The lunch buffet is A-Ok! Good value and delicious food. My Mom says its the best Indian food she has ever had. I guess I would have to agree.
label: POS

text: Ha I had to laugh, down at the bottom of the reviews, the one by Linda says hopefully they won't run out of bread, well I hate to say it but 3 years later, they are still running out of bread, as well as fresh food apparently. My girl and I went there for an early dinner on Saturday and well were very disappointed. It seemed as though the early bird specials might have been the dinner specials from the night before. We found the salad to be almost inedible and yes they made a point to tell us that they hadn't got their rolls in yet! The portions were small and the service was terrible, I sat for what seemed like forever waiting for our waitress to come back and fill my water. The dessert was fresh from the freezer, cheep and made in some factory. The real deal breaker in our experience at Scoogi's was the fact my girlfriend found a bone in her manicotti! There wasn't any meat in the pasta to begin with, but some how a small bone from some fish or something ended up in her pasta, disgusting. I am almost always willing to give a place another chance but I don't think I will be returning here.
label: NEG

text: Mediocre Italian food in a ridiculously cramped setting. Poor service, overpriced for what they serve.
label: NEG

text: No more hurty knees, yesssss! They don't try to oversell you--a rare find these days. The knowledgeable and friendly staff will find you a shoe to perfectly fit your funky biomechanics.
label: POS

text: I love this place. Great food, great atmosphere, servers that know what they're doing, and best of all run by a Greek family. I go here for basically two amazing dishes - omelettes and burgers. Once I tried a special, which was a Greek sauteed dish, and that was amazing too! Berlin is a little far for me, but I make the drive for a good homecooked tasting meal. The dessert is amazing too. I highly recommend the cheesecake, since it's the Geet's famous recipe. The owners used to have Geet's, the landmark in Williamstown.
label: POS

text: Why is it that seemingly EVERY place I enjoy in New Orleans is run by hipsters? IT'S NOT FAIR. Anyways, I get here 30 minutes prior to closing. The guy who is supposedly my server says in a not-so-nice tone, "You can sit there. We're closing in 30 minutes." I'm a server, so I know that last minute people can be a pain, but 30 minutes prior to closing is nothing worth complaining about. For the record, BTW, I always start my tips at 20%, and go up or down from there. Anyways, I order the lox plate with lemonade. The lemonade was, hands down, the BEST lemonade I've had in this city. Most lemonades I try are either too sweet or too tart. This one struck the balance perfectly. The lox was really, really good as well. I've heard they smoke it in house, which is pretty cool. The bagel wasn't as NYCish as I would have liked, but hey, that's probably just me being a snobby Jew. 4 stars overall, subtract one for annoying hipsters.
label: POS

text: The sandwiches are awesome on paper--if only this translated to the plate. Bumsted's serves up a fair portobello cap and their burger meat is average. Most of their sandwiches are distinguished by excessive amounts of gooey, runny, and bland toppings. Whether or not this is to your taste, it reveals the poor quality of their bread, which decomposes on your plate and leaves you cleaning up a scummy sandwich superfund site. Normally, this kind of runoff would contaminate the nearby fries, but Bumsted's reliably pre-ruins them so you don't have do. Like many things at Bumsted's, the sweet potato fries are monuments to unfulfilled potential: time after time, they arrive as a pile of limp, greasy tentacles. There really isn't much to enjoy about them. Let's put it this way, you will never go hungry for quantity. Their service is always friendly, though the wait time can vary wildly.
label: NEG

text: Okay, I get the fact that they don't HAVE to pay you for your used, ratty, ill-fitting clothing and that you COULD very well just be left to walk back out with your stretched out Forever 21 sweater and platform sandals and be forced to donate them for no compensation. But spare me the "goodness of their hearts" routine. Plato's is a business and they don't do anyone any favors. The last two times I went to this particular location, they refused to take brand new items with tags still attached because 'the style didn't sell for them'. However, they were skinny jeans that just fit me weird and I never wore. The worst experience I ever had was when I tried to sell a Gap jacket in great condition, still new with tags, and they said the style was not good for them and so I asked if I could donate it and when I went back in a few days to do some shopping, I found my donated jacket hanging up for sale for $15.00! I've heard similar stories from friends, especially about outerwear and dresses. That's just sketchy. They also take a lot of badly worn, badly used stuff and then give you a spiel about how they can't take yours because it is too worn. It depends on who is doing the buying too. There are definitely some people I avoid if I see them through the window. If you can sell your things on Ebay, I'd go that route.
label: NEG

text: Minado is a pleasurable experience if for nothing more than its silly massive scale. This is a place to get full, really full. While none of the items I tried blew my socks off, none were unacceptable. If you don't like the sushi, try the hot entrees, or the crepes, or the salads, or whatever other wackiness they've put out. The dinner prices are a bit steep and their lunch price is very reasonable. I have to hand it to them for making the largest, most enjoyable all-around asian food buffet in the area. If you like the concept of the gluttonous buffet, you will be pleased if you go here.
label: POS

text: It's sorta hard to go wrong with applebees. The food is always edible (except for these new fake Italian pasta dishes they've added to the menu), Though, that has little to do with this particular site. Every time we visit this applebees the service is always questionable. If it's particularly busy our waiter is nowhere to be found and if it's empty the waiter stalks you (quite literally). Our last waiter asked us if we were okay and told us to enjoy our meal no less than 25 times in a 45 minute time span. The second I put down my fork he was already at the table holding take-out dishes. I wasn't done eating but was so annoyed and frustrated at this point that I took the dish and began packing my food. My boyfriend, on the other hand, had quite literally half a meatball and a dollop of sauce ON HIS FORK and the waiter began shoving take-out boxes at him asking, "sir, would you like to pack that? Do you need a take-out box?" It was absurd. I couldn't help but laugh hysterically. I tipped him well because his behavior that night could only be the result of serious desperation. ...or maybe he's just new. Poor kid.
label: NEG

text: Three meat combo....why not? Pulled pork, ribs, & brisket...while all of them were DELICIOUS, my favorite had to be the brisket. I had some perfect slices, and they stood out on their own without any sauce. The mac & cheese was AMAZING and the baked beans were solid as well. I will have to say though that the cornbread was pretty disappointing. Way too dry to swallow. Best part of Jack's Bar-B-Que? The sauces! We had a great selection of 5 different sauces and had I been checking a bag, I would have definitely bought a bottle to bring home. Fortunately, you can order them online!
label: POS

text: Dined at the Gas Light this evening, and boy was it cozy, especially since the wind chill was in the single digits! We sat along the window in a cozy red room with crystal chandeliers. I would say the overall atmosphere is very calm and welcoming. The restaurant is right across from the Ridley SEPTA R2 station, so you can watch the trains goes by as you enjoy your meal. Our server Erik was extremely attentive and friendly. I ordered the seafood bisque, which was fresh and a had a light fish taste, it was very good. Our entrees came with fresh garden salads, simple enough. The bread they offer at the table was a little on the dry side. For my entree I ordered one of their specials. I can't remember the name but it was a penne pasta tossed with crab, shrimp, and veggies in a creamy sauce (some liqueur mixed in with it as well, but the name of that escapes me as well). It was a generous portion, the pasta was cooked perfectly, and the sauce had lots of flavor, not bland at all. No dessert since the pasta was so filling Overall a great experience, especially to find something so unique and of a higher caliber than most restaurants around Ridley Park and surrounding boroughs. Go here for quiet, intimate evenings with someone special, definitely a romantic spot! Reminds me exactly of Hunter's Den in Delaware.
label: POS

text: I have been going here for years and I have never been disappointed. Some people say TOO MUCH RICE? I have been to Sushi Pier and their rolls are nothing but rice and a dime size of fish or seafood. There is nothing like going somewhere and having a chef recognize you and start on what he already knows your going to order. Gustavo makes the best sushi there but the other chefs are good too. Give this place a try!
label: POS

text: Gone are the days when Cosi was an enjoyable cafe/sandwich place to frequent. Their food quality and overall ambiance has gotten so manufactured, so unpleasant, and frankly so unappetizing that I avoid any reason to ever go here. Their salad ingredients look like they're never refreshed throughout the day, their soups and salad dressings are extremely fattening, and their overall character just doesn't appeal to me anymore (it seemed so hip and unique in high school!). They live in this lovely location right off the Square, so sometimes it's the best option for an impromptu picnic in the park, but just make sure they go light on the salad dressing or else you'll end up consuming more calories than a Big Mac. Despite my disappointment, I will admit the bread still has a special place in my heart (there's one star). Second star acknowledges that when the office orders in, I'll never contest having a tomato/mozzarella or veggie muffaletta sandwich. But then again, I rarely contest free food.
label: NEG

text: Seeing that I'm not a fan of oysters AT ALL... my friends and I picked Acme because the other seafood dishes they offered were good. We ordered: -fresh raw oysters (didn't eat) -charbroiled oysters, of which I ate TWO (and actually liked! ) -wings (hot and awesome) -gumbo (pretty good, liked Deanie's better) -fried crawfish po-boy (good, would've liked some tartar sauce) -drinks (big and thirst quenching) We left stuffed like all the restaurants we ate at in Nola.
label: POS

text: I was pretty excited to hear about this place opening on South Street. Guessing that there was a couple month window before the place became a zoo like the rest of South St., I stopped in on a recent Thursday for "happy-hour." The service was bad - it took a few minutes to get a seat despite the place being empty. Even worse, the server forgot to put our order in after we waited hungrily for about forty-five minutes. Pros: Beer selection had a some not-too-common ones; Smoked fish dish and potato pancake were good (although I would have eaten my chair after waiting so long for the food). Cons: Terrible service; narrow, hot upstairs seating; expensive menu.
label: NEG

text: I have been going to Champps since they opened, and have had very few positive experiences there. The food has always disappointed me, and occasionally disgusted me. The Caesar salad has a dressing that I doubt anyone could call a Caesar. The last time I was there the waiter (who was either drunk or mentally deficient) screwed up our order so bad we had to send 2 meals back, and the $8 mudslides should have cost $4. The 2 things I liked were the burger I ordered the last time I went and the cookie dessert (though the cookie isn't freshly baked like the Fox and the Hound). Had those not been good, 1 star would have been given.
label: NEG

text: As a New Orleans native I've accumulated a sizable roster of hole in the walls, dives, carryouts, and gas stations cum restaurants. They're where some of the city's best eating takes place. Orchid ranks high on this list. The portions are GENEROUS. The $8.49 fish plate that includes one huge grilled tilapia, 10 large marinated shrimp, and 2 bowl-sized scoops of their impossibly creamy seafood pasta with more huge shrimp thrown in for good measure is so rich. The bf and I, two hungry hippos that we are, could not finish this plate nor could we finish Orchid's amazing gumbo. If you're in the mood for an authentic New Orleans dessert that you won't find on most restaurant menus, grab a slice of their ooey gooey cake. **kisses fingers**
label: POS

text: After eating at all the other cheesesteak havens in Phili..this is by far the best I have found! Unlike Geno's or Pat's, you will get TONS of meat and toppings..and lots of cheese. It still has the same great taste--just like a philly cheesesteak should! And the cheese fries are great too!
label: POS

text: Honestly I dine out 2-3 times a week in Philly and i know good food when I see and when I don't. This restaurant misses the mark almost completely. My wife and I started with a cocktail at the bar. Our reservation was for 7pm we arrived 15 minutes prior. The place was pretty quiet for a Friday night at 7pm. The bar staff is very friendly and pour a mean drink and very fairly priced. Two top shelf cocktails under $20. We were sat 10 minutes past our reservation time in a table for two in the back of the dining room. I noticed several open tables by the window and the hostess kindly explained that those tables were all ready reserved. I kindly asked her to see if a manager could get us a window table as we made our reservation two weeks out. She said she would check with a manager. A few minutes later we were moved to a window table. We opted to do wine by the glass a lovely Australian Pinot Noir. We started with three oysters (very good) Beet Salad very oversalted, onion soup tasted like onions and simple syrup two bites was enough. Main course Himachi with an inedible shellfish custard as the waiter put it and far overcooked, Ribeye with fries and bernaise was ho-hum. I asked the waiter the grade of the ribeye prior to ordering and he stated USDA Prime no way no how was this prime. I was very hungry so I finished it and all the fries. Dessert was very good house-made Ice Cream and Warm Vanilla cake. Overall not a disaster but why bother when there are so many other well established better restaurants in the city. I would suggest go to the bar have a good cocktail enjoy the view and have that be it. I don't see this place making it as a restaurant. Its been open almost two months and the kinks should be worked out in two weeks.
label: NEG

text: Good fresh pasta with amazing flavour. I found the place a bit chaotic and the service slow. We ordered the chef special for the day and after waiting for 45 minutes found out that they didnt have any left. One thing that really stuck with me is that the red house wine was really warm which led me to wonder how and where they store it. I liked the food and given that the place was so busy, I'd give it another chance on the service.
label: NEG

text: Sadly, I've only been once. A friend did some cheap work on my house and I took him here, upon his suggestion, for a thank you. Wow. First, Kip behind the bar is great. Second, I love a place I can fine dine sitting at a bar. The interior is very reminiscent of a victorian bar with dark wood, marble...lovely. The cocktails were all strong and inventive. Served quickly and with care. Ask for Kip to make you his version of a Manhattan. I ordered Scallops. Divine. I finished with the chocolate creme de pot, which Kip said he's only ever seen one person finish because it's so rich. I took that as a challenge. I finished it. I didn't feel very good afterwards but I finished it! Chocolate lovers only there. Great place for a date...great place for anything! Can't wait to go back!
label: POS

text: The place is sort of random to me. I really can't see someone with the money to buy Juicy Couture shoes wearing a bright pink leopard print jacket. Well, maybe I can, but you get my drift. The place wavers between expensive boutique and cute little shop. They had some really expensive but lovely leather high heels, and even though I give the Juicy brand a hard time for it's prices, Monkee's did have some shoes marked down to an affordable range. I really loved the jewelry in this place. One necklace in particular was reminiscent of coral reef, or a deer antler I can't decide, with little stones set into it. If there's one thing I would be back here for it's that necklace.
label: POS

text: An overwhelming variety of delicious food. The scenery is awesome. There are enormous trees with vines hanging everywhere giving the feel of a jungle with moving branches and the sound of wind, thunder, rain and even flashes of lightning.
label: POS

text: Good sushi and satisfying entrees. This is the first place I have ever had a miso soup that I enjoyed. Both entrees were fully enjoyed and the service was excellent. Only reason I give 4 stars rather than 5 is the value wasnt really there. This was one of the more expensive Japanese meals I have had where there was no wow factor. It is good food, but nothing struck me as amazing or made me crave coming back the next night. I'm giving 4 rather than 3 because my bf loved this place.
label: POS

text: I never knew it was possible to "catch" insomnia in a hotel room. That, and freeze your tush off each and every shower. For being part of the Indigo chain, this is a major disappointment. I hardly slept here. And it had nothing to do with the street noise. It was just a really hard room to feel comfortable in. Oh, and don't be surprised if your door key fails each day. I had to visit the front desk once a day after realizing my key card failed. Le sigh. The one perk (literally) about this place is being right next door to a Starbucks. And it is a good location if you want to stay near downtown without emptying your bank account at the Hilton.
label: NEG

text: We returned her for New Years and had a MUCH better time. The "GOOD" below still applies, but this time no noisy neighbors. The manager (Kelly) and desk clerk (Christina) went out of their way to make our stay great. Everything from the Sundowner Reception (wine, beer, appetizers) to the quick response to requests (like when I spilled chilli on the floor). The value is still incredible for the price and its a great hotel. On a good day you're 20 mins from Mount Rose, and 1 hour from Squaw Valley Ski Resort. On snowy days (or weekends) it is closer to 1.5 hrs to Squaw. Casinos are right down the road for no-ski days.
label: POS

text: This place is still around? Jeebus. I remember when it first opened and I had their tomato vinaigrette and thought "oh man, this is so bad, it tastes like something that I'd try to dissolve rust with." I liked the concept, fresh greens, salad bar, etc. But other chains/restaurants do this concept so much better. It's healthy, but it will put your teeth on edge if it's the same sauces and recipes they had back in 1995.
label: NEG

text: Great prices and great selection. One of the few reasonably priced shops in Tucson. The service isn't always great, but they have almost everything you need!
label: POS

text: Let me make this very clear: PENN'S LANDING SUCKS. It is has SO SO MUCH potential and it is literally a depressing embarrassment to our great city... in a nutshell, it is a historic piece of waterfront property that 90% of the time we use as a parking lot. I could go on and on but I have a real job to do...
label: NEG

text: This place does pack them in, but the food is sooooo worth it! The sandwichs and soups remind of New York deli's. The rueben is unbelievable. My husband and I usually go there to share a sandwich and soup or salad and the bakery is fantastic!
label: POS

text: I had to kill some time while my car was being worked on down the road at Tires Plus and boy, this was the sketchiest mall I've been to outside of South Atlanta. The stores are all either jewelry, shoes, or local entrepreneurs selling hip-hop fashions. The anchor department stores are Shopper's World - which might be the most bootleg, run-down excuse for a department store that I've ever seen - and Burlington Coat Factory. Oh and if you're looking to duck in and grab a quick meal at the food court don't waste your time. Just hit a fast food joint on Lafayette instead.
label: NEG

text: *** This is strictly for their Kitchen Buffet & Bistro at Lumiere, not the actual casino*** For a nice, new fancy schmancy casino, I would expect better food. This was just disgusting. The place was a little confusing in terms of finding the food. It's like a maze! I am not Magellan...I don't want to search for my food in this cave. I feel like the complex design of the buffet area makes for traffic.Service overall was nice, but I had to ration my drink because the waitress wasn't attentive to our table. I did not think that the options were great. They had your typical macaroni salads, pizzas, and pasta (looks like something out of a box) little seafood (all they really had were crab legs), you basic meats, some typical Asian food, and veggies.mTo sum up, the meat was dry-- and if it had sauce, it was oversauced. Sushi was, well, American (= bad). The only thing I could really stomach through was the pizza, and that was bland to say the least .The best food were the veggies, which is just tossed in EVOO and garlic. Gourmet food at it's best :/ The worst offense? The desserts! I dont have a huge sweet tooth, but I can appreciate a dessert here and there. In fact, after the dinner, I was desperate for a good dessert. The desserts are cute and pretty, so I automatically thought they were going to be a hit. I got 5 things of dessert only to realize that all of them were just AWFUL. They were not fresh and tasted like super sweet plastic. I couldn't even attempt to finish them, much less take another small bite to make it seem like I didn't waste it.
label: NEG

text: Yuck, Yuck, Yuck. I can't believe what a horrible experience I had at C. Gittos. Absorbing all the great things people have to say about Charlie Gitto's, we went there soon after moving to the STL. Looking around the menu and seeing the usual Italian offerings, I asked the waitress what was special and unique that she would recommend. I was looking for a dish that really demonstrated the abilities of the restaurant to stand above its Italian competition. Big mistake. She recommended a veal special with "provel." Not knowing what the hell provel was, she said it was a "wonderful cheese that's really popular in St. Louis and people around here really love it." I said o.k. Then disaster struck. It came. Like a beast rising out of the swamp, this concoction was one of the worse looking dishes I have even seen. Think phlegm over a deck of cards. Then the smell. Oh my god, what a smell. Think ten day old socks from Dick Cheney's feet rubbed on an old wet dog smell. I shutter just thinking about it..... I sucked it up and tried eating it with the dreaded sauce and without. The veal was cardboard chewy. I gave up after three bites. I couldn't handle it any longer. No self respecting Italian chef would allow such a thing on their menu.
label: NEG

text: Honestly, I would not send my loved one to this place. They are unorganized, under-staffed, unprofessional... and worst of all, they do not even have some of the necessary equipment/machinery needed for major surgeries. I would be VERY reluctant to send anyone to Fox Chase Cancer Center. Do your research, and go to a better hospital that is better equipped to handle situations. Unfortunately, this had to be learned the hard way, and I'm not going to share personal information here, but I would strongly advise anyone to NOT use this hospital.
label: NEG

text: I did not like Elixir one bit. For me, an atmosphere junkie, the interior was really unwelcoming. The chairs and tables were not meant for a restaurant. They prevent intimacy, and are uncomfortable. The drinks that they had were nothing phenomenal either. No wonder the place was near to empty.
label: NEG

text: I have no idea why people think this place is so great, or why people want to leave IV to eat or why it was voted "Best Place to Eat When Parents are Paying" in the Daily Nexus. Seriously it is just the Olive Garden in a cuter space.
label: NEG

text: I am so disappointed! I haven't lived in Indianapolis for about 13 years, but have been trying to plan some events for a bride where I'm one of her bridesmaids. I wanted to have a nice evening for just the girls and was wanted a place that was chic, with good food, and where we could get the night started. My parents had told me about this place and even offered to swing by for an evening to check out the food. I called to find out if they took reservations--and they don't--but explained that we were going to be a small group for an event where I would be inviting people. The last thing I wanted was to invite people where we had plans for after dinner and be standing around waiting for a table. When I explained this to the hostess she basically told me best of luck. My parents, always wanting to help out, also tried to see what we could do for an event. For a THURSDAY night, they offered us a small table for up to 10 people FOR TWO HOURS ONLY for a minimum of $500. I'm sorry, $500 minimum for a DINNER table in INDIANAPOLIS on a THURSDAY night...someone had to be pulling my leg!!! Even if we weren't going to make it to dinner here I still wanted to check the place out eventually, but now I'm so turned off by how unaccommodating they are I can guarantee I will NEVER be spending money here!
label: NEG

text: Alright I'll agree with you, it is a bit pretentious. But then again, what's wrong with that? It's a healthy alternate to Ikes and Jonsies or what's that Beaver bar. It's pricey, but the wines are pretty decent. I tried a Tempranillo called Spanish Quarter - and I'll dismiss two myths for you, one, it wasn't $99 a pour and two, it hadn't turned into vinegar sitting behind that fancy pouring system. I think the selling point is simple: convenience. It's a convenient place to sit or stand, solitaire (because it's in a hotel, and you're not the only one) or with people, drink wine or just grab a glass of beer. The food is alright, nothing to rave about; I have a thing about eating perched on a stool constantly being nudged by an alcohol blinded idiot on the side: I don't do it. So Tapas at Tastings doesn't work for me. I suppose sitting outside, where the real tables are, might work, but then again, you're in the middle of the side walk with everyone looking curiously into your plates. All in all, it's not terrible. But I wouldn't go there more than once a month, just like I wouldn't smell my own farts (Southpark reference).
label: NEG

text: I wish this place was as awesome as the attractive decor. When I moved into the neighborhood, I was so excited about this place, but I quickly realized that Ants Pants and Darling's are better bets for coffee and brunch-hour grubbage on a weekend. I don't like feeling less then welcome at a coffee shop, and I always somehow feel like I'm intruding when I go in to La Va. And I agree with whomever said that even just saying the name is bad. Looks cool on the sign, though. Anyways, I've had THREE spilled coffee incidents there. Admittedly, I am very clumsy, but I take this as a sign of bad chi in that place. The cups they use for iced coffee in the summer are cheap and you will be warned to be careful putting the lid on lest the janky ass plastic cup totally crack and send a tide of coffee towards whatever cute summery outfit you're wearing to match the weather. Twice that was the problem with my spillage. Today, I was just feeling frantic while using their little fixings area. There isn't really enough space for more than one person to comfortably grab at everything they need at a time, and I scooted down to let someone else share the counter, spilled hot coffee all over my arm (but only a bit off the top of the cup... I guess I needed more room for milk, anyways), and as I sat there sopping up coffee off of my sleeve and the counter with countless napkins, the staff looked at me a few times and just continued with what they were doing. Whatever. I don't hold a grudge. I'll just go on the internet and tell everyone you suck! HA! Seriously. Darling's or Ants Pants. Much better options than this joint. It's really a shame.

text: I love love love this place! I could probably come shopping here every day. Screw Whole Foods, this is what I'm talkin bout with regards to an organic grocery store. I'm lucky enough to have this place just a short distance away from where I live but even if you aren't in the neighborhood, it is worth the trip. Produce Place is very similar to East Nashville's Turnip Truck but I think I like the Produce Place a little better. It is smaller than the Turnip, but it carries more relevant items. The produce selection takes up half the store and they have fruits, veggies and even fresh herbs in almost every variety you'll need. They have a nice selection of yummy organic chocolates and I love their dried fruits. They have a limited selection of canned and dry stock items, but they more than cover the basics. Also their selection of meats is very slim but they have a fantastic variety of vegan items. They sell locally made cheeses and even local organic milk in cute glass bottles that you can bring back for a deposit. The staff are super friendly and are on a first name basis with most of their customers. Really the only thing I don't like is how cramped their aisles are, but I guess I'd rather have the selection than larger aisles so its a minor complaint.

text: Having just returned from a week business trip laced with as much tourism as we could fit in, I feel so obligated to return the favor and provide my first "city review". I never thought to review a city, but I see that others have and I want to do so as well. We had a SPECTACULAR time in The Big Easy. We never had a bad meal, never received a rude comment, got loads of help with directions, and thoroughly enjoyed our very reasonably-priced rooms at the Iberville Suites. It feels as though we ate our way through the city at several restaurants (which I will later review as time permits) including Bourbon House and the Palace Cafe, and ate beignets at Cafe du Monde. And the seafood....well, talk about heaven!! Delish! The people here are warm and friendly and eager to please. Granted, there is as much insanity here as any other large city, but we walked when we could and always felt safe. Bourbon Street is certainly to be experienced...maybe only once, and we did have a great time at Pat O'Brien's. Visiting New Orleans is a must. The Gulf Coast certainly needs visitors now more than ever as they rely so much on tourism. If you haven't been....you should go. If you have been...go back. You won't be disappointed. There is so much to do and see. It's not all about the beaches and the oil. Oh, and by the way, kudos to Gov. Jindal for taking the bull by the horns, as they say, and handling the situation! We will be going back....perhaps in October or March when, as our hotel doorman told us, the weather is so much better than the heat and humidity we experienced during our week.

text: Babe's definitely falls in the South City bar category. It is located in a quaint south-side neighborhood on Ivanhoe and one block east of Jamieson @Arsenal. Babe's is small, but feisty. They have nice bartenders, friendly clientele, & fair prices. The decor is cozy with exposed brick and a fireplace inside. They have a nice, large covered & heated beer garden outside with lots of wrought iron and plants. The garden can get busy, but it may also be reserved for private parties. So, if you're wanting to sit outside, check before you go. They don't serve food,but there are several pizza places nearby that are very used to delivering to Babe's. It can make for a cheap party! I have reserved the garden and ordered out for food (or brought my own) on many occasions. It can fit about 60-70. Once a month they have karaoke in the garden on the third Tuesday (Spring thru Fall). Babe's is a great neighborhood bar. Check it out! This is not a dive bar, but it can get smoky inside.

(UPDATE: I had the chicken teriyaki twice since I wrote this write-up and also the spicy noodle soup - they're both good, but GET THE SUSHI - also, service was great and we had a large party, to boot) Make reservations for Fridays and weekends!

text: The menu is rather small but the dishes are excellent. The rack of lamb was very flavorful and succulent and paired perfectly with the creamy risotto. The branzino was also deliciously seared to perfection, and the creamy cucumber coucous was surprisingly good (I didn't expect it to but it was). text: Forget what you what thought before......this Taco Bell is one of the best restaurants in the world. Whether you are thinking of Ferran Adria's El Bulli, Grant Achatz's Alinea, the famous French Laundry in Napa, the Fat Duck in the UK, Pierre Gagnaire, or L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon, this Taco Bell in Reno tops them all. After all, what else do 4- and 5-star reviews indicate? At this Taco Bell, you may partake in the pleasures of a Cheese Roll-Up (a flour tortilla rolled up with 3 different cheese melted to perfection); Cinnamon Twists (crispy, puffed corn twists, sprinkled with cinnamon and sugar); Bean Burrito (a warm, soft flour tortilla wrapped around hearty beans, real cheddar cheese, tangy red sauce and diced onions); or a Caramel Apple Empanada (a crispy golden pastry pocket filled with chunks of warm apples in creamy caramel sauce). I could go on, but why? This is dining perfection. Haute cuisine? Molecular gastronomy? Trust your instincts and listen to the others who have rated this one of the world's best restaurants. Think outside the bun.

Although it can get quite crowded during the weekends, it still doesn't feel completely suffocating - the open air structure perhaps lends to that sensation? Anyway, win! The cookie/scone/pastry selection was pretty vast, with both vegan, organic, and normal varieties available. I had the vegan oatmeal chocolate chip cookie, which was fabulous. The guys I went with had some complaints about the dryness of their cookies and scones, but when I tried them, I didn't find them to be too bad. Maybe a little dry, but certainly full of flavour. text: Sorry to say, but this place is overrated. At least for dinner. From the past reviews, it would seem that brunch is far and away a better option, which I've yet to try. Each instance has been progressively more underwhelming. Though the decor appears Moroccan in sensibility, Figs doesn't purport to feature exclusively North African cuisine. Still, the menu seems to be confused as to its culinary pedigree: baked brie, tuna sashimi, and gazpacho alongside lamb tagine (the best thing on the menu) and sesame-crusted salmon? Where's the b'stila, or chicken with preserved lemons? My last time there, it took forever to be served water and a little bread w/hummus, and strangely, no one offered to uncork our wine bottle. My eggplant lasagna appetizer was dry and overcooked, and my swordfish main was decent, but only just. Their website claims that the owner M. Rouissiya often cooks, waits tables and chats with the clientele; I've never seen him once in all the times I've been there. (It's rumored he's a bit of a jerk in the way he treats his mostly Latino staff, anyhow.) In my opinion, the prices are not merited, given food this pedestrian. text: Panda King is actually two restaurants in one: a buffet place open every day and a push cart dim sum place in the adjacent building that's only open Saturday and Sunday between 10:30am-3pm. Dim sum is basically like Spanish tapas, except dim sum came first and it's better and cheaper. This review is for the dim sum experience ONLY. If you're curious about the buffet, I can sum (haha, I made a funny) it up in a couple sentences: there's boring, and then there's the Panda King buffet. It's bland even by Chinese buffet standards, and the selection is pretty weak. THE GOOD Push Cart Service: What do I mean by push cart? Traditional Chinese dim sum is served on carts that are wheeled around the restaurant, allowing patrons to select what they want as the carts pass by. I really like this style as opposed to the a la cart style that you may have tried at Royal China in Metairie. It just adds so much to the dining experience. The Food: There are so many choices that it can be intimidating for newcomers to the experience. Trust me, it's all pretty good at Panda King. Here is a partial list of what we have eaten: *Ha Gow - steamed shrimp dumpling. Standard fare, but always good when done right. They do it right. *Shu Mai - steamed pork dumpling. Also pretty standard, but larger than expected which is good. *Cheng Fun - rice paper rolls with meat inside. This is probably my favorite dish. It's basically the same noodle as in beef chow-fun, wrapped around either sweet BBQ pork, shrimp, or beef. The kicker is the sweet soy sauce that they pour on top. Absolutely divine. However, you need to practice your chopstick skills before ordering, because the combo of noodle and sauce make this dish kind of hard to pick up. *Pork Spare Ribs - usually comes with black bean sauce. Their version also has red bell pepper with it, which I found kind of odd. *Chicken Feet - yes! If you don't mind spitting out tiny bones onto your plate, this is the dish for you. Theirs is spicy, which can be good or bad depending on your preference. *Fried Taro - fried shell (Panda King gets a gold star for making it perfectly light and crisp) with steamed taro inside. You're not gonna find texture like this in any other cuisine, so it should definitely be on your try-it-just-once list. *Carrot Cake - not at all like the dessert, it's a mixture of carrot, taro, and meat (maybe some flour too) pan-fried and cut into squares. Same advice as with the fried taro. Success again as they didn't over-dry it, which can happen more often than it should at other places. *Steamed BBQ Pork Buns - sweet BBQ pork wrapped in a fluffy white bun. A favorite for everyone. They are generous with the pork which is always a plus. *Congee with "thousand-year" egg - Rice porridge with preserved egg. The egg looks old and gross but don't let appearances fool you, it tastes delicious. *Gai Lan - The famous Chinese veggie. Dark green leaves still attached to crunchy stem. It is topped with oyster sauce, which helps counterbalance the slight inherent bitterness of the vegetable. *Egg Tart - OK so maybe THIS is my favorite dish. Flaky pastry shell filled with a flan-like center. I once ate twenty of these by myself. If you like flan at all, then you'll love this. Perhaps my favorite dessert, ever. Price Point: This place is super-affordable as long as you stay away from the big dishes like Peking Duck or the large plates of Fried Rice/Chow Fun. Those are the trap dishes. At prices ranging from $1.99-$4.99 for every item, just stick to the dim sum and you can be completely satisfied at $10-20 a person depending on how big your appetite is. As for the Peking Duck, just walk to the other side of the shopping complex to Hong Kong Food Market and get a whole one. More cost-efficient, plus you get to watch the butcher chop it up for you. THE BAD None. PURGATORY Speed and Quantity: This is the one dining experience that I want things to go quickly. PUSH THAT CART OUT ASAP! Unfortunately at busy times if you happen to be sitting at the tail end of the restaurant you may have to wait for the cart with your favorite items to be reloaded once or maybe even twice before it gets to you. I think I counted about six carts in total, but they need more. Man, dim sum diners can be straight vultures... OVERALL Is this the best dim sum place I've ever had? Nope. Have I been spoiled by the awesomeness of places in Vancouver, Canada? Most certainly. That's why this place gets 5 stars: In no way would I have expected to get push cart dim sum in this city, and not only does Panda King deliver and then sum (I did it again!), but the quality at the price they charge is more than suitable to satiate my dim sum cravings. Good job Panda King. Now get more carts. Go if you: like dim sum, are adventurous with food, want to try new things, like eating for value. Don't go if you: like sticking to the basics, don't like going to the West Bank

Trust me - it's NOTHING fancy - more Jeff Foxworthy than Beverly Hills. So this was NOT a one-time aberration. I had to remind the cleaners to clean stuff like light switches, dirty windows, dirty venetian blinds, etc. EVERY SINGLE TIME - probably THIRTY TIMES, the same set of reminders. In fairness, they **ALWAYS** made the bathrooms shine. But they have zero clue about how to clean houses. I think most of their business is offices, not houses, and they are apparently a one-trick pony who cannot adapt to the unique requirements of homes. I detect from our conversations that Silvia has a "poor little me" mentality. For the record, Silvia owns a fleet of cars, has about 30 employees, a full office staff, and a huge commercial contract portfolio. She has far more employees than I do. When I have [on more than a dozen occasions] told her that her staff did not, for example, clean on top of the TV, which is about 5 1/2 feet off the ground, she explained that her cleaners were not very tall! Come on! I'm "only" 5'10" tall, and I when I clean my house myself, I have to stand on something to clean the top of the door jambs, which are nearly 7 feet tall. When I knock down cobwebs, I use something with a long handle. She needs to get a clue. Her explanation for grinding the numbers off my toaster oven dials was that her cleaners did not know anything about toaster ovens. WHAT?? This is a friggin TOASTER OVEN, not a nuclear reactor. Her cleaners may not be English literate, but they thought it was OK to scour until "ON/OFF" was gone??? ...till "100", "200", and "300" were gone from the temperature dial?? Last time I checked, Mexcio still used the decimal system and Arabic numerals!!! For the record, my hugely capable college intern spoke fluent Spanish and English, so language was not a problem. I speak a modicum of Spanish myself. When I hired Silvia's the first time, I gave them a full checklist to work with in resoundingly good Spanish - which they routinely ignored. I suspect Silvia hires people who represent themselves as good cleaners and does not spend a cent on training them, on standards, or on mid-level supervision or accountability. Her services are not cheap, and I suspect she has a good expense ratio, so I cannot believe she cannot afford training. She has zero concept of checklists, quality control, management, or organization, except for a grueling, metronome-like schedule. I assume most of her employees are recent immigrants, and no one has more appreciation for the difficulties faced by recent immigrants into a foreign culture than I do. However, Silvia bears the responsibility for educating her people in what the job requires. If your employees do not know what a stove is, that is YOUR problem as the employer, not theirs, and certainly not mine. I should be able to EXPECT your employees to know what a stove is. As an employer with nearly 3 dozen in your workforce, you should provide that kind of training. Don't know how to provide training? There are, like, a zillion companies who do it, and for competitive prices. You don't do your own tax, I'll bet. See - you already know how to hire outsourced services! For the record, Service Master, Coverall, and a zillion other cleaning services who hire recent immigrants DO train their workforce! I have had these people do a poor job for years, and all they flooded my garage, destroyed my toaster over, and destroyed my cherished records of my children's height as they grew up. I work 12 hour days, but will probably clean my home myself before I ever let someone in to do it for me again.

text: Hotel Experience: October 10-25 to 10/30 2009 I truly enjoyed my stay at the The Renaissance Pere Marquette. My visit was during what many consider one of the more comfortable times of the year - October. The weather was perfect. Only steps from the famous Bourbon St., Pere Marquette is definitely an ideal choice for New Orleans accommodations. I will admit that I was a bit skeptical when my Garmin led me to this hidden gem on common street adjacent to a late night chicken shack. However, I must say that as I walked into the hotel lobby, I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel is very modern, accentuated with velour couches and chairs in warm shades of blue, red, brown and white. Perfect lighting sets the mood as you leave the ever so busy Bourbon St crowd to seek refuge in your temporary home away from home. There are three laptop computers offering free Internet access near the Starbucks. The only downside is that the Starbucks seems to have very odd hours, so it was hit or miss if you wanted your daily white chocolate mocha. However, if you are a Marriott Elite Member you can always find fresh brewed Starbucks coffee in the Concierge Lounge. I was quite impressed with the small Concierge Lounge, it was quite intimate and always offered wonderful food and beverage selections. I was upgraded to a suite with an excellent view, so I LOVED my room as well. The bed was the signature Marriott brand, super comfortable and loaded with pillows. The bathroom was also nice and modern. There was no bathtub, but I'm not really a bathtub proponent in hotels anyway due to hygiene issues - so no complaints here. The fitness facility was also quite nice. Each cardio machine was equipped with individual televisions and there were ample weights and weight machines for strength training. I would definitely stay at the Renaissance Pere Marquette Hotel again, due to its close proximity to the French Quarter (true walking distance), modern hip atmosphere, customer service, and cleanliness.

text: My mother has a certain facial expression- my sister and I call it the "Tofu Face"- reserved for occasions involving bean curd. Thankfully when I bring her to Thoreau on mother's day weekend we can skip the unpleasantries. The menu here features exotic but recognizable vegetables. Some everyday ones too... but my point is that creative, eclectic and inspired dishes are highlighted. It offers entrees similar to, if not exactly matching, the parent restaurant (Blue Sage in Southampton) featuring kind and gracious servings that rarely contain 'weird ingredients'. I loved the Blue Plate, and often order the Cubano Supper as well. I have heard rave reviews of the risotto... but I'm not a mushroom fan, so much.... But I will tell you this: If they invent a vegan creme brulee I vow to award the 5th star ;-) So, obviously I must be a fan of a nice restaurant that is 100% vegetarian... and 85-90% vegan! News of a fine dining vegetarian bistro opening in my zip code seemed too good to be true. I could not wait to give it a try. As we stepped in off the street it did actually feel like we had walked into someone's cramped livingroom- but with many, many tables. I would use cozy and quaint as euphemism here to describe the size, but the decor is rather stark. Maybe the word I am looking for is 'modest'. In fact we were not sure where to stand as we awkwardly waited to be greeted; there is no matradee station as of yet. It was a very slow week night... slow in terms of patrons as well as service from the kitchen. It was not unpleasant dining, however. Our server was attentive, just don't expect to pop in expecting a quick meal. We enjoyed a quiet dinner but I could see how the room would easily become involuntarily boisterous. This time, however there was ample elbow room and opportunity for intimate, healthy banter with the waitress who we adored like a step sister in college. She divulged some interesting plans for the spring/summer which involved the transformation of an adjacent double-lot into a lush garden with outdoor dining terrace, all sandwiched between two existing murals. That would be utterly amazing!! ...although this business is an oasis in the desert of a struggling Spring Garden row. It mirrors the monstrous pasta facility (note, there are no murals in society hill or rittenhouse). I'm sure they would figure out a way to make it work! It is definitely a destination type of place and when it picks up some momentum it will be an asset to the area. It already is, no doubt. I do believe the prices are a bit much and as a result I reserve this restaurant for special occasions. text: Pretty shabby for a place that aspires to "upscale." On the plus side, the bathroom was wonderful -- I had an "upgraded, 2 queen beds" room, although when I saw my colleague's regular 2 queen bed room, I was less impressed with my "upgraded" room. I will also say, the staff was very professional, and the view from my room (12th floor) and location were very good. Now, the facilities... Since the hotel was fully booked due to a conference in town, they could not change my room. The TV volume was fixed and could not be changed from its way-too-loud setting -- so the TV was essentially unusable. The bedspreads were stained and dirty looking, and the sheets were equally bad. The hotel changed the sheets for me, but the new set was no better. One of the pillowcases actually had what looked like a cigarette burn hole in it -- why would the housekeeper even use that one? There was half a bag of opened M&Ms left on the desk in the room in plain view, an indication that the housekeeper wasn't paying much attention. The carpet in the room looked dirty. The pool and fitness center are essentially a children's play area -- I realize there's nothing the hotel can do about that, but if you're a business traveler like me and really rely on using those facilities, you're going to be disappointed. This was true on both weekends and weekdays. "Family friendly" in this case means not adult friendly. The internet access was both horribly slow AND expensive ($12.95/day) -- not a good combination. There were two gaping holes in the wall where large light fixtures had been replaced with smaller ones and the hotel did not bother to patch or fill in the extra space -- obviously not critical, but yet another indication that things are not kept up. One more thing -- the on-site restaurant is too expensive for regular dining. As a business traveler, I just want a basic, moderately-priced restaurant that's within my expense limits, but Loews is explicitly trying to make this a "destination restaurant" (which makes no sense since New Orleans already has tons of great restaurants with which a hotel can not compete). I would never stay here again -- too much deferred maintenance and icky bed linens. The price-to-value ratio is off, and nasty linens are a deal-killer for me, regardless of price. PS: I almost forgot -- how could I forget? -- the prominently placed Gideon Bible. While I appreciate the retro factor, I don't think it's there for camp value. It's not even hidden in a drawer. Nope, sitting right out there in plain view. The Unitarian in me finds it offensive that a hotel is trying to convert me to its owners' religion. Tacky!

text: Cool place. I'm torn between giving it 3 stars and 4 stars - so I'll err on the positive! Aesthetically it's an interesting looking restaurant and the bar looked awesome. I love the old black/white photos of hollywood folks on the walls. Food was great...however, I do agree that service was not really up to par. Very friendly staff (our waiter was so nice!), but not really a seamless experience. First, it took our waiter forever to get our order, and then things like bread and water took even longer (I shouldn't even be thinking about these things with a $300 tab for 2 right?) I could overlook the above - we weren't in a hurry and we were having a nice time, but when the bottle of wine we ordered was corked, and they wouldn't open another one because they only had a few bottles left....I just thought that was such poor form. Granted we could have pressed harder to get the bottle, but whatever, I'll try something new and not make a big fuss. Here's what happened with the wine: We ordered the Foxen SeaSmoke Pinot Noir (98pts parker -or something like that - super low production and I don't think it ever made it to retail shelves)...when the bottle arrived we discovered it was corked! This is the first time I've gotten a corked bottle in a restaurant and of all the wines for this to happen with - we were kind of bummed. Myhusband said it was cosmic forces punishing him for being a wine rating whore! :-) So our waiter called over the maitre d' and he suggested it might just need to open up. We wanted to be good sports, so sure, let's decant and give it whirl. But no luck. He mentioned the bottle might be off because they just moved their last 6 bottles from the cellar up into the restaurant (hmmm, a 5-10 degree temp change isn't going to make wine smell like cardboard). He suggested the Hitching Post Highliner (ugh! no thanks - no touristy Sideways wines for me). We said we'd like another bottle of the Foxen and he didn't say anything and then suggested a Cab from Napa we'd never tried. Bottom line, wine is wine, and we weren't about to get into a showdown over a bottle - but I really think it showed poor form on part of the maitre d' and the restaurant. Don't tell me you have additional bottles of the wine and then deny me a replacement bottle. My take is that whatever you're serving on your restaurant list (food, wine, etc) -if it happens to come out flawed or damaged, you should be ready to replace it no questions asked. Ugh! just reliving that kind of re-irks me....I think I may have to lower my rating to 2 stars. And unfortunately I don't know if I'll revisit next time I'm in the area. The place was really full on a Wednesday night, so obviously they're doing something right. I'm just bummed that our wine issue was handled so poorly. (Apparently Oprah dines here, so maybe they're saving the Foxen for her?) Oh, and yes, wine list in general - good, but could benefit from some expansion. They had some killer Bordeaux (a little on the pricey side) but really great houses and vintages, Burgundy was quite nice as well - they even had a Richebourg. I just feel that the California offerings could have been beefed up a little bit, just to offer a little more variety. But what they did have from California was a really nice broad offering.

text: Oh my effin' eff, seriously. Before coming to Chutney Company, I hadn't had a wada in FIVE WHOLE YEARS. I was so excited when I walked into this place and looked at the menu that, no joke, I ordered the wada appetizer, samosa appetizer (both to split with my husband), and idli appetizer with sambar. My hubby also got a chutney wrap (we didn't realize that the chutney wraps are American-style). Everything was really good. I actually don't think I've ever had idli/sambar at a restaurant before and I was shocked that it was under $5. Even though the idli/sambar is considered an appetizer and side, it was actually the size of a whole meal, with three medium-sized idlis and a cup of sambar. I wish we'd tried the dosa as well, but that'll happen next time. The wada appetizer was also three wadas. I'm surprised that Katherine got three of those huge samosas when she ordered the appetizer. We ordered the same one and only got two (super huge and super filling). It's possible though that they're still revising the menu... I know they are planning on doing delivery in a few weeks as well. Anyway, now that I'm done with all that scatterbrained excitement, here are my basic feelings and rationale for the four stars: 1. availability of idli, sambar, wada, dosa 2. price, quickness of service, friendliness of staff 3. ambiance -- it's cute and clean; big windows; lots of color on the walls/floor/furniture 4. general tastiness and freshness of food I took away a star because I felt like somethings could have tasted a little better. A big one for me is the chutneys. Many reviewers say that the chutneys are excellent; we got the cilantro, coconut, and mango chutneys and all were decent but not incredible. I was especially disappointed by the coconut chutney, which was excessively watery. I could be slightly biased because my mom's chutney is out of this world... either way, I can't wait to go back!

The rolls were poorly formed, rice was mushy vice sticky and somewhat firm, the "filling" was grainy and bland. I understand Indiana is landlocked so I'm trying not to be overly critical but the sushi was gross. Rainbow roll didn't even have the avocado-topped pieces I'm accustomed to. Frankly the sushi seemed nothing more than a biscuit to sop up soy and wasabi. What a shame. The steak wasabi tasted like rice-a-roni seasoning and the "steak" was cheap chop steak not worthy of the $15 price tag. Stringy and chewy meat, generically seasoned pasta, underwhelming sauces. Dissatisfying. I will also warn you I got a little "digestive fluidity" once got home, and I normally eat quite a but of sushi, so I'm sure it's not just me getting an upset stomach. It's not food poisoning but something in the sushi did not agree with me. On a final note, the service is atrocious, especially for the price tag. Then again, it is behind an abandoned KrispyKreme, so ... There you go. Don't waste your time or money if you have even a marginally discerning Asian pallette.

text: This place SUCKS. Let me tell you why. 1. Me and Andy came tonight. It's their last week. It was crowded, but that was understandable -- it's their last week, after all! 2. I ordered it cooked MEDIUM, with a fried egg on top, as well as bacon and pepperjack cheese. The waiter warned me that their version of 'medium' was a little pinker than most other places. I secretly get a little happy inside, because HEY, maybe a restaurant will cook my burger RIGHT for once! We place our orders and wait. And wait. And wait some more. Two tables are seated after us. They order their appetizer and burgers. They eat their appetizer and burgers. We still wait. No food. Finally, I call the waiter over and politely ask him what the FUCK is going on with our order. He tries (fails) to placate me, and simply says our order is on the way. Andy suggests just paying for our drinks and leaving. I'm still holding out hope that the burger will be worth it and want to stay. Finally, about 90 minutes after we sit down, we get our burgers. I bite into it. The ciabatta bun is HARD. The burger is, too. Where's my medium cooked burger? This is well-done. It's dry and hard. Ugh. This sad excuse for a restaurant didn't have any barbecue sauce, so it was just me and this sad, dry burger. I was starving, and I managed to choke down half of it before I decided that it wasn't worth the calories. I can't remember the last time I had service this bad at a restaurant. Listen, I understand that you're busy, and I don't mind waiting for my food. But when TWO tables come in after us and order the exact same thing and get their food BEFORE us? text: I went on this tour a few years back and I hope it has changed since I experienced it. I don't share the mostly bubbly assessments of the plantation and tour, and found nothing "quaint and romantic" about it. I was turned off by the cover up and/or diminishing of the sad "other" story. The tour and preservation efforts focused almost completely on the wealthy owners of the mansion. The slaves were a footnote. Yet it was the blood, toil and misery of the slaves that allowed the grand lifestyle of these spoiled confederate slave owners. Let's not forget, slavery was an evil institution. The historic presentation at Belle Meade should focus more on the plight of these enslaved people. Ask yourselves, weren't their lives at least as important as their blood sucking slave owners? Then why is their contribution minimized? At least when I took the tour, there was no presentation of slave quarters, no attempt to show how slaves lived and how integral their lives were to the running of the facilities. Merely halfhearted, cursory comments in passing of what slaves contributed. And no mention of how miserable their lives were, no attempt to balance the story by telling how these people were bought and sold, whipped and punished, how heroic their efforts to escape upon pain of death. One african american was singled out because of his contributions to maintaining the race horses, but the "less valuable" fieldhands and less skilled workers were hardly mentioned. My several questions regarding the lives of the slaves were largely unanswered. In light of the way the slaves on the plantation continue to be suppressed and treated as lesser beings by the superficial treatment given them at the Belle Meade Plantation, I found the tour completely creepy and depressing. The BMP does too little to educate about this equally important aspect of the BMP and southern life. The romanticizing of the south during slavery a la "gone with the wind" continues to this day, as evidenced by the BMP presentation. Where are the slave quarters? Why are they not maintained and shown in detail? How many of the tour guides are african american? Until they do more to honor the contribution and memory of these enslaved people and come clean with the plantation owner's complicity in furthering this evil institution, I cannot recommend this tour.

text: Seriously over-hyped! Perhaps I should give Zahav 3 stars, but with the overly-complementary buzz the place gets, 2 stars will perhaps offset things better. I get that the concept is Middle Eastern/Israeli tapas, a evening of small plates. Ok fine. I love tapas. I have no problem with small portions that allow you a wider taste of the menu, indeed I love the approach. And although a happy omnivore, I dig the vegan-friendly menu. Tasty? Overall, yes. Although one dish, essentially a chicken-paste egg roll ala Tel Aviv, was probably the most distasteful thing I've been served in a long, long time. Overall was the food mind-blowing? Not in the least. Here's my main problem with Zahav. Value. We (a party of 4) ordered (amongst other things) the large Salatim, a daily selection of eight salads, at something like $40. It came on a overly-grand multi-tiered, multi-armed serving pedestal reminiscent of my mother's amateurish holiday crudîtes. Each arm carried a small (and I do mean small) dish containing a small salad. Were there some marvelous proteins incorporated into these salads? No. Each was composed of perhaps 25 cents worth of spiced, shredded vegetable (think cucumber, eggplant, carrot, etc.) There was only enough of each salad for each of us (4) to have a small forkful, no more. The same was true for many of the other plates we ordered (some 12+ in total) One tasty cauliflower dish, at $9, had six small florets, artfully displayed on the plate-to be sure. The server made a huge production of inquiring if we desired more pita bread, then brought one pita for the four of us! While the atmosphere is nice, Zahav is incredibly loud. The patrons, bar traffic and semi-open kitchen combined to create a draining din. The servers (several and ever-changing) seemed largely disinterested. Again, I might have given Zahav 3 stars, but felt 2 stars offsets the overzealous 5 stars that people seem to give this place.

Our waiter was very knowledgeable about the beer selection and was able to give me some good recommendations. In addition to the beers available on tap, there were dozens(must have been close to 100, maybe more) of bottled beers available; pretty much anything you could ask for they have. The beer wasn't too expensive. Expect to pay between five and seven dollars per beer, but you definitely get what you pay for. If you're looking for two dollar Miller Lights(e.g.) go elsewhere. I had a good time at Eulogy and I'd recommend it. If you enjoy Belgian beer you absolutely must give it a try.

Time check of 10:12. We wait, see other people leave, wait, see more people leave and wait some more. Finally at 10:47 Stephanie B goes up to the valet stand and inquires how much long it will be and informs them we've been waiting 35 minutes. Some guy who looks like he's a manager can't believe we've been waiting that long and tells them to get our car right now. Problem solved, or so we think. It's 11 now and still no car in sight, at least 2 other couples who showed up after us have already left. Stephanie B again goes up to the valet stand and low and behold our keys are still at the stand. This is where I pull out my popcorn and watch. By now we've been waiting a little more than 45 minutes and the valet who is passing keys out to the runners tries to give someone else's keys to one of the runners. Stephanie B is having none of this and using her powers of persuasion, leaves the stand having petrified two valets but at least one of them is running away with our keys. Then more minutes pass by and Stephanie B is about to go medieval on their a$$es. She has another conversation with the guy who appears to be a manager in which she is told that the 1st time she came up was the first time they had seen our valet ticket. She promptly corrects him and informs him a short, middle aged guy, took our ticket 55 minutes ago and said it would be right out. The manager told her this was not their protocol on how they do things, which is all fine and dandy, but we've been waiting 55 minutes, just bring the dang car already. She was kind enough to point out to the manager the man who took out ticket initially and was the cause of our extremely long wait. I would like to think he got a stern lecture or something, but I doubt that happened. Another couple we had been sharing our waiting woes with car arrives before ours and the poor guy seemed genuinely sorry that their car arrived before ours. Luckily as they were getting in their car ours showed up. I believe it was 11:15. I will say this, if I ever attend another event where Midwest Valet is providing valet services, I will gladly park my own car and walk 10 blocks just so I don't give these jokers my car keys again. To say I was underwhelmed by their service would be the understatement of the year. I know at least 3 or 4 other people waited at least 30+ minutes for their vehicle last night so we were not a totally isolated incident. If you do decide to use these clowns, make sure you stay on top of them from the start, otherwise you could end up waiting an hour for your vehicle.

text: The first time I ever came to New Orleans- in order to find living accommodations, and quick!- I stayed at the Park View Guest House. I can't believe that I haven't thought to write a shining new review of it since then! This charming place overlooks Audubon Park and sits on the corner very regally. It is just beautiful, inside and out. As you walk in you are welcomed into a lovely sitting area with locally written books all about New Orleans. The smell of chocolate chip cookies baking will draw you back to the dining room. Each table has a beautiful flower and is elegantly set. Breakfast in the morning includes almost anything you could ever want- including different types of juices, different types of coffees, a waffle machine, fresh fruit, fresh breads, etc. Every afternoon one of Park View's workers makes freshly baked cookies and there is wine, tea, etc. laid out for an afternoon snack. The rooms were gorgeous! Our bed was huge and comfortable. The decorating was impeccable- my own Grammy would've approved. I felt so lucky to have stayed here for my first time to the city! What really made a difference, to me, was the spirit of the staff and the owners. We stopped the staff every day to talk about where to look for an apartment, if they had heard of anyone looking to rent a place, and for suggestions for restaurants. The owner of the Park View actually called a few of her own personal contacts, gave me her personal number, and took time out of her schedule every day to check-in and see how we are doing. That is customer service. They really take care of you here. I would suggest that anyone visiting the Crescent City stay here and enjoy themselves. Let the warm and welcoming attitude of the staff and the luxurious accommodations help you enjoy your stay in New Orleans.

text: On a raw bar kick lately and trying out a number of places in Philly. Tried Snockey's last week on Thurs. with my uncle and cousin. We were there for 2 things - raw oysters and beer. Gruff service and the decor didn't phase us. I would be happy eating raw oysters & drinking beer sitting on a milk carton as a seat. This place though was a major disappointment. Oysters were simply gritty and not fresh. Asked the server when they had their oysters delivered and he said 'this morning.' It was either a blatant lie or whoever inspects their deliveries before signing off from the seafood purveyor is incompetent. It is pretty easy to tell you got bad oysters & refuse receipt of an inferior product. Yeah, they will be some harsh words but it is part of the restaurant business. My bet is that the oysters were delivered sometime earlier that week and they improperly stored them in plastic/water in their walk-in. What irked me though was that they were so gritty. Out of the dozen oysters I got, 7 were notably gritty. Even if you get shellfish which aren't the freshest or have been around for a few days, any seafood place should adequately clean them. Yeah you sometimes have to really scrub and spend a fair amount of time cleaning shellfish to get the grit out of them. Hell might take you to scrub them 3x or 4x with clean water to really get them sufficiently cleaned. Did my share when I lived in Boston & worked at a place that had a raw bar. Just takes time and effort. This clearly wasn't done here. The capper though was just how indifferent the manager was when we told him about the oysters. Didn't expect anything like a refund, just an acknowledgment and an apology. Nope. Prices at this place are reasonable for raw oysters. It isn't the $2-$3/oyster at some high-end places for more exotic oysters. Just need to take the time to make sure they clean their oysters thoroughly and get rid of product that has been in the walk-in more than 4-5 days. Hell, just bread those old oysters with a beer batter and fry them up. Even if I lived around this neighborhood, this wouldn't be a place I would come to for the raw bar again. Just to grab a cheap beer at happy hour.

text: Best Greek Food in Reno, methinks! I love Greek food, but it's always so expensive! And finding a Greek place with reasonable hours is very difficult. Enter: Niko's Greek Kitchen. For under $7 per person, you get a full meal with all the trimmings. Niko's gyros are the absolute best. The lamb is shaved off a vertical spit and it's always tender and delicious. The tzatziki sauce is flavorful, creamy and has noticeable chunks of fresh cucumber in it. The produce is fresh and the gyros are made with soft, pillowy flatbread. The dolmades are out of this world. Sprinkled with feta cheese and lightly covered in chopped onions, they are tart and vinegary outside, rich and savoury inside - with a mint-like aftertaste that cleanses the palate. The spanakopita is also delicious. It seems to be made here with the baklava crust. It's definitely worth a try. The only downside to Niko's is the lack of a soda fountain for bottomless refills. He offers some great beer choices and some decent soft drink variety, but the only diet options are water or Pepsi Max in a can. Do yourself a favor. Bring your own drink if you don't want beer. My mom had the Souvlaki and allowed me to sample some. It was tender and delicious and perfectly seasoned, served over a bed of crispy fries. Everything was wonderful, especially the atmosphere. If you like upscale, polished locations, this isn't the place for you. I don't like locations like that. I like very casual, comfortable, airy atmospheres that are unpretentious, not crowded and maintain a feeling of being part of the community you find yourself visiting. Niko's does just that. They're tucked away inside a little pavilion of shops in downtown Reno. Parking wasn't an issue, which was surprising for us. The chairs are lawn/patio style steel furniture which matched the table, but it was all shockingly comfortable. The floor and ceiling are bare and unfinished. It looks more like a warehouse than anything else and the door is kept wide open, so you can freely move in and out to dine in the pavilion or inside the building if you so desire. All the while, you see people going about their daily lives in Reno and, due to the style of the set up, it's easy to feel like you're actually in a small village in Greece. And, of course, Niko and the others who work there are incredibly eager to please. They're very nice and exceedingly helpful. They genuinely care about their restaurant and the satisfaction of their customers. In short, this is one of the very best places to eat Greek Food on the West Coast. Believe me. I've looked.
