text: I travel to New Orleans frequently on business, so I have stayed at almost all the hotels around Canal Street, and this one was my least favorite, for several reasons, the most notable one being that I felt cheated and swindled. Perhaps they got more for their money than I did. My room was not properly air conditioned, and no matter what I seemed to do, I could not get comfortable. The hotel sets a limit on the temperature so that the unit cannot be set below 65 degrees, and when it's over 90 with humidity at night in New Orleans, that simply will not do. If I pay for a room I expect to be at least reasonably comfortable, and I did not sleep well even one night there. Little things began to add up to big irritations. I would put money in the vending machines to buy bottled water and they would spit out Mountain Dew- then after wasting several dollars trying again I would try to order from room service, only to be further disappointed. And questionable fees seemed to follow every single interaction with staff, or any attempt to utilize the facilities I had already paid for. The last straw was when I went to check out and they tried to charge me for using the gym- I had walked in to check it out, and promptly left after being informed they make additional charges EVERY time a guest uses the gym. They tried to charge me for walking in and LOOKING at the facilities. Then they tried to charge me for a series of mini bar items I never consumed that were missing from the fridge since before I checked in. When they put me in the cab to the airport the driver quoted me a flat rate, and then waited until we got to the airport to inform me he had no change. Even a fool could see that the entire operation was less than professional, and lacking a significant amount of integrity. These types of petty scams for nominal hidden or misleading fees are unacceptable. I would not stay at this hotel again, nor would I rec commend it. "Fool me once, shame on you"....it won't happen twice with this hotel.

text: The Hog Pit suffers from either an identity crisis or a complete lack of caring on the part of the staff. They're either a decent bar that serves food, or they're a sub-par restaurant with good drink prices. I gave them the benefit of the doubt and tried going for lunch, dinner and drinks on several different occasions. Not once did everything go right. I'm not expecting everything to amaze me, but I sure would love it if everything were at least adequate. There are a few positives about The Hog Pit, mostly dealing with the bar. The bartenders are nice and they know what they're doing. Drink prices aren't high and the beer is cold. The restaurant side of the house is where things begin to break down. I've never had a good experience with a server here, let alone a great one. They frequently forget drinks, bring out the wrong orders and take too much time to come around to each table. Once, when I asked for some extra sauce, one of the line cooks finally brought out a squeeze bottle. My server was talking at the bar. The food might be good sometimes, but I'm not sure. The main issue I have is that on five out of six attempts to eat here they were out of whatever I wanted. One day it was brisket, the next pulled pork. Time of day doesn't seem to matter either. Sunday afternoon or Thursday night, they're out of multiple items. If you're a BBQ joint, please try to plan ahead. Multiple times over several months is inexcusable. The sauces aren't all that flavorful, and they don't give you much to go with unless you ask for extra. Sadly, the meat doesn't stand on it's own. The sweet potato fries are good, but really could use some sort of dipping sauce. Ketchup just doesn't do it. The barbecue market in Tucson is expanding, and there are now several options. If The Hog Pit wants to thrive as a restaurant rather than a bar they really need to step up their game.

text: It's not as ephemeral as total consciousness, but they're the closest thing to a sports bar in the area, so they've got that going for them. Golf was only one of the many sports playing on the couple dozen high def TVs as I entered the restaurant off the first block of Royal Street. Kitschy signs and of course parrots decorate the walls of the large dining area anchored by a bar near the entrance. A covered patio faces the street. I ordered the steak fajitas, and as no complimentary chips and salsa are offered here, occupied myself with the many games playing above my head. My dish arrived maybe ten minutes later, the steak comprised of a carne asada which I felt was a step above the tough, chewy ribeye meat used at Country Flame around the corner. It was chopped into smallish pieces rather than sliced lengthwise, and arrived on a hot plate atop a large mound of sauteed onions, bell peppers, and mushrooms. All the elements were hot, but they weren't sizzling and steaming like you get at Superior (some others scoff at Superior, but I do enjoy the fajtas there). The sides of chopped iceberg lettuce, diced tomatoes, and crumbled cheese were mediocre. Sour cream and salsa were served in plastic containers. Guacamole did not accompany them. My four flour tortillas were a tad on the dry side, and obviously not made on site (RIP Cucos on Carrollton). The bar offers a small selection of beers for $4 and a dozen or so fruity cocktails for $10. Premade margaritas bubble in a plastic vat on the back wall. The most striking feature to this restaurant is their policy of not offering tap water. Customers are forced to buy bottled water. There's no faster route to earning a "tourist trap" designation in my book than inconveniencing patrons by scheming so obviously towards the bottom line. The food wasn't outrageously bad, but it wasn't good either, and better options for southwestern food exist in the Quarter. If I'm with a group of friends who demand a sports bar atmosphere I could see myself considering the Checkered Parrot, but outside of that scenario I wouldn't go back.

I was in the mood for some French toast, so that's what I ordered. It was good. Also, the coffee was excellent. I'm not sure why, or what it was, but it was perfect. Apparently their sandwiches are their specialty, so my friend had the Dindon, (turkey and Swiss) which looked fresh and delicious, with a somewhat delightfully quirky presentation. That's how I would go about describing the restaurant's overall vibe, though. There's a genuine sort of cute quirkiness in the air here, from the chandeliers (there's lots! And I think they're plastic) to the boulangerie that is nextdoor (they're two separate businesses, but connected inside). There is a nice shaded patio outside where you can have breakfast/brunch like a real cafe, and although we almost sat outside, it was a bit crowded and a few tables hadn't been cleared yet. Inside, if I could suggest a slight upgrade of the furniture, I would like this place even more. The chairs were kind of DMV-waiting-room status with that dark, smooth "wood" that you'd see in bars and lounges in 1986. Weird contrast with the cute chandeliers above. A little bit of love would go a long way with the overall ambiance here and feel less "Tucson strip mall" and more "Parisian cafe". Loved the chalkboard with the soup/wine du jour. Friendly, fast (crazy fast! It was busy and our food came out in minutes) very attentive service is the icing on the cake. I'll be back.

We decided to just split a bunch of appetizers and we each had soup. First let me just say the soup was awesome. They have several options each day and the day I was there there was a potato soup, a Thai sweet potato & peanut soup, and gazpacho. The potato soup was creamy and was listed as dairy-free. I had to order it because 1. I love potato soup and 2. I am really not supposed to eat dairy so I felt less guilty ordering that. Well, it was delicious. It was so creamy, you'd never know it was non-dairy. The waitress said it was made creamy with coconut milk. Yum. My friends had the sweet potato & peanut soup and they both loved it. For appetizers/meals we ordered the hummus platter (OK, but not really my thing), the blue corn & asparagus tacos (really good), and the goat cheese nachos (heavenly). Yeah, I know, I'm supposed to stay away from dairy but once I tasted the nachos, I had trouble stopping. Oh, and meat lovers, you really don't miss the meat, I promise (at least I did not)!

text: It seems like some of the reviewers had a bad time at this place. I gotta say I thought this place was freakin' awesome. I was here for a wedding in May and I feel like it was a great choice by the couple. The architecture is classically Floridian. It's beautifully done. St. Petersburg has really come along in the past 15 years. The surrounding area is a gorgeously wealthy neighborhood but with enough grit nearby to make anyone feel comfortable. The staff couldn't be more supplicant. I felt like some of these people thought I was going to shoot them in the face with battery acid if they didn't call me sir twenty times in every sentence. The one serious complaint I had with this place is the fee for the golf course. A round of golf - $150. They gave us a discount and let us play for $120. I felt that it was very nice of them to only charge us 3 times what playing on their course was worth. The course was deathly brown in many areas. Too many for $120. The greens were infected with some kind of virulent grass eating fungus. On about 6 greens I had to move my ball so I could put on grass. Unfortunately, even if this course was in pristine shape it would still be a $40 round at best in Florida's very competitive golf market. Didn't try out the restaurant and only had an hour of time in the bar. Additionally I wasn't there for a vacation. However, If you are looking for a place in the St. Pete / Tampa Bay Area give this place a serious look.

text: Worst Chinese food I have EVER had anywhere! As my opening statement said, it was by far the worst chinese any of us had ever had. For our meals we had a Beef and Broccoli, Kung Pao Chicken, Sweet & Sour Pork and two other dishes which no escape me. When calling in the order the waiter told my GF "oh, you do not want that one, that is no good, its not like what you would expect" about some dish (sorry, dont remember which one). Looking inside we could see table settings where guests had dined and the food was still sitting for what appeared to be sometime later, could see into the kitchen for what looked to be a complete mess (and not so appetizing). You typically know it is a bad sign if there are no other guests there at all while you are there / waiting. While we waited for the 20 minutes for our dinners to finish we saw no other customers inside at that time nor any cars pulling in / out. Once we got the dinner home we served dinner family style so everyone could try everything. Needless to say each one of the dishes seemed to get worse than the previous. I will say the only good thing of the entire meal it seemed was the fortune cookies. They were quite good ... I can only suspect that to be the case because they order them in instead of making them. After it was all said and done and we tossed all the left overs and trashed their menu ... we vowed to never return to this place. I do not know how they can continue to make it.

text: Deano's saved my life, and in a most delicious way. I've heard enough childhood stories of growing up with Deano's, and suspect there is a slight bias because we like to go with what we know. But this weekend was my first time eating there and I loved it. The pizza parlor atmosphere had a great vibe - a little dark and gritty, like a local hangout spot should be. Lots of families and lots of friends there to kick back, share a pint and eat some pizza. There's a line of arcade games including the elusive Pile-Up game that had a couple families glued to it. It's worth playing, btw, because I've won an iPod Shuffle from a similar game at another arcade in town. ;) There are long tables and benches to eat at, great for groups. Just extend out along the table for as far as you need to. Anyway, the pizza. I loved it! The crust was not too thick, and not wafer thin. Just the right amount for me for a little bit of chewiness on top, and a crisp crunch on the bottom. The sauce had some zip to it, the toppings were ample. We got pepperoni and mushroom. The mushrooms were finely diced and ensured even distribution on the pizza. And what I loved most was the small slices. Their large - which some might consider medium-sized at other parlors or warehouse shopping pizzas - had probably 20 slices. I really hate it when the slices are so thick that you eat way too much, or the pizza's gone in a flash. With the small pieces I can easily eat the amount that fills me up. Ate there Friday, after a serious round of hot tubbing that left my friends and I famished, and we needed food and beer to recharge for events later that night. I thought about eating more Saturday night. I'm sure I'll think about it tonight, too.

The inside is really pretty sad, even for your gritty dive bar style that I happen to love. They use barstools. Maybe if it was just a bar without a dance floor and stage, this would be acceptable but goddamn, you got a decent dance floor and you use stools. And not that many. Would it really be that big of a deal to make some benches that stick out from the wall, I mean, I think Ybor could use bars with more than just stools. The music. What makes those DJs think that they can get away with playing indie hits from 2000? The fact that drunk people still will dance to it, that's what. And it angers me because a good DJ would be passionate about their music to keep it updated, and serve to the more alternative crowd that keeps at least a pinky on the pulse of the music community. They don't even mix it, literally could have plugged an ipod into the PA and no one would have noticed. I wish a place like the Orpheum would try just a little harder because I would hate to think that Miami is the only place in Florida that steals the spot light for nightlife entertainment.

text: I was visiting St.Louis to see in-laws and was taken here for the first time. It was the day after Christmas, a Friday, and I think everyone's internal calendars were off due to the holidays and it being a long weekend. When we called at 1:15 in the afternoon to make a reservation for 6 we were told reservations were not taken for Saturdays. No one on either end of the phone caught that it was actually Friday. We got to the restaurant just before 5:00 pm and my mother and sister-in-law, who was on crutches from recent knee surgery, went in first and were told to stand and wait by the hostess. When the rest of us arrived we were told by the manager the best table we could get would be one for 4 with a seat at the end to accommodate the 5th (one of our party had dropped after we could not get reservations) since all of the bigger tables were being held for people that had called and gotten reservations. My in-laws pointed out that we had called and were told reservations were not being taken. The manager responded that we were told that because we only had 5 people. We then explained we did have 6 at that time and were still told reservations were not being taken. She then responded that she was not the one we had talked to so she could not account for why we were told that. She led us to the table in a room where maybe half of the tables were occupied and my father-in-law again stated we had called ahead for reservations. The manager responded that it was not anything she could explain since she had not been the one on the phone and it was his choice to stay if he wanted to. The exchange got heated. My father-in-law did not want to go elsewhere so we stayed, A hostess came in a moment later to give us menus and literally threw the last one on the table, knocking off a place setting of silverware in the process. Both sides could have handled this better but I really do expect more in terms of customer service from a restaurant manager. At no point was an apology spoken for the mix-up over the phone or was an offer of an accommodation of any kind made; I think even a free appetizer could have diffused the situation. Bottom line, a customer was upset and instead of trying to sympathize and solve the manager chose to argue and set the example to her staff to treat paying customers with indifference at best. The food was fine, large portions and nothing exceptional either way in terms of taste. Chicken Antonio nice for those watching fat and calories and the Chicken Marsala had green peppers in it which was unusual. While the house salad dressing is tasty and popular enough to be sold by the bottle getting a salad (mostly iceberg lettuce) literally swimming in it was overwhelming; ask for it on the side to really appreciate it.

text: We had Mother's Day brunch here, $85 per person. (On Mother's day, brunch is served all day, we had a reservation for dinnertime.) Three stars for the food , minus 1 star for the service. The good part: they had a lot of high-end dishes using a lot of expensive ingredients (lobster, caviar, etc.) So why such a low rating? After having the brunch buffet here, I became convinced that high-end food can't be served buffet style. There were dishes that I could tell would have been good had they been cooked to order and not sitting out. It's really disappointing to have overcooked pasta or a cold escargot tart. And remember, for $85 / person, you can have a tasting menu at many restaurants where food is cooked to order for you. Another thing we discovered was that there was too much to try and too much going on. We got lots of little tastings of everything , but never had time to savor it. Before our mouth could savor an item, we had switched to another. Having a prix-fixe meal of 5-6 courses is much better -- sure you don't get to try as much variety, but then you really get to savor the different flavors and textures that the chef is aiming for in a dish. You let a dish grow on you and understand the nuance of a dish. Instead this buffet brunch is like taking the top 40 pop songs and taking a sentence from each stanza and just playing them right after the other. It's a mad slapdash of really good things - but you don't really have time to savor and enjoy. Service: OK, this can't be too hard considering it's a buffet service. Yet our service was not good. We ordered sparkling water and had to wait a good 10 minutes (after we had already gotten our food). We ordered wine, and it also didn't come promptly. They took away my silverware but didn't replace it. A lot of things we seemed to have to ask for twice -- really, service should be a lot better than that. It wasn't rude or anything, just not top notch. And it seemed like they were really trying to rush us out of there. They kept pushing us to go to the next course. My boyfried and I like to use our expensive dinner dates as a time to talk and catch up on life , but instead it was like "go! speedracer go!'" to the next buffet table with these waiters. So we didn't get a nice elegant romantic dinner, we got a mad dash to try all these buffet tables.

I voiced that we were disappointed, he told me that the chefs get sick of cooking the same thing. Oookay. So we ordered the Quinoa Salad, which was bland, and boring. There was 4 slivers of smoked salmon (I mean the total size of a potatoe chip each) for like 6 bucks added on, but I told the waiter "I dunno, its okay, Im picking at it because its there. I think you are just a victim of your success because we are used to coming here and getting double orders and leaving so impressed" He told me that he just looked at it, as though if it doesnt taste good, at least quinoa is good for you and you're getting your vitamins. Uhm.. I can get my vitamins at home for 1/10th the price. Now there was no Apology, nothing. He took the salad back half eaten because I said we were done. At this point our mood was ruined and had no patience for the college pizza night movie pick. So I left without drinking the last glass of wine in my flight. Paid my SEVENTY dollar bill (not one item removed) left a 10% tip because I almost felt that they were judging me when I made complaints. Its not like I went in there in sweat pants, I went in there wearing a $500 jacket, boss clothes, clean shoes, well done hair, and my girlfriend was the most elegantly dressed woman in the room. My bills are almost ALWAYS $200 and will be very unlikely to even go anymore. Looking for another wine bar now, on Yelp.
label: NEG

text: After a terrible color experience at another salon, I was in desperate need of color correction. Gerry Hebert really saved the day. He is the quintessential professional. Gerry took me in right away for a consultation. When I arrived at the salon the first time, I was visibly shaken from my bad experience. The receptionist was so sweet, and gave me a free lipgloss to make me feel better. When I went back for my appointment with Gerry, he spent hours with me, patiently working on my hair to get it back to beautiful. This was no easy task, and he never once appeared rushed, annoyed, or tired. He did a wonderful job. I will definitely keep going back. I feel safe in his hands.
label: POS

text: Let me preface this by saying I still like this place. Just that my latest experience left much to be desired. I'm not a cigar connoisseur by any means so don't think I'm some sort of expert in the matter. I'm like your normal casual cigar smoker (events, celebrations, random nights), so I will basically smoke anything, know about 4 brands, and know not to inhale. But yesterday, it just wasn't a good experience on the fact that the cigar they sold me sucked. In the first quarter inch (a panatella size) of smoking, the ash split down the middle. That meant I had to ash quickly, rather than let it sit. Then, halfway through, while actively smoking, the cigar went out. The leaves were flaking off with barely a touch. And the firmness of the cigar was like a well done steak - if it's not what you want, it's not what you want. We brought this up to the host. He was sitting at the bar, enjoying his own cigar. 1. When asked about the ash splitting, he stated that the ash split because it was lit improperly. Ok, that may be the case (I use a match, put the flame to the end while puffing), but I have smoked over 30 cigars using the same exact method and it has NEVER split. I've always had my ash last at least halfway down. 2. When asked about the flaking leaves, he stated that since it was a single leaf wrapper, the glue may have come undone and thus flaked off. He also stated that the band should be left on (I was playing with the band after it had gone out and it came off. I leave it on until it's about to burn). 3. I wish I asked about why the cigar just went out. I did not. I have had cigars which were still burning 15 minutes after I stopped smoking them. Again, this went off while I was smoking. Also, did not ask about the firmness. It was about as firm as if you touched your thumb to your pinky, the flesh underneath the thumb. That's how firm it was. 4. Finally, he stated if they had something to compare it with, he could see. We didn't feel like dragging it out anymore, but my other friend with us had the exact same cigar (Ashton VSG) and it was fine. I didn't really care about the money spent. I did not appreciate him making me feel like a jackass, thinking I was a retard. I hate that air of superiority specialized people feel when they know a product more than most others, and when there are a lot of "rookies" doing it. It was a $19 cigar, and for that, I'd expect it to be what I wanted. If you ordered a steak medium-well, and it came out rare, do you need someone to tell you how to eat a steak? How it should be cooked and eaten? No. You get it the way you want. I don't like my cigars dry, flaking and going out midway. The second star is because I ordered a roast beef sandwich. That thing was good. Really good, even though the waitress looked like she was going to stab me because I wanted a menu after 11pm. After all that, I'll come back. It has a great atmosphere, great vibe, and is very relaxed. One bad experience will not make me dislike this place. I just hope it was a one time thing, and not a recurring theme.
label: NEG

text: My toddler serenaded a grizzly bear. When she stopped singing, the bear woke up, popped his head up and stared at her - "Entertainment and dinner all-in-one." Huge, stunning zoo. The zoo entrance may be free...but that's because you pay up the wazoo for everything once you are inside. Branding and sales opportunities at every corner, but many locals are staunch member supporters. It was hilarious that an entire circle around the zoo on the mini train only passed by one or two actual animal habitats. The insect area is quite amazing. Imagine every zoo and critter exhibit you have ever been to on one property. Part of the American Zoological and Aquarium society, so get a membership to a partner zoo to take advantage of member benefits. There are also packages to cover the main attractions.
label: POS

text: I am a fan of the Gap outlet store! I shop here often for shirts and I always find a great deal. Yes, the clothes are on the plainer side, but that is Gap style, and I like it. I went in here today in search of some tank tops and ended up finding two: one on sale for $7.99 and the other one, not on sale, for $24.99. She spent the entire time talking to her friend. This kind of annoyed me. Gap outlet is awesome though, because you will always get a good deal here!

I love med food and will prob not be going back here. The only reason I would is convenience from Vandy. text: So at my last haircut I got wind from Joe that he's planning an over-the-top rehab of the space commencing in late summer 2010. Given Joe's impeccable design sensibility, I know it will be superfly. So...I'm reinstating that last star. Vive le Groom!

text: Seems like they've done some redecorating since these pictures were posted, but a wonderful little tea room! I'm going to try their chai next time - this looked good being scooped from the pot! Otherwise, a nice little place to have a cup of tea. Their baked goods also looked good. We shared a chocolate cherry scone, which was ok but not phenomenal (I'm particular about baked goods).

text: Five stars for the food, three stars for the mixers. We actually chose this place because the mixers looked so good, so we grabbed a small bottle of Patron and headed in... The mixers were decent, but nothing special. The food, however, was incredible. We split the beet salad which was good, but nothing that stood out too much against other creative beet salads. I ordered a hazelnut crusted duck dish with a cranberry sauce on a bed of plantains (delicious), she had the braised short-rib (equally delicious). Both dishes were some of the best prepared, and absolutely mouth-watering combinations of flavors I had had in a while. Despite barely making it halfway through my plate and still feeling like I was going to roll out of the restaurant, we split the bread pudding desert (rather, each had a bite and took it home). Amazing. Great atmosphere, a little crowded so you have to be open to eating right next to other groups (which can be amusing, we had some pretty funny people - one very awkward first date, one hilarious couple - I can only imagine what was being said about us...). Definitely worth a shot, we might have had a bad night for the cocktails. But if you're going somewhere for the cocktails, try a bar. Go here for the incredible food.
label: POS

text: I really dug this place when we went. The steak was cooked to perfection, the baked potatoes were awesome (hard to mess those up though), and the wine list was extensive. The servers were very knowledgeable about the menu and wine selection. Overall I thought it was great, if maybe a little pricey (for Boise). If this place were in San Francisco, the prices would be a steal! But 4 stars means I'll be back again if I'm in Boise and craving some red meat.

text: This is another chain paper owned by an out-of-state company and therefore local coverage leaves a lot to be desired. The online edition consistently has a lot of errors (wrong locations, names, etc.) The Star I grew up with (and even shortly after it was sold about 9 years ago) was staffed mainly by native locals who worked there for 20-30 or more years. Now a days a lot of its employees are, so to speak, using our city as a stopoff from Little Rock to Chicago. The state high school basketball finals this year, played in Indy granted had no local teams, but this paper's editors chose to place stories on page 9 of the sports section. Lame. And if you're not a big-league pro or college sports team, don't expect to see a Star reporter covering a game after opening night. But at least as a quick-pay subscriber I got two free tickets to the Indy 500 pole day.

text: Maybe when they changed locations they lost their cooking abilities. I don't know, but eating here made me switch to eating for survival instead of for pleasure. We ordered the ortega skillet which, with green chilies and Spanish sausage, should have been quite flavorful. Instead, we got a skillet of bland potatoes and overcooked green peppers. They did give us hot sauce with our food - so with a lot of that and a significant amount of salt, it was tolerable. It is engrained in us to finish our food, but in this case we just couldn't do it, despite having paid $10 for a dollar's worth of ingredients. (the portions are huge though) The biscuits and gravy were ok, but sadly the highlight of our meal was the sourdough toast with butter. That was delicious. So, one star for toast!
label: NEG

text: I used to enjoy staying at Eldorado Hotel but my last experience here may very well be my last experience here. Mom and I stayed here instead of our usual Holiday Inn since we made this trip sans felines. I was impressed with the security detail (must show your room key to go up the elevators). I was a whole lot less impressed with the rest of my experience however. It's not busy when you stay midweek and they had plenty of vacancies. I actually don't remember much about the room itself, except for the awful experience I had in it. I know it was nicer than the rooms at the Holiday Inn, but not that nice. I do enjoy the buffet at this casino and that I will review separately. So, after eating and gambling for the evening it's time to turn in. I don't sleep well in the best of circumstances and I am often up several times a night to use the bathroom. On this particular evening I had more than one reason for that middle of the night need. Imagine my utter surprise and dismay to get up and discover that all of the water had been turned off in the middle of the night! What??? Can't flush the toilet. Oh terrific. Can't wash my hands? Just great! Can't clean up things that needed cleaning up - no, not priceless. Horrible! I called the front desk. They acknowledged that the water had been turned off in several of the rooms in my area for some weird maintenance reason, and said that I should've been told upon check-in. Well, I wasn't. They offered to come up and give me a key to a room several doors down the hall if I wanted to go in there and use that bathroom. Are you kidding me??!!! Um, no! Not walking down the hall in my nighties to use some other bathroom. Why wasn't I booked into that room in the first place if it was available?? The whole experience left a really bad impression on me. When I checked out, I had intended to ask for compensation and was hoping they would half price my room or something. They had already logged my middle of the night call and did immediately offer up compensation without my asking. One star for that. And one more star for comping my room; so no charge. I later received a coupon in the mail to come and stay with them again, for free, but I don't know if I'm willing to try this again. I've had a few other bad hotel experiences but this was certainly one of the worst.
label: NEG

text: We loves the Cheeseboard! The setup is a bit quirky and the prices sometimes a little higher than other places, but what you get is simply better. Personally, I like the get-in-line-to-order set up. Gives me a chance to look over the delectables and chat with the staff and other patrons. The food quality is always top-notch and the atmosphere is simply the best. Other Reno lunchaterias are either chains or crowded little holes-in-the-wall. The Cheeseboard has consistently great food served in a European-style bistro setting.

text: Ended up staying at this hotel for 4 nights. It ended up being one of the worst stays at a Starwood Hotel in my experience. The room had a smell of chlorine during the whole stay, with or without the AC on. House keeping was definitely not up to par. If 2 towels were used, they took the used ones and did not put new towels to replaced the used one. They actually did not even both to come clean the room on Sat. Had to call front desk later on that day to request the service. I was also disappointed that there was no internet/wifi service unless you're in the main lobby. For the amount of money paid($190/night), I was also hoping to have a mini fridge in the room - no luck there. My friends that stayed at the Holiday Inn 8 miles down the road had the same size room, a mini fridge, microwave, free wifi and breakfast and for only $90/night. Needless to say, I definitely won't be staying or recommending people to this hotel.

text: Since first reading the reviews on Yelp for this restaurant, I've been itching to go... I've been foiled a few times by their "we close at 9 so you have to be finished with you meal by then" policy. Finally, this weekend, I got my chance! We were definitely NOT disappointed! The food was amazing; far better than the other West Philly options. The dishes were cheap ($11 for the lamb, less that $10 for the veggies) and came with a ton of food. We opted for the lamb dish (which came with a ton of lamb) and the veggie combination plus two other sides, which three of us gorged ourselves on. Our total bill was less than $25 and we were stuffed! The service was nice and certainly faster than most of the Ethiopian places (where I've waited over an hour for food). A friend of mine (who just joined us for coffee) loved the coffee and the biscotti she ordered. All in all, this is just what West Philly needs; a great coffee shop with fair trade coffee alongside an amazing, inexpensive restaurant. Yay!

text: How I long for the days of a $10 cut. And $60 highlights. Sigh. My two most dramatic hair moments involve the Chop Shop....and in good ways. The first time I went to the Chop Shop was after I dyed my hair red. My boyfriend at the time convinced me that deep red was a great color for me....so I gave it a try. And you know what, he was right! It was a great color for me. For three days. Then it faded to this awful orange. I was horrified an immediately tried to get it back to normal but at the time I didn't know you can't go from red to blonde. (silly, silly, girl.) Luckily my hair was salvageable and I have the Chop Shop to thank! Fast forward a year. I go in and see a different stylist who literally chops my hair off. At least 6 inches.....I went from below shoulder length to a bob. Up until that point the thought of short hair like that horrified me.....but it looked SO good. Now, another girl may have had a panic attack right then and there in the chair but I didn't. I'm glad the stylist pushed the envelope and took a chance. But of course it may not work out like that for everyone.

text: I love the Muttart. If you're new to Edmonton and have wondered what those glass pyramids are shining in the river valley, go check it out. Or if you've lived in Edmonton all your life but never made it there, you don't know what you're missing. It's a beautiful oasis in the middle of our city. These giant greenhouses are a beautiful stroll on a winter's day, through temperate, arid and tropical climates. There are all sorts of beautiful plants and eco-systems maintained by city staff and passionate botanists. I love to head over here in February or March when winter is really getting to me. Unfortunately, the Muttart is closed for renovations until the beginning of '09, so check out the website before you go. This is a great place to take kids and out-of-towners. A holiday away from home, right in the centre of your city.
label: POS

text: I really admire and commend the owner of this shop, Jean-Luc Labat.-only open about one week. They are situated across the street (Oracle) from the newest iteration of Beyond Bread, a very well known local bakeshop with quite a reputation. They are different businesses in some ways and similar in others. Frogs offers, like Beyond Bread, bread, pastries, and other baked goods along with breakfast items and then lunch/dinner items such as quiche, eggs, salads, soups. Frog's is "organic" and "French style." I met a friend there for breakfast this morning about 10. I must say that the renovation of the space (used to be Paradise bakery) is very pleasing. The counter/display area is inviting and the offerings beautiful and very tempting. One orders at the register and either takes the food themselves or it is brought to you. Seating is indoors or out. Indoors was very comfortable, spacious, attractive. I asked if the omelets were "French." Unfortunately the very nice young woman who appeared to be overseeing the front did not understand my question at all but it was soon apparent that the omelets served here are prepared in a standard manner. ( in hindsight I am sorry I did not think to take the time to explain the difference to that young woman. It might have been helpful to her). Having not mastered the art of the French omelet myself, I am always on the lookout for any restaurant that serves them up that way. Otherwise, I really dislike them. So, my friend and I ordered 3 pastries between us and each had coffee which was decent but, for my taste, nothing very special. Despite our having our meal "in" the coffee was offered only in paper cups. There were no pitchers of dairy products, i.e. cream, milk to be had. Instead there were only those little, wasteful, and non-organic 1/2 and 1/2 single serves. Maybe they plan to correct this. The pastry: one plain croissant, one puff-pastry "twirl" with raisins, and and a kind of cake/muffin pastry made with blue corn meal and goat cheese. My friend found the latter to be dry and tasteless. I have to say I liked it a lot but it did lack flavor of the cheese. I could only taste the cornmeal. Serving with a pat of butter might have helped-none of our pastries came with butter or jam (which is $1.00 more). The croissant was okay, not notable. The raisin pastry was better, crispier on the outside and very flavorful. No one came by to ask how everything was. As my friend said, "I wouldn't go out of my way to go back." Now, maybe I will go back after the holidays and after the owners have had a chance to work out the kinks. (the cashier did now know how much a coffee refill was, e.g) They are in their infancy. I left my "You've Been Yelped" card and hope they will read the reviews which can only help them to correct some problems. Bon Chance.
label: NEG

text: Going to a Sounds game is a fun way to spend three hours on a delightful spring or summer evening. The team has a multitude of cool promotions throughout the season and none are better than Thirsty Thursdays. I mean where else can you watch a baseball game and get all the $1 beers you want until the 5th inning. Fellow Yelpers see you at the game.

Menu celebrates local produce as well as local chicken, lamb, beef. Chef truly understands how to prepare fish... try the salmon, tuna or swordfish... fabulous! The local vegetables that garnish the plates make the entire experience a perfect evening (and at a reasonable price). BYOB.

text: Hugely disappointed. Locals recommended this place and Yelp seemed to support those recommendations. What? Is there such dearth of breakfast options that this is considered good? So good that there's a wait to get a table? What? No pancakes were ordered by my party so I can't speak to what appears to be this place's specialty. Omelette was brought with very flat/thin eggs (most omelettes have fluffy eggs?) and the home fries were GREASY with no flavor. Okay. I know those potatos are fried and should be greasy but seriously, it was just grease, slightly undercooked (home fries should have some minimal crisp, right?). Service was great though. Friendly, highly efficient, and lots of attention. Even then, I can't seem to get myself to give me more than 1 star.

text: I've been to both locations a couple of times. I was pretty much trying to find something different from the chains. The food here is mediocre at best. The latest time I went the service was horrible. Waited 5 minutes to be seated even though the restaurant was only about 25% full. After being seated for 10 minutes we had yet to see a waiter to at least take our drink order. We ended up walking out. It's unfortunate this establishment isn't better as it could do really well in the sea of cookie cutter restaurants in the in the area.
label: NEG

text: Hudson Beach has seen better days. Not that I was expecting much from this place but it still was a disappointment. In fact, as a lifetime Floridian I was embarrassed by the "Beach". If a tourist came here first and thought this was what Florida's beaches were like they'd leave and never come back!! Let me explain... Most of this park consists of a seawall/cement walkway along the water. There is about a 2-3' drop from the wall to the water. There is no sand here, just lots and lots of nasty rocks. They do have a sandy section of the park. This small area starts with some sand, and then there are lots of piles of dried sea grass which leads to the water and plenty of rocks. Again, the sand leads to the water and nasty rocks. Some of them as big as a football! If you make it to the water (you HAVE to wear shoes or risk cutting your feet) then you will find some sand, some rocks and lots more seaweed. The swimming area is small and borders the canals which lead to the housing development. That means you are swimming right next to where all the boats come in and out. It is kind of smelly here too. And the sand they did have was FULL OF CIGARETTE BUTTS!! My poor son was trying to play in the sand and just about every handful of sand had someone's nasty butt in it. If people are going to use the beach as their personal ash tray then it shows how little respect they have for their local beach! It is just trashy but there was plenty of other trash to keep the butts company: fishing line, wrappers, bags, etc. It wouldn't cost a dime to have some volunteers come out and clean up this small beach. The beach does have some redeeming qualities. Free parking (there is no way they could charge people here!), a couple of small playgrounds, bathrooms, fresh water showers, and a covered pavilion with an observation deck. I'm sure the place has nice sunsets and the adjacent restaurant (Sam's Beach Bar) looked interesting.
label: NEG

text: Order Denied! I attempted to make a delivery order today. When I called I was told to call back in fifteen minutes. That should have warned me off, however, I called back in twenty minutes. When I called back I was told that they were no longer taking orders. I reminded her that she told me to call back in fifteen minutes and her reply was, "actually its been twenty one minutes". She never mentioned their 5 minute ordering window policy. In the end she still refused to take the order. They advertised delivery hours until 9:00pm on this day. The second call was made at 8:40pm. With an insulting display like this no one can honestly say that customer service is of any concern to this business.
label: NEG

text: The remaining stops on your French Quarter Confederacy of Dunces tour are limited, the past decade hasn't been kind...Penny Arcade on Royal Street, Werleins Music, and the Joy theater joined Holmes' on the list of places old Ignatius frequented but now "aint de're no more". We do have, though, a not quite large enough statue of Ignatius available 24/7 for worshiping, hugging or just saying a quick hello to. Standing right under the clock of the old DH Holmes building (now the Chateu Sonesta) where Ignatius waits at the beginning of the book for his momma while "studying the crowd of people for signs of bad taste in dress" he is a reminder of the greatest book of New Orleans fiction ever written. Read the book. Love the man. Visit the statue. Easy. Docking a star because haughtiness level is just not high enough, the artist seemed to put a glimmer of compassion in his face...not sure if Ignatius needs that. Also, I'm sure material for statues is expensive, but he can use 80 pounds of heft also....the man was not a healthy eater. Incidentally, the model for the statue is Spuds McConnell a local, and typically under informed, talk radio DJ from when he was a younger actor and portrayed Ignatius on stage here in town.
label: POS

text: This place has great sandwiches at a decent price. I like that it's a quick lunch with zero hassle. Try the chicken cordon bleu -- the mustard in that sandwich makes the thing so good!
label: POS

text: What a wonderful find! We stopped in here for a drink and to get change for the streetcar - ended up staying for dinner in this fabulous french restaurant. The raws were delicious, the beet salad was yummy, but the shrimp and grits were a work of art. The white cake with apples and creme fraiche was decadent. I tried their absinthe frappe - and though it has a strong licorice flavor, it was fun to sip all evening. We missed the happy hour which was over at 6pm, but during oyster season they offer raws for .25 a piece. They were a buck apiece regular which was the going rate as far as I saw. Will definitely go back here and also look for other restaurants by this owner. Excellent!
label: POS

text: Picasso is a welcome addition to the rapidly gentrifying Media PA scene. My review is based on two different occasions when my BF and I went to eat. We found very good service, good ambiance, excellent food and moderate-to-high price. Although the restaurant was full when we arrived at 7:30 PM, the maitre d' did the impossible to accomodate us and we had a table within 10 minutes. That was admirable. We were also welcomed by an attentive and knowledgeable waiter who obviously was well trained and had experience with their dishes. As we've been there twice, we've had several of their plates. Their smoked salmon salad with Manchego cheese and pears is outstanding. Same for their entree-sized crab cakes, an outstanding feature. And their baked Bass with fennel is delightful. A really good wine selection complemented the meal. The restaurant also serves excellent Espresso to top off the meal. We were very satisfied.
label: POS

text: I tend to do a lot of my mall shopping up at Oxford Valley these days. It's not terribly far from my house, they've got more stuff than Neshaminy, and I can stop by to see my aunt, boyfriend, or friend who live nearby after I've shopped till I dropped. Their food court is decent, and they've got a good amount of stores. They've got a Williams Sonoma, Macy's, JC Penny's, Sears, Boscov's (all the cheaper dept. stores), Banana Republic, Forever 21, Bath & Bodyworks, Delia's, etc., so whomever you're buying stuff for, you can usually find something. They've also got lots of stores nearby - Ulta, Old Navy, Target, DSW, etc. The only thing I don't like is the Sesame Place traffic in the summer. You have to drive past Sesame Place to get to the mall, since SP is in the mall complex, and you inevitably get the super long red light while the stroller patrol takes their good old time crossing. It's seriously like a 5 minute long light. In the winter, though, you don't have to worry about that. This isn't the most unique mall on earth, but I like it. It's a mall in the suburbs, so it is what it is.
label: POS

text: Meaning to try and found a coupon in Clipper mag. text: I thoroughly enjoyed my dinner at Yangming. While most of the dishes are inauthentic, they are prepared very well and the atmosphere is pleasantly upscale. They even agreed to seat the three of us who had showed up and were tired of waiting. Our server was good, if a bit slow to take our orders. It took forever to get the check at the end of the meal, but it was a busy saturday night and we were in no rush. The food itself was very good, even if it was very Americanized. I may have been the only non-Asian whitey at dinner, but I know my Chinese food. My friend ordered one dish off of the chinese language menu, and that one tasted authenic (some sort of spicy chicken, I forget exactly). We sampled beef, chicken, seafood, and crab pad thai from the regular menu and shared amongst the table. The dishes ranged from slightly bland to really tasty. Unfortunately it's been nearly a month since then and I forget what was what. Darn backlog of yelp reviews. It was nice to have a large table to ourselves in a back corner of the restaurant, tucked away. I also enjoyed the classical piano music playing in the restaurant. For bball fans, the Nova/Pitt Elite 8 game was playing in the bar area that night. Exciting, but a bit of a headache trying to get into the city from the restaurant after Nova won and the entire school was rioting in the streets. (Yangming is practically on Villanova's doorstep.) The price wasn't astronomical either. We had tons of food, a few drinks, paid for the birthday girl, and the overall bill including tax and tip came to about $40 a person. Not too shabby. I'd definitely return to Yangming for a special occasion dinner with a group. They handle that sort of thing well.

text: This story all started when I unexpectedly got the afternoon off from work on a beautiful day. What do you do on an occasion such as this? Well I hopped on my bike and rode around the city! He said that there was an excellent shop down on 9th st, Via's. So I rode down and was immediately impressed by all the bikes outside and the free compressed air hookup that anyone can use. I was very quickly greeted by Curtis, the owner of the store (with a killer mustache!). He was busy helping someone else but told me that someone would be right with me. I took a seat on the bench and waited for him to finish up with the bike at hand. I told him the problem I was having and he said he needed to replace the crank arm and would have me out of there in no-time for about $17. I told him that the shop came very highly recommended and you could tell he really took that to heart. He said that he really prides himself on his shop and if "the guys aren't doing the best job for the best price, they're outta here!". He did have me out of there in no time and the bike feels great. I was a little short on the cash (about $5) and he said that when I came back this weekend to get the petals tightened up, I could bring the rest of the money - I really liked that. So go to Via's, tell Curtis he is the man and RIDE ON, PHILADELPHIA, RIDE ON! PS: This shop is CASH ONLY!

Excusing the hostess' inaccurately executed priority queue, the recorded list of waiting patrons revealed a disproportionately high number of 20:30 reservations indicating the possibility that the restaurant may simply have overbooked the reservations. While an inexperienced management team could be excused from having promptly arriving guests with reservations wait for 40 minutes, any such team that was familiar with Valentine's Day booking cannot be. After we were seated, our server failed to give us a wine menu. When he finally fetched it, he did not offer any suggestions on it nor did he even remember to ask us which wines we were interested in. The pork chop and rack of lamb both had a terrific aroma and fairly decent taste. Although the menu misrepresented the Yukon gold potatoes as 'whipped', they were actually au gratin. Regardless, they were tasty. Their vegetables are also salted to perfection with a spritz of dill adding a surprisingly pleasant flavor. In summary, the food is almost worth the price, but the Valentine's Day service is one to avoid. Though it's priced as a fine dining experience, the service is not one where you'll meet a calm and collected hostess with smiles, a waiter who's genuinely interested in serving, and a kitchen that strives for perfection. While one doesn't expect a $40 meal to achieve perfection, one certainly wishes for a good-faith effort.

text: You have not seen a basketball game until you have been to a packed house at Hinkle Fieldhouse. It is simply the finest arena to witness Indiana's Game in action. This is where they used to crown the state champions, this is where the last act of the movie Hoosiers was filmed to recreate what the state championship would be like. And this place is loud. I grew up about four blocks from Hinkle and used to ride my bike all through the adjacent Holcomb Gardens, but every springtime in March, I knew when basketball season was coming down to crunch time. Hinkle Fieldhouse generated sonic booms when the drama enfolded. When I watched the semi-state games on live TV, It seemed like I would hear the crowd reaction from outside the house before the television signal reached my antenna. I've been told on several occasions by people who work for Butler athletics that Butler's opposing teams hate playing here because of the noise when the crowds is going at full tilt. They try to schedule their games during academic breaks so that the crowd noise isn't so great. And now over the past ten plus years Butler Basketball has returned to its old glory and it has become the hottest (and loudest) ticket in town. When you witness a game here, you witness history. Buildings like this are rare and every attempt will be made to make sure this arena survives another 80 years, but if you want to see the action for yourself, make a trip soon. Unfortunately, you never know what could make the last event at a building this old it's final one. PS: I witnessed the greatest game of all time at Hinkle Fieldhouse: Washington vs. Ben Davis. Washington was the westside inner city public high school and was closing after the school year. Ben Davis was the westside suburban township high school to which some kids from the same neighborhood were bussed. And Ben Davis and Washington were ranked #1 and #2 in the state respectively. So the semi-state for this game was the greatest collection of talent in the city of Indianapolis on one court, from one side of town (west), from the same neighborhood (Haughville) playing in an emotional game of winner takes all. These kids grew up together, played AAU ball on the same team, and were in the same youth leagues. Both teams sported the same colors: Purple and White. It was a sea of purple and white and nobody knew which section each school was supposed to be seated. But the famed "Battle of the West Side" still is one of, if not, the best basketball game I ever witnessed. Back and forth drama, heroics on both sides, and a sprinting down the court pull up 35-footer at the buzzer. Game! Unfortunately, Washington's last season came to an end. Washington is now back open after, almost 10 years closed, as a Junior High School.
label: POS

text: Always on the lookout for a good meal at a fair deal, especially when traveling, it never hurts to ask a well-fed looking local. Thus prepared, four hungry travelers rolled into the deep NOLA warehouse 'hood to sample a restaurant recommended by two area hipster types as "my favorite place to eat". With no reservations we could have been immediately seated in the back room. Instead, we asked to wait a few minute's at the bar for a table in the much livelier main dining room. The young n' hunky bartender (hunky per L. and K. the vivacious females in our party) mixed up some excellently classic cocktails while we waited. Despite my initial skepticism, the guy turned out to be one of the better bartenders I've been served by. Soon seated, we found ourselves more excited by the intricate appetizers than the more vanilla-sounding entrees. The starters were so tantalizing in description that we ordered eight (of nine, less the charcuterie plate) and skipped the entrees entirely. It turned out to be a meal not to regret. However - I would caution others NOT to repeat our folly. The starters, especially the crab and asparagus gratin dish, were a delight, but so rich that none of us could face dessert. In a nod to the staff, halfway thru our our meal the building power went out, darkening the whole neighborhood. Candles were quickly it, and glasses refilled. After fifteen minutes the lights came back on. We discovered later that the maitre'd had negotiated a reprieve (possibly involving a little lagniappe?) with a nearby utility work crew to provide power until 10 PM (closing time). Our waitress and the kitchen apparently never missed a beat, and our meal service was flawless. All told, our meal at Dick & Jenny's was a little slice of Nawlins heaven. Local food, fair prices, great flavors and service, all in a funky homestyle spot that felt like home.

text: Celebrated NYE 2010 at Cochon with a group of friends. None of us had been there before, but all had heard good things about it. There was a special NYE menu, and I chose: Lobster bisque, Pig's feet trotter & foie gras croquettes, roast suckling pig, and rice pudding. We all received an amuse bouche of chicken liver mousse, which was actually maybe the best part of the meal. Bisque seemed kind of watery/thin but had a nice present lobster flavor - weird twist to the dish was adding some sort of spicy oil which added a kick. Croquettes were overly fried which overwhelmed the foie gras flavor. The suckling pig was probably the most disppointing. The waitress "warned" us that there would be some skin in the dish, to which we all welcomed - what is roast suckling pig without skin? But what we were expecting was not what we got...I hardly had any skin in my portion & the skin that people did get was no where near the crackling, crispy skin that we expected - instead, it was flabby & chewy. Also, the meat itself was dry and didn't seem well seasoned. Earlier the same day, I'd enjoyed a delicious roast pork sandwich at John's Roast Pork which had way more flavor & moistness to the meat. All desserts were way too sweet, so much so that we couldn't finish them all. However, I will say that the service was quite good. It's too bad the meal wasn't more satisfying, but maybe I'm hoping it might have been because of the holiday? I'm not entirely sure whether I'd try it again - am curious to try the regular dinner menu to see if it's any better...

text: I go to New Orleans nearly every year to see the fun and bawdy Krewe du Vieux parade with a group of my friends and I always stay at Lafitte's. It sits in the French Quarter on a quiet stretch of Bourbon street, so it's close to all the excitement, but you're not kept up all night by howling drunkards. Everything in the Quarter is no more than a 10 or 15 minute walk away, so the location can't be beat. The rooms are all different, though all have lovely high ceilings and are tastefully furnished with antiques. Many have either communal and private balconies so you can enjoy the view, but as there's not a lot of foot traffic around the hotel at night, don't expect to be tossing beads down to a rowdy crowd below. Bathrooms tend to be on the small side, but they're functional enough. (Oddly, the last time our toilet seemed to be fed with hot water, so that every time you sat down you were treated to an unintentional butt sauna.) The staff is friendly but non-intrusive. The front desk closes late at night and you're given a passcode to let yourself in the front door, which is locked for security. Rooms come with a complimentary continental breakfast- hot coffee, juice, and some fresh hot biscuits. If you're hung over and can't stumble towards Cafe du Monde right away, this can be a life saver. Lafitte's Blacksmith's Shop (a dim, candlelit bar built into one of the the oldest structures in the Vieux Carré and a tourist stop in its own right) is right next door if you want to grab a cocktail. Sometimes loud conversation from the bar can carry up to some of the lower rooms, but if you're boozed up enough from the evening's festivities, you'll probably not be disturbed. Clover Grill across the street is great for a quick bite to eat in a cute 50's style diner. For the price and location alone, I can't recommend Lafitte Guest House enough for the traveler that wants to stay in the Quarter, but also appreciates a quiet night's sleep.

text: This place has a lot of promise, but I have to say, I was disappointed with my experience last night. My father in law had a restaurant.com gift certificate, so we thought we'd try out this cozy little italian place. The atmosphere is casual enough, but I wouldn't feel comfortable in just a jeans and a tshirt. It was 6:45 on a Thursday, and I'd say maybe half the restaurant was full. It was early, so they should have anticipated a dinner rush. They seemed pretty short staffed, actually, so the bartender, and even the cook came out to refill drinks and take orders. Maybe this was an unusual night for them, but because of this fact, the service was really slow and I'm not sure we had a trained server speak to us once. Shouldn't a restaurant over-staff and then let go employees as the night progresses? The bread was served with a concoction of olive oil, garlic, basil, and some other spices. It was superb, and one of the only saving graces of my review. The other saving grace? The house salad. It was a traditional italian dressing (perfectly tangy) with provel cheese, lettuce, and pimentos. Oh so very tasty!! Not redeeming enough for the restaurant as a whole, though. I got the fettucini alfredo with chicken. First of all, the sauce wasn't spectacular. It was a little thick and somebody over there REALLY loves pepper. It was all over my dish. In fact, my husband had a side of white sauce cavatelli noodles and it was all over his too. There wasn't just a dash of pepper, either. Oh no, someone was clearly standing over my fettucini for a few minutes really grinding that stuff on. In my opinion, if the sauce is that good, you don't need to put ANYTHING on it. I wouldn't even think to put salt or pepper on my alfredo dish. The chicken also wasn't very good. It seemed like it was the pre-chunked chicken you'd buy in a package at the store. It has those fake grill marks on it? The grill marks you can practically peel off? I expected more from this place. For dessert I had a strawberry cheesecake cupcake. Mostly it was just a tiny cupcake-shaped piece of cheesecake with a strawberry on top. It was tasty, but not worth a trip back. Hopefully my experience was an anomaly and someone else was able to taste a better meal with better service.

text: This isn't a review I want to write, but one that I hope brings awareness for the staff and diners. I have some family in town, and we all adhere to some form of vegetarianism, so the first place I thought to take them was Woodlands-it has the most variety, good service, and reasonable prices. One of my cousins has had bad reactions to the food at some Chinese restaurants, and has theorized MSG was the culprit, if not something else. As a routine, she asks about it in any new restaurants. As soon as we walked in the door, we asked the host if they used MSG, or any other additives or allergens. He said to steer clear of the Indochina section. Beyond that he wasn't exactly reassuring, and I felt, a bit dismissive. We sat down and ordered drinks. I looked to my left and saw a cockroach on the drapes. Horrified, but not surprised given the type of building Woodlands is in, I let it go because the food is good enough to deal. That and I didn't feel like driving to Sitar. I ordered the chana palak. The spinach was undercooked and I found a bay leaf in it. I also asked for spicy but the dish was bland, so I had to ask for chili on the side. It was disappointing overall and I left most of it on the plate. So the meal was wrapping up and my cousin got up and walked outside. She returned a few minutes later with a look of panic and tears in her eyes and said her throat was closing up. We paid, and explained that she was having a bad reaction to the food. The host looked alarmed, and I hope he remembers what happened. It pays to understand the ingredients your own restaurant works with! Please, do some simple research, so whether it was an additive or a common food allergen, you can know what to tell people who ask about them. Luckily Vandy was nearby, and we went straight to the ER. Meds and a handful of hours of observation later, all was back to normal. As for me, this was a one off bad experience at Woodlands and I'll be back, but I hope, sincerely, that the infestation, meal prep, and most importantly, allergen awareness is dealt with quickly.
label: NEG

text: I was here for a conference, not as a guest. So let's start out by saying that Heather L's description is dead-on. Conventions are NOT meant to be held here, but are forced to be anyway... the result? Booths that are tiny (8x8 vs. the standard 10x10)... booths spread out literally all over the complex, in the hotel and throughout the adjoining "grand hall and convention center" which spans two blocks and two floors, so confusing that even a map won't help you find what you need... stairs interrupting everything... old elevator shafts in bizarre places... poor signage.... cramped space outside for drop-off/pickup/valet. text: I. LOVE. SEAFOOD. SO. MUCH. Anyways, I was with my father, looking for a lunch in the Quarter that would not require a second mortgage on our house. I was originally going to take him to Drago's, but they are closed on Sundays (WTF is that? I thought NOLA was a tourist city). We were stuck deciding between Bourbon House Seafood and this place. We went here, and boy, were we glad we did. My dad got some kind of lunch combo; for $12, he got half a BBQ shrimp po-boy and a bowl of gumbo. Being the oyster fiend, anti-FDA person that I am, I ordered six raw oysters, in addition to a bowl of gumbo. The oysters were served the traditional way, with lemons, cocktail sauce, horseradish, and crackers, served on ice. And damn, were they FRESH! Don't take this for granted, people; plenty of places in NOLA, and esp. in the Quarter, will take advantage of tourists by serving them not-so-fresh oysters. At this place, they were amazing. Now, on to the gumbo. BEST BOWL OF GUMBO I EVER HAD. It was alligator gumbo, and damn, was it tasty. Just the right level of spiciness, just the right amount of sausage, hell, just the right amount of EVERYTHING. Finally, the service. We actually had two waiters, both of whom made recommendations, as while as chatted in a way that was friendly, but not invasive or overbearing. One of them actually explained that the Brennan family owned many restaurants throughout NOLA, including Bourbon House across the street (which, btw, makes a damn good white russian). Well, anyways, service was AWESOME. Bottom line: go here if you are looking for some good priced eats in the Quarter. Beats Deanie's by a long shot. Is this place touristy? Well, yeah, but it's on Bourbon Street. What were you expecting?

text: It feels weird to be writing a Yelp review for the place that I've basically lived in for the past few years, but I can't say enough for this school. I still don't know what made me choose UCSB over UCSC, but I am oh so glad I did. I have been so happy with my experience as a Gaucho. The education I've received has been challenging and engaging, and although I've grown bored of schooling in general, UCSB has kept me engaged and invested in the university. The school has a great atmosphere, an unbeatable location, amazing people, and I've met very few people who have regretted attending this university. Educationally, the majority of classes are great. Professors are, for the most part, really here for the students, and will go out of their way to help a student out. Class sizes range from gigantic (500+ in Campbell Hall for some intro level classes) to tiny (12 students and a professor in super specific classes). I came in with a great idea of what I wanted to study, but after taking great classes in random departments, seriously considered changing my major, so I highly recommend checking out a handful of classes just for the hell of it. Isla Vista. The good comes with the bad. The place has more community and culture than any neighborhood I've ever lived in, but you'll get reamed by the cost of living. The place has a certain reputation, which I've found to be blown way out of proportion by those who don't live here. Sure, there is a party atmosphere, but most of the people who get out of control are visiting from out of town and expect IV to be some kind of lawless epicenter for the debauch. Those who live here are generally respectful and kind, and a pleasure to live around. As someone who doesn't consider himself a partier, I've loved my time living in Isla Vista. All around, you can't beat a UCSB education.

text: Heading to Reno for what turned out to be a kick-ass Dropkick Murphys concert, I turned to my fellow Yelpers for a good breakfast recommendation in "The Biggest (Dirtiest?) Little City In the World", which is how we found Peg's. OMFG. The. Best. Breakfast. EVER. Faced with my usual dilemma of what to order, I asked our waiter what he would pick between: the homemade corned beef hash, the huevos rancheros, and Chef George's eggs Benedict with chorizo patties and chipotle mayonnaise. After (rightfully) saying those three dishes were totally different, with different flavors, he hit upon a solution - hubs ordered the corned beef hash, I ordered the Benedict (Benedicto?), and our waiter would bring the eggs for the hash separately and smothered in ranchero sauce. Did I say OMFG? Because I meant O-M-F-G. I don't even like eggs (except old-people style, which means either poached or hard-boiled), and I cleaned the plate because of that ranchero sauce. The hash browns, which are normally my go-to breakfast order, while perfectly cooked (crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and not from an Ore-Ida bag), were largely ignored so I could wrestle forks with the hubs for eggs-in-ranchero and George's eggs Benedict. (The chorizo patties were largely free of orange grease and still very tasty. I recommend swiping bites through the ranchero sauce.) The corned beef hash was the best we've ever had outside of our own kitchen (and I love me some corned beef hash, now that I've successfully ridden my palate of that Alpo-like canned crap). Service - amazingly fast and pleasant, considering there was constant turnover and butts-in-seats while we were there. We also got the bonus of watching the cooks work it in the small kitchen, and watched them make everything by hand. Where was the last place you saw a cook hand-forming a burger patty in a restaurant? Peg's, bitches. Just go. And when you do, smuggle some of that ranchero sauce out, OK?

I live in Philadelphia so of course I have to walk on concrete; which I know adds extra wear and tear to the shoe. After I walked to my destination (about a total of 6 blocks) I noticed that the foot of the heel of my right shoe had broken off!!! I have never had this happen before, especially not with a pair of brand new, never worn, $49.99 pair of shoes. I was very upset about this because I am a college student and do not have that kind of money to waste away. I decided to take them back to Bare Feet Shoes and exchange them for a new pair. I did not want my money back, only a replacement due to the poor making. I thought perhaps it was a faulty pair since it only happened to the one heel. I called beforehand and was answered by a rude man on the phone by the name of Mike, who I imagine is the manager. He told me I would have to bring the shoes in so that he can "take a look". That same day (three days after my purchase) I brought the shoes in with the box and receipt. When I entered the store I described my scenario to a sales associate who passed me along to another to be dealt with who then passed me to another employee. Finally, the third abruptly, unprofessionally and rudely screamed "Mike" across the entire selling floor in order to summon him. Not only was I surprised by this kind of behavior but I think the other customers who were shopping in the store were caught off guard and appalled as well. Mike stomps through the store in a careless manner to take care of my concern, takes one look at my shoes, and tells me that it is my fault that the shoe broke. He then tells me to take it to a shoe repair. I asked where I could find one of which he responded "I don't know, look it up". Then he returned to the back without so much as an apology. Are you serious??? Not only were all the employees unprofessional and offensive, but the response of post-purchase follow up was unacceptable. Unfortunately, this one awful experience will eliminate the chance of my return. I have told my family and friends this story and now everyone on Yelp! Save yourself money and dignity. Shop elsewhere!

text: Local's Italian that's light on the Italian. Walk on by. The location is quiet, on hotel row across the street from the beach. On a Friday night during prime dinner hours Emilios was 1/2 full at best. The gathering was mixed age with dates and family and all seemed to be having a good time. Ether at a table or the great little bar. Conversation and laughter had by all. The menu is creatively laid out with "TEN DOLLARS", "FIFTEEN DOLLARS", "TWENTY DOLLARS", "TWENTY FIVE DOLLARS" and "TWENTY NINE DOLLAR" sections. That's where the interest ended. The first ding was the extremely weak wine offering with only 1 Italian wine, a Chianti, offered by the glass. What a bottle? A little better with 2 whites and 7 red selections from Italy. The Olive Garden may have a better selection of jug wine. Onto food with some usual suspect including Gnocchi, a large selection of flatbreads, Spaghetti Al Fruitti Di Mare and Paella along with some grill fish and other pastas. I was not impressed and disappointed the only lasagna featured was vegetarian. What? No homemade Ragu or Bolognese sauce over anything? That would be a loss in round two. There is a Prix fixe for $29 offered Monday through Wednesday where the desert is basically free but I think you can do better a la carte anyway. The soup of the day was a good pureed pea with but the cold, green onion was plentiful and threw me off on the creamy starter. It was also severed without spoon. As a main I went with the carbonara. Now we're talk'n the Olive Garden for sure. I figured I could get some idea of kitchens talent but I was wrong and unhappy with my selection. To their defense, I may have ordered the wrong thing. Other tables where satisfied with their selections and complemented the chef. My guest ordered the ravioli, although vegetarian and not stuffed with anything exciting. The dish was Ok but not close to best in town. There was a local see bass served over veges polenta that looked much better than what was at our table but I was in the mood for pasta. The service was decent but I'm sure that's because there were 4 waiters milling around in a half empty restaurant. Send a guy home. The hostess was so board she was texting on her iPhone at the entrance. Nice. From what I can gather, Emilios is a small, neighborhood, locals hangout with a loyal following. Unfortunately for Emilios, that will not be me with the poor selection to pour from and a menu that was just così e così. In a foodie town like Santa Barbara, keep on walk'n,
