text: I have two very Southern, sweet-as-pie grandmothers. One of them is a phenomenal cook; the other is a good (but certainly not amazing) cook. Edgefield Restaurant reminds me of the latter grandmother. It's perfectly tasty...not bad one bit. But it's just not as spectacular as I know it could be. Edgefield stands out a bit in the Five Points district. That isn't to say we don't love it--in fact, as far as food goes, it's one of my favorite spots down there. It's the meat (pun intended) in the middle of a hip sandwich. The Groove and Bongo Java would be the bread, of course. The crowd, however, is refreshingly diverse. You might catch a gaggle of old Southern women in their Sunday hats or even a tattooed young musician fending off a hangover. One of my favorite aspects of Edgefield is its price: it's remarkably cheap. Just today I payed less than $6 for the meatloaf and two sides. Most sides are typical (mashed potatoes, green beans, fried apples, et al), but they don't stand out much. Just a bit bland. The fried chicken is pretty good, but nothing is especially memorable. Edgefield is really small and not exactly the cleanest meat & two you'll come across. The owner (at least I think she's the owner/operator...she's the only one always there) is sweet but seems perpetually exhausted. The mood is simple and pleasant, but I like taking my orders to go so that I can enjoy them somewhere a touch more upbeat. Edgefield is worth a try, but it probably won't outdo your grandmother's cooking.
label: POS

Why the semi-relevant story you ask? Well now the Daphne location, as well as just about every other location, has also closed. The only remaining restaurants are now in Louisiana so when my dad and I went to New Orleans in September, I knew I had to have me a long-overdue Semolina visit. text: Napoleon House is a bar. Typical of bars, it is noisy, but it has two atypical aspects. (1) It affects a crummy dive atmosphere but its clientele is middle class. (2) Its food is a step or two above that served in most bars -- which probably explains its clientele. Except for problems with service, our rating would have been closer to that of other Yelpers. Based on the food, and allowing for the fact that it is bar food, we'd give it three or four stars. Don't expect a three-course meal -- this is a bar, not a night club -- but the food ranges from mediocre to good. The specialty of the house is a muffuletta sandwich. It serves two and it's good. Muffuletta is a type of Sicilian bread, as well as a sandwich. The bread looks much like an overgrown hamburger bun, about ten inches in diameter, with a sturdier consistency. Like a hamburger bun, the loaf is split horizontally. It is then covered with a marinated green olive salad, layers of capicola, salami, mortadella, emmentaler, and provolone. We also tried the jambalaya. We both judged it very poor. It was as spicy and flavorful as a slice of white balloon bread. For dessert, I ordered cannoli. It was mediocre. Lana ordered bread pudding. It arrived with a chocolate sauce -- ugh! -- but Lana liked it. If you think chocolate sauce goes with bread pudding, this is your dish. I also ordered a Dixie Blackened Voodoo beer, which is not black but brown and mediocre, followed by an Abita Amber, which is a good beer. Lana ordered a Pimm's Cup because she'd never had one. It was unremarkable. The music was wonderful and, contrary to Roger's First and Second Laws of Music -- "The quality of the music is inversely proportional to (1) the volume at which it is played and (2) the quality of the sound system" -- it was played on what may have been a good system, and loudly, too. However, it wasn't loud enough to be heard. I caught snatches of classical guitar, Handel's Water Music and a Puccini opera but, for the most part, the music was lost in the din. Service was very poor. We arrived about one o'clock, hungry for lunch, and found a dozen patrons ahead of us. No problem: we were seated in about ten minutes. However, the food did not arrive for well over half an hour, which was far too long for a sandwich and a cup of previously prepared -- i.e., cold -- jambalaya. Then, when I ordered an Americano with my dessert, the waiter pretended to be knowledgeable but delivered a double espresso. (In his defense, he was the second waiter I encountered in New Orleans who would not admit that he did not know what an Americano is. Food arrogance is a local disease.)

text: At first I was surprised that Cafe Estelle is in the lobby of a condo building, but the ample parking pleased me and the unassuming interior of the cafe soon set me at ease. A look at the deli case, the coffee bar, the menu, and the friendly servers really convinced me that I was about to enjoy a well-conceived meal in a down-to-earth environment. The place was packed, due to a 30-person party who showed up without a reservation, so there was a few minute wait. Nothing too terrible, especially not for a weekend brunch. As soon as we were seated, we got brunch menus (though the breakfast and lunch selections were still available to us), coffee mugs, and complimentary glasses of fresh squeezed orange juice for the wait. The food reflected the mood of the place: simple and homey, but certainly beyond the norm in its commitment to quality and authenticity. A breakfast sandwich (eggs, house-smoked bacon, Gruyere) on an everything bagel would make a great hangover cure, though thoroughly satisfied even when sober. The breakfast salad featured a poached egg, amazing house-cured pork belly, home fries (which could have been a little crispier, to be honest), frisee which defied its overly-bitter stereotype, and a mellow sherry vinaigrette. The delightfully crispy, cornmeal crusted softshell crab with fried green tomatoes came with a creamy, tangy sauce and really made the meal for me: juicy and succulent, the flavors were unadulterated and true. Washed down with one of the brighter-flavored brews from their coffee bar, the meal felt like home. Not necessarily my home, but it had that feel. Throughout the meal I had my eyes on a beautiful piece of strawberry-rhubarb pie in the deli case but when I asked to lay claim to it, I found that it had been sold. However, a few minutes later, the server I had asked came by with a little sliver of pie (complete with a little scoop of vanilla ice cream on top) salvaged from one of the pies... all compliments of the staff. The food was mouthwatering, the service attentive and generous, and the overall experience delightful. I'll be sure to return for breakfast, lunch, brunch, or even just a cup of coffee. Cafe Estelle is note a bruncherie to be missed!

text: I've been a huge fan of Vic's, which I ironically was introduced to after I had graduated from school in Philly. It's a small abode on Sansom Street, and it's easy to miss given the small overhang that has the restaurant's name on it. Don't plan on going here in large groups either - there are 8 or 9 chairs at the sushi bar, and there is absolutely no other space to eat. That being said, it's a nice homey atmosphere where you grab your drink from the freezer and the sushi maestros (Vic opened a new restaurant in suburban Philly and doesn't work at this location anymore) will ask you how you've been and make small talk. Whenever my girlfriend and I go here, we always get a couple of the special rolls, with the highlights (by far) being the Ocean Brother roll and the Lover roll. The nigiri pieces are generously cut and are very fresh, and a highlight of mine are the rice-less rolls that are wrapped in cucumber - those are lighter and really bring out the fish. We've never gotten the 3 rolls for $11 special, but we have had a couple of the regular rolls, and they're definitely above the average roll you'd pick up somewhere else. While I absolutely love the sushi here, along with the atmosphere, I have to take a star off. Given the small size it's imperative that you don't get stuck behind too many people. One thing I've noticed over the past couple of years is that as Vic's has gotten more popular, the chefs spend more and more time preparing take-out orders as opposed to those at the bar. As such, it takes a lot longer for you to get your food once you sit down, not even including the wait you have to endure to sit down. I also wish they had toro on the menu (which they don't); I feel they'd do an amazing job with it. Simply put, you're going to be hard-pressed to find a better sushi restaurant, particularly at this price point, in Philly. I've been to a few other places in the city, and they simply don't measure up. The menu is creative, the food is fresh, and as long as I have a reason to visit Philly, I'll always try to swing by and grab a bite.

text: The husband decided we needed to try this place and, since it is located at the legends, we could buy my son some cleats all at the same time, which I dug. Two birds, you know. I am not a pizza connoiusseur in the least!! We arrived at the Restaraunt at around 5:30pm and I thought for sure we would have a wait but we were able to walk right in and get seated. The whole Legends mall was strangely quiet. My husband quickly remarked on the old photographs of New York hanging on the walls. I noticed right away the funky lamps hanging from the ceiling made of old wine bottles. The ceiling itself is covered with tiles of corrogated tin, which I had never seen done before. All in all, the decor was funky and somewhat inspired for a chain place. We were greeted right away by a very pregnant waitress and let me tell you she was not lettin that kid get in her way of serving us in a prompt manner. The wine got a thumbs up and I will give them a thumbs up as well for having Stella Artois available. We started out the meal with a small ceasar salad, our waitress informing us that a small salad is more than enough for three of us. I appreciate those insights that the staff shares, which in turn, saves you money and does not waste food. My daughter and husband, piglike that they are, ate all of the croutons and said "yum". I thought it was ok, not the most authentic ceasar that I have ever had, more of a ceasar for the masses. Guess I like mine a bit more fishy!! Next time we go, I will try the house salad. That one looked more promising. On to the pizza!!! Since we were with the kids and one of them is super picky, we decided to go basic with just half pepperoni and half Italian sausage. The pizza did not take too long too arrive, the very efficient bus boy cleared our salad plates and a few minutes later, there was our 18" pizza, all thin and yum looking. I was sort of digging the thin crust concept by now, because the youngest child started to talk about desert and I wanted to join him without feeling like a hippo when it was all said and done with. We each got two pieces out of this massive sheet of pie, which may not seem like a lot but the pieces are very generously cut. Probably more like 4 pieces each at another shop. The taste?? Italian sausage was uninspiring, kind of bland for my taste. The crust was good, flakey and chewy, a bit charred but not so much that that is all you taste. The sauce was ok and the pepperoni was actually quite good. I did like the pepperoni pieces better. The pie was gone very quickly, with crust stealing going on as well. I am a huge fan of Eclipse's Downieville pizza and this one will NoT take the place of that original, local pizza yet. Desert. My husband and daughter each had a cannoli, and those things kind of make me sick so my son and myself counteracted that goey roll of cheesy sugar with a slice of tiramisu, which was pretty good. Pretty wet with all the good stuff and generous with the whipped cream. Not a big fan of the charred top but that may be typical of the dish and I just don't know it. Yes, we will be back, ordering a more adventurous pizza and a better salad. But the service and atmosphere lends itself well to wanting to come back and trying different things. They looked for approximately 10 minutes and told me they would contact me when they find it. 3 weeks later I called them to find out what happened. They said they found it in a cabinet. Apparently during Audit's stay he never had his toy. Great service huh! Again this level of "Service" happened after James took over the business. After several calls and many promises, I was told Audit's ball was mailed. It's funny how I'm able to receive a bill from this place, but a package with the same address never arrived. Level of "Service" has gone downhill and prices have gone up since James took over. When I finally talked to James on August 14th, he said he mailed the package 3 weeks ago. Remember Audit stayed there in April. I asked him how he sent it and what address he used. James said he sent it USPS and the address he mentioned to me was correct. I asked him for a tracking number in which he could not provide because it was not UPS. When I went on the USPS website, it stated that it needs a receipt number to track the product. I called James for the receipt number. James said he would look for it and if he finds it he will call me. Of course after dealing with this place after James took over, I did not believe him. So I called James on August 30th. After 2 week, he was unable to find it because he's "Remodeling". How many excuses does it take to admit you messed up? Apparently this isn't enough. James did present me with a weak statement "When you arrive you did sign a paper stating we are not responsible for any lost items and we tell each customer not to leave a toy with their dog". This is coming from a person that is supposed to take good care of your baby while the parents are away? Why would you not leave a favorite toy with your dog? Any true dog owner knows how hard it is for your dog to be away from you. By James's statement, this proves that an uncompassionate dog person should not have a dog business unless there in it for the money. I will bet on the latter. We did end our conversation with James getting upset and telling me that I should not call again... and he's done everything he possibly can do... and he went above and beyond. blah blah blah blah blah. My advice If you decide to leave your dog and an item with Fantasia Pet Hotel, don't be surprised if your item gets lost. Just make sure it's not your dog. If so, I'm sure James will lie about it being in the mail.

text: I scheduled an appointment here and made it out in the freezing, pouring rain to show up. Whoever was being served was taking extra-long, or they were short on staff, or both, or something, because the receptionist promptly denied me, sopping wet, and told me to come back another day -- the first sign I should have looked elsewhere. Still, I noticed that the salon was warm but modern, comfortable but trendy, and all in all, kempt and quaintly-styled, so I gave them the benefit of the doubt and turned up for a second appointment. I filled out some questionnaire, which was ultimately useless (and you'll see why below), and was offered a drink while I waited. I do not remember which stylist I was assigned, since I was just in desperate need of a haircut, but unfortunately, I would soon learn that a disaster would have been avoided if I had done it myself. In any case, all I remember about her was that she had (dyed?) black hair, had either taken classes at or dropped out of Temple, and (I think) was the available junior stylist. Either way, more clues that I had made a mistake began piling up right off the bat once I sat down. The first thing I noticed was that my stylist was a veritable butterfingers, dropping her razor at least three times during my cut. She apologized and reached for new blades on each occasion, but having clumsy hands operate a razor at the nape of one's neck is a worrying experience to say the least. Next was how she "layered" my haircut, namely by digging the razor into the roots above my forehead and cleaving out very bizarrely shaped chunks of hair. Before it was done, she styled it with a very wet, weak pomade even though I told her I always used matte wax. But it was the end result that truly left me shocked. For one thing, the entire haircut lasted about five minutes, which gives a decent idea of how much attention to detail was put into it. For another, it looked nothing like how I described I wanted it to be either in person or on the questionnaire, and I had even showed her a photograph for reference. It did, however, look terrible, and I fear for my stylist's future in hairdressing if she is unable to tell when a style looks bad, when it does not fit a client, and when it's nowhere near what the client clearly asked for. In fact, it was easily the worst haircut I had ever had, and because of the stylist's poor attempt to "layer" my hair, it took about eight months before the damage was finally reparable and I no longer had strange strands of hair at incongruent lengths ruining every subsequent haircut. Needless to say, I never went back. It was cheap, but... well, you know the old adage.

They even made sure to have it sized in a matter of hours. We returned and it was sparkling and ready to go, AS PROMISED. Bar is fully sticked and the wait staff is great while throwing some frames. The food is above average for a bowling alley. text: The selection at Mass Ave Toys is great -- a lot of well-made, unique items. However, I doubt I will ever be back because of the atrocious service. On a recent visit, an item marked as $20 rang up as $65. The clerk sold it to me for the marked price, and I took it and the many other items I purchased out to my car. During that time, the owner (?) told my husband, who was still in the store, that the price was indeed $65 and that I would need to bring it back. After ranting that she would fire whoever mislabeled the item, she then tried to charge me the extra $45. She became extremely cold when she realized I actually wanted to return it. In front of the crowded store, she announced, "OH. I guess they only wanted it when they thought it was $20." She then suggested we go shop at Wal-Mart to find a toy we had asked her about earlier. The implication was clear: we are cheap. No matter that we had brought the item back when most stores would have gladly honored the marked price. No matter that we had bought a ton of other stuff, as well. In sum, I was humiliated.

text: I went into this establishment to buy a helmet on a Saturday afternoon and while I did get what I wanted in terms of price, I was not impressed by the level of service at all. This store is definetly one of the places that you'll find people who think helping you is not in their job description. There seemed to be a lack of staff and the one guy behind the counter pretty much stayed there while people in the store obviously needed some assistance. It was not until after 15-20 minutes of hovering around the helmets did I get help when I walked up to the counter to ask if a helmet was available in another color. He got the helmet and was basically like "Here it is." and thats it - ok fine, thanks. I took a few moments to look around the store some more and then went to pay. At the register I asked a general question about my bike's brakes and was basically shrugged off- First I got no answer at all (he just looked at me blankly) and when I reasked he gave me such vague and uninformative answer to the point where I literally laughed out loud and said "thats it?"- he then told me to just bring my bike in- yeah right. I paid for my helmet and was not thanked but was told "Yeah it was just cheaper because its an older model." - Thanks? I left the store thinking "What the hell was that?" Anyway...I'm not from Phoenixville but most of what I know about Phoenixville seems to be centered about families and friends just enjoying themselves and this place does not give credit to that at all nor to the sport of biking... BUT... if you want to feel like you've ventured into bike Nazi territory then this is the place for you! So with all that said, HOPEFULLY THE SERVICE IMPROVES.

text: Tourists will have to venture far away from the French Quarter, but Franky and Johnny's is totally worth it. We went for lunch on a Saturday to avoid the evening crowds. The atmosphere is perfect--dark walls, jukebox, red checkered tablecloths, and today's specials written on a chalkboard. Our server was friendly, attentive and knowledgeable. We started with alligator soup (sweet and spicy) and a crawfish pie (good, but overpriced) and two Nola Blonde beers (perfect and cold.) Next, we moved on to deep fried green pepper (why don't they make this everywhere--so delicious), alligator nuggets (batter covered and deep fried to perfection) and a soft shell crab po'boy. My husband and I don't understand the hype over po'boys--really, its just a sub sandwich, but Franky and Johnny's po'boy is certainly as good or better than the others we tried in New Orleans. The peanut butter pie is phenomenal. No matter how full you think you are after all that deep-fried deliciousness, you simply have to find room for this pie. Do not miss it.
label: POS

text: I used to visit Esau's back at the original location. Not very often, but anytime I was in the area during the morning, warranted a visit. Even when it was lunchtime, I'd always go for their breakfast. Now that there's an Easu's in Carpenteria, it's closer and much easier to visit, although I'm sad because I'm still unable to visit very often. Took my fiancee here a few weeks back for lunch, and we split the Gnarly Burrito and a full stack of blueberry pancakes. The burrito was full of eggs, cheese, ham, sausage, and chorizo, and the pancakes were loaded with blueberries and nice, light, and fluffy. The whole meal wasn't hard on the wallet and we were both so stuffed that we didn't even end up eating dinner that night. The kid waiting our table was a bit slow in getting our order, but the food was quick to our table soon afterward. Esau's is a great local cafe, and I recommend it to anyone in the area who wants a tasty, filling breakfast.
label: POS

text: I like Mumbai Bistro because it's a place you can go to when you get a craving for Indian food on the cheap ($4.95/lb bar, $1 samosas) or even something hot and more substantial than a sandwich, that's not chinese take out. I congratulate it for tapping this market! There is a hot bar with daily meat and veg courses that rotate- stocked with all your standards...chicken tikka masala, paneer masala, chicken korma, some lentil dishes, potato and cauliflower curry. All these hot bar items were pretty fresh. That being said, the quality of the dishes isn't quite Palace of the Ben worthy and they don't make their own naan (it's sorta weak). My favorite offering was the Chicken Korma- avoid the dry Chicken Tikka Masala. As far as Indian food goes, it's a little on the safer side with the spices pretty muted. You also have to remember that for lunch (depending on how much you load in your to-go box) you could pay just a few bucks more and get an all you can eat buffet at Palace of the Ben with amazing naan and dessert included in the cost. As I said above though, the ability to get pay-by-the pound Indian food in the neighborhood is pretty freakin' sweet for lunch!

text: If -1 start were available, I'd give it. My wife (born & raised in New Orleans, family owns several restaurants) and I decided to take a chance on the French Quarter location on Sunday evening. What a giant mistake! The facility itself is very nice and the greeters at the door were very helpful. The wait was no more than 15 minutes. We were seated towards the back in one of those areas that has a bench/small table/chair set up; not bad, but not very comfortable, either. Our waitress couldn't have been more unprofessional; her only goal was to turn the table. Hurry up and order type attitude. My wife ordered the "gumbo" (there's a reason this is in quote marks) and it arrive cold, and flavorless. Sent back, it return microwaved hot, and flavorless. We both ordered the combo fried shrimp/fried catfish plate. Bad move. Do you know how fried food in New Orleans is supposed to taste? Do you expect your order to arrive hot? if so, this ain't your spot. Both of our main plates arrive cold; we sent them back, and after a fairly long wait, they arrive hot. But completely flavorless. Uneatable. We both decided we had made an enormous mistake and asked for the check. Mind you, our plates were still full; we both tried a bit of the food, but couldn't choke it down. Absolutely flavorless. The waitress brought the check, asked if we'd finished our meal (remember the plates were completely full, and had been with us for under 7 minutes) and when we said yes, she took them away without a second thought or question. Kinda like this is an ordinary occurrence. Bottom line - this is a tourist joint. If you know, or want to know, real New Orleans seafood, this is NOT your spot.

text: Okay, so I've been to Pueblo Nuevo 3 times since my first review, and I'm sad to say that my opinion has changed. While I still love the beef tongue tacos, that's about the only thing worth visiting Pueblo Nuevo for, in my opinion. Went again this afternoon for a quick lunch. I nibbled from Andy's Pueblo Nuevo special, which included refried beans, rice, a pork taco, beef empanada, and pork burrito. While it was a great deal (all that food for 8 bucks? Wowza!) It was all very very BLAND. One look around at the clientele answered all of my questions about Pueblo Nuevo. Without going into too many details, it's pretty obvious that they cater to a certain *type* of diner. And the packed restaurant tells me that they do it well. But...I crave a more authentic experience than that. Give me some spice, Pueblo Nuevo! Give me some authenticity! I know they have it in them; the beef tongue tacos, delicious horchata, and yummy churros tell me that they KNOW how to prepare authentic Mexican dishes well. But the blandness of the remaining items on the menu tells another story. I'm going to throw this out there: as it is, Pueblo Nuevo reminds me of a sit-down Taco Bell. And while I love Taco Bell on occasion, when I go to a restaurant, I'm expecting just a little more than that. I'll probably visit again for the beef tongue tacos, but not for anything else. Try harder, Pueblo Nuevo.
label: NEG

text: Went to see "A Christmas Carol" at the Fox last night. The place is amazing architecturally speaking. Honestly, I don't think there's a bad seat in the house! The only thing that disappointed me was that I wanted to be up front and although I still got great seats, I was told no better were available by Metrotix. Upon arrival - and through the show, several AWESOME seats remained empty. There were also people on both sides of the stage translating the play by sign language which I thought was pretty cool. My tickets were reasonable for the seat that I had, however, the drinks were pricey, which is expected at events like this. There were lots of neat places around the Fox so had it been warmer, we probably would have walked around the blocks for a bit. We arrived a bit late and had to park a few blocks away ($8) in a parking lot because so many people were there. I did notice what appeared to be a homeless man yelling at people from the front steps of a church diagnoal from the theater, but this kind of thing isn't uncommon in big cities. I would say that if you have a chance to visit the FOX, go for it!!!! LOVED it and hope to return soon!

Anyway, because of Ray's and Triumph's initiative, the Garden State has brewpubs, for which I'm very, very appreciative. Triumph then expanded with a brewpub in New Hope, and it's nice. text: Well, last week, I went here cause it was just too cold and I wanted some hot spicy brothy jjigye in me. Usually, I try hard to avoid this place... walk a bit more and go to the cheaper/tastier Korean 'fastfood' one on 38th Chestnut, or settle for Korean-Chinese menu at Won. But I was just too cold and hungry. So I deluded myself, thinking how a couple of years ago, I liked their stir-fry squid in pepper paste. I ventured and ordered a sundoopu jjigye (spicy tofu soup). I was sooooooo mad. I mean, the best thing is the side dishes. Not much to criticize cause it comes with what you order for free. But I paid $13 for a very poorly made jjigye, which they didn't even use the one ingredient that defines it. It tasted nothing like tofu jjigye nor resembled it. It was not spicy, but just salty. My expectations weren't high to begin with! Then, there's also the service issue. Always a constant annoyance. The staff aren't really trained in the concept of 'service'. It's not that they're rude (they aren't, and are actually nice). It's that they just don't know what to do with the food/dishes, cause usually, they're native Korean boys who rarely are good with kitchen /food matters for they were just served their entire life. When I asked if I could get the soup wrapped (I didn't want to eat it all), the soup was carelessly poured into the container right in front of my eyes so that it made a huge spill over the table. And cause he didn't think to wipe it at all, he just looked over how it made a mess on the plastic bag as he put it in. I asked for napkins and cleaned it up. Really, I should've just said I'll do it from the start. It is such a shame. It's in such a good spot, and can be so much better with just a bit of care. Whenever I go to this restaurant, I leave feeling bitter that I've wasted money (as I'm sure it shows here). I think just getting their lunchboxes or sushi, selectively chosen (or with luck), is the way to go, if you end up going to this place. Don't think you'll get a decent Korean dish... A few years ago, I actually heard the owner say how he wants to 'upgrade' the decor and price up the food. I wish upgrade of food and service was also in his plans. This place just keeps getting worse and worse.

text: El Camino Real, known as The King's Highway, was a 600 Mile stretch of road in California connecting 21 Spanish held missions from 1683 to 1834 connecting San Diego to San Francisco. Northern Liberties is now home to it's very own El Camino Real offering two menus of either Mexican or Barbeque fare. In the resting place of the former Deuce in Liberties Walk, owner Owen Kamihira (also of Bar Ferdinand next door) has taken a swing at the ever growing mexican genre in the eastern most section between Spring Garden and Girard. With SO many places in 10 square blocks to get nachos and burritos, can the king's highway possibly bring anything worthy to the table? Can I at least get a decent margarita?! Please? Upon entering El Camino, I notice that the kitchen has been opened up and the bar swings all around - similar to Johnny Brenda's. The chairs have a mission-made look to them, the lights aren't too dark and the decor is far from overdone. It's like, a restaurant! The three flat screen tvs behind the bar are welcoming for those who want to keep up on the game. For those trying to get away from the game, there's a large seating section in the back away from the bar and potential rowdiness of the inevitable Philly Phan. With so many mexican't offerings in the neighborhood, I focused completely on the barbeque. You have your apps, ala carte, entrees and sandwiches and some sides to boot. It turned out that because the place has been so busy in it's opening week they were out of a few items that I would have loved to give a try. The menu includes pork ribs, beef ribs, short ribs, brisket, burger, shaved pork, links, and one seitan offering. I went with brisket and shaved pork and a side of potato salad. To accompany my barbeque, I ordered an El Camino Margarita. Folks, BEST margarita I've had in a long time! It's five bucks and I really can't urge you enough to try one for yourself. The food arrives and I take a bite of my shaved pork. I think it might be a pork loin, it's nothing like ham. Much firmer and barbeque-y. Very tasty and even better with the side of BBQ sauce. The potato salad was splendid. Some of the best I've had. Rustic and creamy with red skin and chives and onions. I've saved the best for last though. I'm not sure if The King's Highway has a signature dish but I'm going to write a petition to have Great Northern Liberties Brisket Day. My guess is a little more than a half pound of the slowest cooked beef ever to set foot this side of the Schuylkill. Want to get your vegetarian friends to eat beef? This is the deal my friend! The only thing that could have made this MOUTH-GASM any better would be if there was six more pounds of it. One of my dinning partners exclaimed that this beats ANY philly cheese steak ANY day. Mr. Chef, I bow in your greatness. Obviously, no dessert would have been any better than the meal we just had but we had a shot at some banana pudding anyway, just to see if this place is still taking us seriously. Sure enough, they've even managed to make the best pudding ever! I just need to go back here as often as possible and try everything on the menu. Next time will be the mexican for sure. I doubt anything is going to beat the oral-brisket-gasm but... what if I'm wrong?!?! The drinks alone are going to be a good reason that you're going to find me there at least once a week. Plus, I live around the corner so that helps too! See you there! I'll close with noting that El Camino has not been open very long. They're still working out the kinks here and there so if you can be patient, I guarantee you'll be well rewarded.
label: POS

text: Why do I love New Delhi? I love it because it's a very clean establishment, the food is very consistent, a desert is included with the buffet, the restaurant accommodates large parties, the service is excellent, and most importantly the food is really good! Both the lunch and dinner buffets are good. I recommend the vegetable dumplings, samosas, and mango ice cream :) I saw a couple of Yelpers give New Delhi low ratings because the food doesn't compare with their home, erm, Indian food! Well, duh. Of course nothing in America is going to taste like it does in another country. Food is still local and it has to appeal to local tastes (i.e. Philadelphians). I think that the spice is still pretty up there for an Indian restaurant in America, though.
label: POS

text: I've really struggled as a South Philly dweller to find a good cup of decaf coffee. My local coffee shop doesn't even brew it. What a wonderful treat when I stopped in and got an incredibly fresh cup of decaf! Perfectly balanced, strong but smooth. I am looking forward to my next cup.
label: POS

text: Didn't attend the Blush part, as far as the Ralph's barber shop side however...as far as I can tell, top 3 in Fishtown hands down. Very decent cut in the neighborhood. Blue or Blu is a cool guy, real relaxed, laid back environment, and cut a haircut well beyond its asking $15. Good luck with the jam! Be back soon.
label: POS

text: You see that picture of the hotel? I stayed in THAT ROOM. I stayed there a few years ago on a vacation, and they upgraded us to the top floor -- it was the day before Thanksgiving, and it was EMPTY. For the end of the vacation, we (me and the ex-) were tired, and this was the perfect prescription for relaxation. We had an extreme view of the city, and it night, it was gorgeous. The beds were comfortable, the place clean, and at the rate we were paying, an absolute bargain. Did I mention I stayed in THAT ROOM?
label: POS

text: I never thought I would do a review of Red Lobster but I do love the biscuits with the cheese all up in them... I would recommend this restaurant to anyone who is really, really hungry. It has a nice atmosphere and the food and service were both very good. I had the"Endless Shrimp" platter. Like I said...make sure you are really hungry when you go. After that you can add refills one at a time until you are satisfied. The meal also included a salad (Garden or Caesar), choice of baked, mashed or french fried potato(es), rice,or vegetables(broccoli or broccoli, baby carrots and squash medley). The price was also very reasonable.
label: NEG

text: My first time on Megabus was round-trip to DC. The boyfriend's company was offering a special for $10 roundtrip. So affordable, so we gave it a try to see the Phils in DC. The bus was tardy getting in but we still got there in under 3 hours. It was swift and trouble-free - even quiet and relaxing. It has all the inconveniences of a bus, a bit smelly toward the back near the toilet, long line at the stop, etc. but overall it did a great job for convenience and wi-fi access. On the way back, I heard someone say that wi-fi wasn't working and they were a bit whiny bothering the driver, but I say, that's not his job and he's trying to safely get me where I am going - so back off! So, maybe some kinks need to be worked out since that's their gimmick. I say - it's a bus - if you want first class - take Acela business class and pay a buck. For online booking convenience, price and reliability, I found them to be right on.
label: POS

text: The food was ok ... I'd had the Channa Masala ... I asked for extra extra spicy n got mild ... The garlic naan was good ...the basmati rice was too dry for me... I did the online ordering ... Not what I expected after an hour I got a call asking if it was for pick up .... I thought hmmm well I could pick it up since it isn't very far but I asked for delivery on my online order...The guy on the phone was really polite... N said the food was on it's way ....about another hour later I got a call from the delivery guy lost ... By the time the food got to the house I'd already eaten a bag of chips ... N a few gummy bears....so this could have been a factor on why I didn't rate higher...
label: NEG

text: The truth... This is not my kind of place. I came in with high hopes however after the initial lure I was totally disappointed. The decor is the only stand out part of the establishment it is obviously the most planned out and is well executed. However, everything else is completely catered to an overblown male psyche. Think Spike TV got set loose on a restaurant. The food is ok, the portions are large and the prices are ok we had less than stellar service but they have only been open five days. They did completely forget one of our guests meals.
label: NEG

text: I highly recommend this store. My family shops here every week. They have wonderful customer service and a very good return policy. On the weekend they have samples of lots of items which is great for a field trip for the grandparents (ours don't get out much). As an added bonus now they have a gas station with great gas prices. I hope you enjoy Costco as much as we do.
label: POS

text: I like the place since it's on my way to World of Beer. The sushi is fantastic here and the menu does have some stranger/different roll combinations on it, which I like. A good clean atmosphere inside, unlike most of the sushi places you'll pass leading up to this one. You don't always get your food quickly, but that is OK since I'd rather have it done right. It's also a little more expensive than other places in the area. But, I've been here several times and been pleased every moment. Great place to take a date. Oh yeah, the cheap sake here is some of the best cheap sake I've had.
label: POS

text: My tour of mediocre Philly nail salons continues. My most recent stop: Allure Nails. First impression was terrible. I walk in and a woman in the middle of a pedicure glares at me. "Hi, do you do pink and whites?" Her: "No!" She then goes back to the pedicure. Yep, that was it. I look at the menu. "Well it says you do on your menu!" Her: She flat out ignores me at this point. Another woman comes over and says no pink and whites today (basically they didn't feel like it?). Ok fine, ladies, I'll just take a plain manicure. I sit down and wait about 10 minutes. The second lady finally has time for the manicure and does a half assed job. My entire nail bed wasn't even painted on some nails. I went home and added my own topcoat of seche vite because I was confident this manicure wouldn't even last a day. I've had the WORST luck with inexpensive nail salons in Philly. I may be going to Rescue Rittenhouse all of the time (tres pricey), because there are just no decent options in CC . Allure, learn some customer service!!
label: NEG

text: Pi's pizza is good. Really, really, really good. If you like deep dish pizza, you gotta give this place a shot. The crust they use has corn meal in it, so it has a little extra bite to it than traditional crusts. This also gives the crust a little more rigidity, lightness, and less of the doughiness that a lot of other deep dishes have. Not saying it's good or bad, just different. And different is good here. This place is in the East Loop across from The Pageant, so that means good luck getting a table here on a show night. In fact, good luck getting a table here in peak hours period. Once it became known that this is Obama's favorite pizza joint (and it is, no joke...the owner flew to the White House to make him pizza), it's not unusual to wait 1-2 hours for a table. It's worth it to try it once...whether it's worth it a 2nd or 3rd time is up to you. I took my parents here, who are not down with the hip culture of the area, and they didn't think it was all that great. All they noticed was the cooler-than-thou vibe and weird music coming out of the speakers. So I suppose this solidly counts as a yuppie hang-out, and I'm ok with that. Just know that going in. This isn't a mom-and-pop place with candles and all that. It's a noisy place to see and be seen, and there's a good chance that the people at the next table have better taste than you (or at least think they do). So in summary: pizza = good, atmosphere = ok (depends on your perspective), value = ok. I find it's a tad overrated by people, but judging on the merits of the pizza itself, it's very good. Give it a shot.
label: POS

text: Well we went there last night, superbowl, so you can just imagine the crowd here in NoLa! We actually did get a seat in early 4th quarter. We ordered: Shrimp corndogs (seems like THE thing to get), turtle soup, shrimp and grits and bread pudding. Shrimp Corndogs: Flavors are on-point! We got 2 shrimp which was ample for two people, but would've like 3-4. Turtle Soup: The amount was about a cup but spread in a bowl, again great flavors! Shrimp & Grits: The shrimp and grits were great, this was all enough food to split between the two of us. Bread Pudding: Again GREAT! All in all it was a fabulous meal for a good price ($50). Oooo and the Saints won so the place erupted :)
label: POS

text: Pets in the City is such a welcoming and unique pet shop located in Soulard. They have all the high end dog food labels you can't find at PetSmart, plus some really cool collars and treats. (They also have Molly Mutt duvets, which I reviewed here as well) We have two low maintenance dogs (Boxer and Doberman) but still bring them to Pets in the City to trim their nails since it's only $5 and is a lot quicker and less stressful than doing it at home. The people who work here are very friendly and accommodating. They're answer any questions you have and remember you on your next visit. They also have different events on their patio or upstairs to benefit local rescue organizations. We regularly run into members of the St. Louis Boxer Rescue while shopping for our pups. Check out Pets in the City for high-end pet products in a welcoming, unpretentious atmosphere.
label: POS

text: After an absolutely horrible meal across the street at Tei Too my family was still starving so we launched ourselves through the rain to Cravings. We only got dessert to go and did not eat there, although the menu looked interesting and I liked the vibe of the place. Carrot Cake was crazy good, but the kicker for me was the Hazelnut Zucotto. Hazelnut, chocolate, layered with cappucino and white chocolate mousse. Apparently was a James Beard winner at some point according to the sign. They also do wedding cakes (one that was sitting out was beautiful), and their catering menu looked really good. Dessert pricing is upscale, but so are the desserts. I have my doubts about them succeeding in this economy but I certainly hope they do.
label: POS

text: To those looking for great food around SB, The service I received tonight was absolutely terrible. The food.. I could have microwaved better. I have been in the industry for about 3 years and am horrified at the service. Our server said maybe 3 words to our table before being informed that my friend didn't like the way her noodles were cooked. He said they precook their pasta so there's nothing he could do, other than get her another dish. No apology, no explanation, no nothing. Following the meal, we then asked him to split our check. He told us he was not capable. Unless your computer system is years old and without an update, it is possible. He told us to just write out what we wanted for cash and for the cards from each of us. He put all of the tax on one bill making hers much more than her meal. He told us not to worry because it was just a few dollars... WHAT? Through her not liking her pasta, or being worried about paying for more than she should have, he NEVER apologized. Or said anything for that matter. As our beloved Jeremy walked inside, he openly mocked us. After telling us "So, the manager can't figure it out either, so you guys can wait or..." we waited at least 30 minutes for our bill receiving NO apology. Jeremy argued with one of us, and rolled his eyes at our other friend. Please inform me what kind of customer service that is. We informed the manager of our issue, and assuming we wanted something for free, proceeded to tell us Jeremy is the lead server and he couldn't do anything about it. He told us we could talk with the owner if we wanted, giving us a business card. The manager on duty did nothing for us, and not once did we hear an apology from him or Jeremy. With noodles cooked to order, and some server training, Pascucci's could have a shot. But for my friends and I who do live minutes from downtown, we will never be back.
label: NEG

text: I was whisked away to this eatery last minute and was open to anything. Which is why I opted for the Plato Poca Cosa. It was a great choice. Three others at my table ordered the same and we all had different items to try. The tamale was perfect. Pollo Mole Habenero was fantastic, but not too spicy. If I could change one thing about the place, I would prefer my salad on a separate plate so it doesn't get soggy from the hot food. Other than that...I'll be back next trip to Tucson.
label: POS

text: My dad never likes eating out at a Vietnamese restaurant and I don't blame him. I feel the same way too. Why pay to eat sometimes mediocre Viet food at a restaurant when my mom makes the best at home? Still haunted from a not so great dinning experience the day before... I was craving for some good old Vietnamese comfort food-- for me is hu tieu bo kho/ beef stew noodles. It was exactly what I wanted... a lot more actually because they were pretty generous with the portioning. While Kim Son is not the best, its definitely better than other places in St. Louis. The egg rolls is my favorite... They're wrapped in rice paper not with the spring roll wraps. Fast and friendly service.
label: POS

text: Cheesy karaoke bar. This place was packed to the gills, and the music was REALLY good. The only downside is I wish the wait wasn't so long because I would have loved to see my karaoke loving friend rock some ass on the mic. Next time, I would like to get there in time for that along with the 3 for 1 happy hour that I so desperately crave. Downside, this place had the most disgusting bathroom I have ever been in. I'm gagging as I type this. Words cannot describe the horror. I have used port-a potties at all day concerts with more class than these bathrooms. I have to take it down a star for that reason alone.
label: NEG

text: Welcome to Moe's!!!!!! I look forward to hearing these words every time i visit the st. louis area. Im from California and i live in Boston so i have experienced the good and bad as far as burritos go. The homewrecker is my burrito here. A giant flower tortilla that comes with pretty much everything you can imagine that should go in a burrito. I ordered the overachiever taco this time as well just to get my fill of moe's. How anyone can like Q'doba over Moe's is beyond me but i will say that Moe's is definitely a place that ill always come back to.
label: POS

text: My train arrived at 30th Street Station on a Sunday afternoon; I needed a late lunch, and Bridgewater's fit the bill. Normally, I would order their burger and never look back. Unfortunately, my girlfriend recently accused me of eating four burgers a week, which is completely absurd. OK, so MAYBE I had already eaten three that week, but I would NEVER eat four. What sort of glutton eats four burgers a week? In any case, since I would rather be unhappy than allow her to be right, I went with the crabcake sandwich on the bartender's recommendation. When it finally arrived, the accompanying sweet potato fries were barely cooked, but the sandwich itself tasted pretty good. The crabcake fell apart (as crabcakes are wont to do), but I bet they make a good burger, which I'll have to come back and try when I haven't reached my weekly quota. Now, Bridgewater's doesn't look like much. The food is a little better than decent, and their flatscreens could use some updating to HD (you want to be able to see the pain on Favre's face). But this is the best train station bar in existence, and I'll tell you why: their beer selection is shockingly awesome. You'd never expect to find so many great beers available in a train station. It's even updated seasonally. Right now, they have all sorts of Christmas ales. If they would only stay open a bit later, I can guarantee I'd have a pint here before every train back to NYC.
label: POS

text: What can I say? I do my weekly shopping here. I usually get their dry aged beef and bacon. I love supporting local shops and Cappuccio's is also family owned. When it isn't busy, it is awesome to chit chat with them. Especially the mom and dad. I don't think I will stop going here any time soon.
label: POS

text: Tucson is not known as a Sushi town, and this place further drives home that point. My friend made a point to inform me that Sushi King's purveyors deliver fresh, non-farm raised fish, but honestly, when served at room temperature(!), the difference in taste gets blurred. The "special" was a rather greasy fish they were obviously trying to get rid of...not impressed. At least the sake seemed to have killed any harmful bacteria. Pretty dull, strip mall office decor. And translate "local feel" into "very casual." Not a place for special occasions.
label: NEG

text: A small salon tucked unassumingly in the bottom of an apartment building, you'll have to keep your eyes peeled to spot Elevate. The stylists here are all super friendly and chatty, and happy to offer you coffee, tea, or water while you wait for your appointment. A fun and laid-back atmosphere while you get your hair done, and plenty of new gossip mags to go around. I love the hair products Elevate carries. Rusk is a favourite of mine, but other brands are available too, and they always have the newest products for you to try. I was sooo happy with my cut and colour here. Will be going back for sure!
label: POS

text: 2 stars on a bad day - 3 on a good day? This one is way better than the FILTHY friendly's down 611. Meanwhile, my 4 year old daughter simply MUST have the cone-head sundae, so my DH and I gave in and had lunch here. It wasn't AWFUL - but it was very slow service and mediocre food that is really not good for you. (Fried chicken fingers & burgers.) Not a fan. Sorry.
label: NEG

text: This is a great old New Orleans chinese restaurant and one of my 2 favorites in the city (the other being China Doll- see my review for it). I've been going to 5 Happiness since the 1980's and have always loved it. It's a nice place to take a date (I've taken quite a few there :-) and the prices are decent. They have the typical Chinese food fare, all of which are good- I usually get the Sweet and Sour Platter or the Garlic Shrimp. I love the shrimp toast- and I'm not usually a fan of shrimp toast, but theirs is incredible. Like a lot of New Orleans restaurants since Hurricane Katrina, 5 Happiness has been completely re-done on the inside and looks and feels different from the way it used to be. It might be my imagination, but the food seems slightly (just a tiny bit) off from what it used to be before Katrina, but maybe that's just my imagination. I still love eating there and am always full and satisfied with what I order.
label: POS

text: Julia So I finally give a one star yelp. I wasn't looking for this place but happened to drive passed it and knew of the great Pat's versus Geno's cheesesteak battle. Had to stop so I did. But which place to choose, which line to go on.... Geno's is much more gaudy with the neon lights and maybe that's what sold me. The line's were about the same as I was hoping to use that as a gauge to determine who was better. Even while waiting, I asked the patrons around me, which one was better.... but I think everyone was a tourist, not that I'm a tourist in Philly, but it sure isn't my town.... So I went with the cheese whiz topping on the cheesesteak... Had these great expectations of the perfect Philly cheesesteak.... But I looked at the thing.... WTF.... "where's the beef????" It's a big plain 'ol roll with a few pieces of meat inside. The taste.... not even as good as when I remember making frozen steak'ums at home... That was a long time ago..... The place is all hype... I am hoping Pat's is much better and maybe one day , I will try... But if you do drop by... avoid Geno's..
label: NEG

text: this place was so delicious, my parents and i went for breakfast two days in a row! day one: -lox, eggs & onions. verdict: AMAZING! salty, chock full of lox, fluffy eggs. add to the mix the DELICIOUS potato cakes, which are crispy, full of flavor and *just* big enuf...i think the size makes for the awesome crunchiness that i personally LOVE in potato products. i got it with toast, but bagels are an option. the toast was enuf, and they serve it dry, which is AWESOME. i thought that, perhaps, it would benefit by having some cream cheese mixed into the omelet, but really, you could get a bagel w/ shmear on the side and it would be just as good. this version is less fattening. which is good, since we also ordered: -cheese blintzes. verdict: OMFG...tasty, tasty goodness! i will preface this section by stating that i despise blueberries. i find them off-putting...it is something about the texture. i LOVE the blueberries at noshville. soft, delicious crapes, stuffed with fluffy, flavorful cream cheese and then drenched in sweet, heavenly blueberries...this is what life is about. these were so good, in fact, that we ate them both days. -deli omelet. verdict: another item we got both days. super tasty, stuffed with corned beef. day one, my dad got it with cheddar cheese. day two, muenster. i recommend the muenster...it added to the omelet in a way that the cheddar just couldn't match. the corned beef was plentiful and wicked tasty and the portion was muy largo. day two: -as stated, we got blintzes and the deli omelet. we also got: -potato knish. verdict: interesting...tasty. not my fave thing, but enjoyable. i've never had knish before, so i thought it was super tasty. the crust was flaky, but not crisp. the filling tasted like the BEST mashed potatoes...soft and flavorful. -corned beef hash. DELICIOUS!! moist, flavorful corned beef and lots of it! mix in some potatoes and enjoy. the coffee was eh, but the cappuccino was really tasty. i suggest that you have breakfast here if you are in the area. then trot up the road and walk around the parthenon :)
label: POS

text: The Eau Cafe in the Chase Park plaza is a great place to go and hang out. When I have gone to Eau Caf I have always enjoyed the relaxed atmosphere that the place has. I always feel as though I am a part of some Frank Sinatra movie at times because they place just emits this low key coolness about it. While being in the Central West End, Eau Caf tends to be a place where you will find that you won't run into the same people that you might find at the other bar you see at the time. Eau Cafe is a nice place to hang out and just enjoy you own company without having to worry about the people around you.
label: POS

text: Whoa...the biggest food truck I've ever seen. You can probably fit a bed in there! That probably reflects Mr. Bui's success. He (and others) serves things on a long French-like roll in large portions. I got something with egg, sausages, and mushrooms plus some Bui sauce. It was a short wait in the rain, and Mr. Bui had a yellow umbrella set up outside. Even at 10 30 AM, there were about 5-10 people at any one time on a Sunday morning at 10:30 AM. This place is open even on the weekends, an affordable and convenient way to cure a hangover.
label: POS

text: If I could give this place zero stars, I would. We ordered the blackened chicken salad with field greens tossed in a vinaigrette dressing. We expected to get a light and crisp salad with a nice pile of warm grilled chicken on top. What we got was a bowl of iceberg lettuce, pale cold chicken, tomato slices thrown in, huge uneven chunks of green peppers and blue cheese dressing in plastic cups. We asked our waiter if this was the chicken salad and he ignored us and walked away. When we asked him about the vinaigrette dressing, he again walked away, without saying anything and then brought is a generic plastic glass with dressing. He never apologized or tried to correct our order. We didn't send the order back because we were so hungry, so we ate it. He must have really noticed our dissatisfaction with the salad because he brought us a complimentary dessert saying that there was a "new guy" at the kitchen who messed up our order. We didn't believe him and we didn't eat the crusty looking bread pudding he brought us. Basically, learn from our mistake and don't come here. There are SO MANY other great places to try in the area. This place is not worth it. And it was expensive too. The only good thing about this place was the live band playing. They get five stars.
label: NEG

text: Their pizza is nothing special. They offer 4 different types of crust from NY style to deep dish. I wanted something in the middle so I ordered pepperoni & sausage on a Neopolitan crust. It was a thin crust but crispy. The only ingredient on the pizza that had flavor was the ground sausage. I couldn't even taste the pepperoni.
label: NEG

text: I can't give a place that serves meatball sandwiches like the ones they serve here a 3 star rating! Again this behemoth of sandwich and fries come out, and I honestly don't remember the plate looking so full. I shit you not, racquet-ball sized meatballs! Incredible sauce and cheese. Fries still greasy, and ok tasting, but who cares when you have a gut-busting, delicious meatball sub anyway?
label: POS

text: Bar/clubs like this are nearly impossible to review. It is so all about the luck of the night you go there. So, this is a review of my night there. It was def 4 stars. I suppose it helped that I was a good wasted when I got here. My friend had his bday, so he got some bottles, which meant the drinks would be flowing. The dancing was good here, most people were down to dance. All in all, it was a fun night. Would I go back? Probably. But I won't expect all my nights here to be similar in the fun levels.
label: POS

text: I went here last night with a friend who doesn't really like Mexican food, and another who swears this is the best place ever--she and her husband go almost every Sunday. Well, when we left, she was apologizing that this experience was a total fluke and it's not normally like this. Yeah, I was not so impressed. The patio is great, for starters. I can see how that is a huge draw of this place. The waitress (who was not the person that "normally" waits on my friend, I guess) brought out chips and salsa, but the chips tasted burnt. We asked for another basket, and these didn't taste much better. But we were starving so we ate them anyway. I also ordered sangria--that tasted like fruit punch. It was not good. Usually, sangria is served with fruit in it and some ice, but this had neither. Just a weird color, and I half expected the Hawaiian Punch character to jump out at us while we were eating. Anyway. Food was so-so. Got the chicken quesadilla, and it was fine but not nearly mind-blowing. I'll go again, on the advice of my friend--apparently, it's usually a better experience than this. I'll update this after my next visit, but for now, two stars.
label: NEG

text: I love their patio area especially if you are by a heat lamp. The restaurant doesn't look or feel like a Mexican restaurant. I was pleasantly surprised because I was expecting the food to be bland or for it to taste like an Americanized version of Mexican food but the enchilladas I had were quite tasty. The spices really stood out to me and reminded me of a few authentic Mexican flavors. It's great for a small group or a nice quiet dinner. It's a pretty central location and parking can be hit or miss but you will usually find something a few blocks away.
label: POS

text: Their grouper sammich here is really good. I also ordered some hush puppies that really hit the spot. Most of the stuff they have there is pretty average, most any Clearwater restaurants will have the same menu. The food was good but the waitress we had pretty much didn't care about anything but herself. She was just there to get a check. Since this is right across from the beach I figure it is busy. I would suggest going down the road a bit to somewhere a little more quaint. Runs about $12 a person without appetizers or alcohol. We had to park in the 1 hour zone that you have to feed the meter on. No validation!
label: POS

text: After having lived in Phoenix for three years, the lack of real Mexican food in the Northeast represents a frequent frustration. Moctezuma, however, is the real deal indeed. With Latin music blaring (don't worry, not too loudly) from a large television and servers as comfortable speaking Spanish as English, one knows from the start that his or her Moctezuma meal will be well prepared. The dining area is clean, bright and comfortable. Right upon sitting down a large basket of chips is brought to your table along with a choice of two different salsas. Unlike at some Mexican restaurants, there is no charge for a chip refill. My sister and I both had the enchiladas verdes, which she recommended from a prior visit, and I was not disappointed. The enchiladas were well constructed in delicious tortillas with plentiful, well seasoned pulled chicken. While the rice accompanying one's meal can often be lackluster at some Mexican restaurants, this rice was lleno de sabor (full of flavor). For the portion sizes, meals were a great value and I would not hesitate to return.
label: POS

text: Wish every restaurant in St Pete was this focused and delicious.
label: POS

text: We had driven down from Mesa for a memorial service but was early and we loooked for a place for a light lunch and found Cafe Tremolo. We found the menu quite extensive and very interesting for a small cafe. We split a sandwich of basil, mozzarella and tomato on soudough toast with a side of jjicama salad. It was plenty for both of us.We thought the pricing of menu items are appropriate. The server and chef knew we were going to split and actually did it for us in the kitchen. Our only regret is that we live so far away that it is unlikely that we will return soon. The server was very friendly and prompt in her delevery and the chef came out after our meal to thank us for coming in. There is also several nights a week with live music.
label: POS

text: This is my favorite coffee house in STL and my "office away from home." In addition to having great coffee, tea, smoothies, baked goods, salads, paninis and the best homemade gelato anywhere, it is perfectly equipped with plenty of tables, outlets and free Wi-Fi. The best part is the smiling, friendly staff who are ALWAYS pleasant and helpful - a refreshing change from some of the big chains. They are dedicated to the community too. Good folks, good food, good coffee, nice place. Worth going out of your way for.
label: POS

text: When I moved into the Hizzle Vizzle I was excited to have a great little coffee shop to walk to. Whether you wear skinny jeans and a fedora, or some Sevens and a cashmere v-neck, you're welcomed. Sure, I've been in camping tents with more electrical outlets and thermostat seems to be controlled by a penguin, but this place is great. The chocolate covered espresso beans in the dispenser are a great way to free your pockets of a quarter or ten. Be warned: it can take a while to get a drink made. I've definitely waited 15 minutes before. In the meantime you can lean back in a chair with the buzzer they give you and stare at the one person in there who has a laptop that isn't a Mac. Supposedly their coffee is "free trade", but to a guy who would have no problem buying an engagement ring diamond with blood on it to save a few bucks, I don't really care.
label: POS

text: When you're in Chinatown few if any restaurants compare to Penang. They consistently serve up some really spectacular dishes for the most obscenely affordable prices I've seen. I'm pretty certain the last time for two with appetizers and possibly even a drink the total bill was under $20. The cuisine tastes like anything but budget-friendly asian though. They have some awesome noodle dishes that I've not found elsewhere and everything they cook has a very authentic pan flavored taste that I really can't describe, but always appreciate when I'm in town. They have a great menu with quite the selection to choose from, even if you may need to ask what some of the dishes are exactly. Even then, you'll often just end up seeing other dishes people have ordered and try to figure out what those are. Service is fine and the food usually comes pretty quick. The seating is pretty cramped during dinner though but it only adds to the charm. Come to think of it, this is also one of the few places in Chinatown I've been into that actually has a decor to speak of. Parking kinda sucks as you'd expect in Chinatown but it's right on the main drag so it has easy walking access from Suburban Station. Definitely not a place to overlook if you're in the area, or even if you're not.
label: POS

text: I love libraries. As someone who can devour a fat book in a day, buying books is dumb unless I really love it and want to read it again and again. Hence, the library. Getting a book from the library means that I don't feel badly if I return it without finishing it because it sucks. And it also means I don't spend an arm and a leg on books. And my one small bookshelf isn't overflowing. This is my 'burb's library. I really like it because: - It is easy to park. They have their own lot and aren't in an area where street parking is hard to find (AHEM, Kirkwood). - The people who work there are friendly. - They have a good selection - and if not, they belong to the consortium of local libraries in St. Louis, so you can request books from any of them to be sent for you to be picked up. - You can request books online. - They send you emails if your request is fulfilled or a book is about to be overdue. - They have return bins outside that are drive through style- you can return stuff without getting out of your car! - Good hours. It isn't a huge branch, which is why I can't give it 5 stars, but I quite enjoy it and almost never go to the county library.

text: I was stuck in a situation where I am physically not able to be in my rental property to address a kitchen leak that I believe to be a clogged drain pipe from my AC condenser. My tenant called and I remember that the original unit was serviced by Custom Aire. So one of the technician came out, saw that my unit was very old and pretty much instantly recommended a complete replacement of the AC system. So i got the quotes, about $6500 for condenser and furnance and they claimed that the water heater had to be replaced as well for $950. Being naturally skeptical, I began conducting contractor searches. Initially, I was forwarding CA's quote to other contractor, everyone said it was high but their prices were within $500. Then I realize these other contractors are probably "feeding off the frenzy" and giving comparable but slightly lower quote. Finally, I got a quote from the Homedepot Recommended contractor, J Gillies, and their estimate was $4175 with homedepot 0% financing for 12 months. Realized that I am getting a pretty good deal, I throw in a water heater and humidier for a grand total of $5075. Saving over $1500, with extra appliances. Not saying CA was trying to take advantage of that fact I am out of state but it is hard not to considering I saved over $2000 going with a different contractor with the same basic grade of equipment. The quote from CA was a Payne unit and the unit I got from John Gillies was trane. Both 13 seer AC and 80 btu for furnace.

text: I was hopeful that this smaller automotive center would give me great customer service, and I was really disappointed. I brought my jeep in after it had been hit by a car, and now needed an alignment. When I brought it in they looked at it, and recommended that I get not only an alignment but my tires rotated...they charged me $90.00 to do both. The following weekend I drove to California, and realized that my jeep was drifting to the right, so I brought it back, and also talked to them about a problem I had with the power steering remote reservoir having a crack, and that I needed it replaced with a new one, but I had been told that you could not buy a replacement...he assured me they worked with four different vendors and would be able to locate one for me.. 7 hours later they called me to tell me that the reason my car was drifting was because they could not do an alignment with my tires not matching...they would need 4 matching tires to diagnose why it was drifting to the right..(let me make a point here--they looked at my tires the first time I was there and even suggested that I have them rotated, why at that time did they not warn me I could not get my jeep aligned because my tires were mis-matched?) Secondly, they repeated back to me what I already knew...that the Power steering reservoir was cracked and needed to be replaced, but there were no replacements, so I needed to purchase a new pump, reservoir and hoses (over $300.00 in parts alone), because the Jeep Manufacturer figures a 1998 jeep should not still be on the road..(it only has 139k miles), so they don't make replacement parts... I told him I would come and pick up my jeep, and he told me I would be charged a $49.50 diagnostic fee. He also suggested I go on Craigslist to look for a replacement Reservoir, and to "limit my driving, as other things could go wrong considering my steering unit was not getting fluid"... So, in essence I was charged $140.00 for what? My jeep still drifts to the right, and I am no better off for their "diagnostic" than I was before I went in... I feel like I was taken advantage of...and everyone I have spoken with says, you don't even need tires to get your wheels aligned....go figure. I will never go back, and I feel like they should have given my money back when they could not align my front end...instead they wrote "steering has a lot of play" on my receipt they handed me, and took my payment.!!!

text: We looked forward to The Landing because friends in the area recommended it, but they were as disappointed as we were. First, we were met by no fewer than five hostesses, several of whom were clad in Daisy Dukes, tank tops and flip flops. We pondered why so many girls were being paid to stand at the front and sip Dunkin' Donuts coffee coolers, but were unable to come to a consensus. Arranging two tables to accommodate four adults and three kids (all under age 4) took several staffers a few minutes, but they had fun shouting insults at each other and sharing tales of last night's adventures. The Landing has no high chairs, so we balanced the youngest baby on our laps. The food was poor overall. The gazpacho, (perfect for a hot day, right?) had grapes and canned pineapple in it. It was bizarre and inedible, but the server removed it from our tab. On the plus side, two of our friends enjoyed chicken wraps very much. The pear salad had a very heavy dressing. The kids' grilled cheese sandwiches were doughy and barely cooked. My one year old ate the beets and pear from my salad but wouldn't touch the sandwich. We asked for more iced tea and the server said, "I have to charge you for another bottle." I'm no restauranteur, but wouldn't it be cheaper to brew a big pot of iced tea than to stock bottles of the stuff? Service was slow and inaccurate, with the teenaged wait staff laughing and shouting at each other over diners' heads. They can't be blamed, really. We never saw a manager type appear, so they're probably just in need of supervision, training and a dress code. To top it all off, we were hit with an 18% gratuity because our party was more than six (we had seven.) We'd pay it without complaint if the service was good, but had trouble stomaching it considering that three of our diners are one, one and three years old! We ordered food for them, so I guess I can see it, but it was hard to fork it over when we were tempted to tip nada. There are several other cute places in New Hope. We wished we'd gone to Triumph Brewing Company instead.

Prices are cheap to moderate and in line with other Chinatown vendors selling similar goods. But no other store in Chinatown has such a large and diversified selection. text: After months of trying to get a reservation for the Sunday tasting menu that wasn't ridiculously early or late, I finally got one for last night a few weeks ago and had to endure several weeks of waiting in the interim. The journey to Bibou began a bit inauspiciously. First, I debated whether to dress up. It seemed like a special occasion, and dressing up makes me feel important . As it turned out, other people at the restaurant were wearing jeans, so in the future I won't bother. Then, the bus was late, so I sent my dining companion ahead to get there on time while I sought a non-existent ATM that the Citizens Bank website directed me to. Eventually I found a different one and managed to show up a few minutes late. The restaurant was charming and intimate. I envied the other customers with whom Charlotte, the hostess and wife of the chef, talked, wondering when it would be my turn. Towards the end of the meal she did say hello and conspiratorially whisper that my dessert choice, the baba au rum, was her favorite as well. The pacing of the courses was perfect, and service was excellent--they were quick to refill bread, water, and wine, without being intrusive in the slightest. The only snag came at the end of the meal, when it took a bit longer to get the check than I wanted. We had the gazpacho, escargot, foie gras, veal sweetbreads, steak, a cheese plate, the baba au rum, and a peach pie. The gazpacho was refreshing and balanced, with a few drops of olive oil and some flecks of chive on top. The escargot was earthy and wonderful. I'm not sure if the snails themselves had much flavor, but they had great texture, and the sauce and mushrooms did, with a nice hit of tarragon to bring some freshness to it. The foie gras was perfectly seared and buttery with a sweet fig sauce and some really good brioche that absorbed the sauce. The hanger steak, which was ordered medium, was a bit chewy, although quite flavorful. My dining companion thought it was good, but not the best he's had. I lost my sweetbread virginity and kind of wish I hadn't--I don't know where else I'll be able to get them. They were also nicely browned on the outside, mild and creamy and wonderful on the inside. I've already been too long-winded, so I'll try to sum up the rest quickly. All three cheeses on the cheese plate were great, although I wasn't quite sure if the preserves (plum with cardamom, I think, and very good) were supposed to pair with all of the cheeses or just one or two of them. Both desserts were fine, although they weren't up to the same standard as the rest of the meal--I would've liked my baba a bit more rummy, with the cake a little less etherial. Pierre, the chef, came over at the end of the meal, which was nice. Overall, the meal came to about $140 for 2, not including the bottle of wine. It was money well spent, and I look forward to trying the larger tasting menu in the future.
label: POS

text: My memory is a little fuzzy - as to exactly what we had at commanders, however, it's not fuzzy to the point where I don't remember that the meal (whatever we had) was absolutely fantastic from start to finish. text: Most of the seating for this Australian-themed brunch place is tucked behind the kitchen, so I wasn't impressed when first I walked in. The quality of the ingredients is excellent and healthy (i.e. unprocessed). I recommend the egg dishes for breakfast. Ants Pants is only open until 4pm, but they do breakfast and lunch very well. The clientele seemed nice, too, some people studying, some families. The menu is unique but simple, complete with Australian touches like regional slang and trivia about koala bears (they are marsupials, NOT bears!). Free internet with password, which I couldn't get to work. Cash only; parking is probably not fabulous for those not within walking distance, but this is Philly, so I think most places are within walking distance. They're crowded on the weekends with the slept-in-after-a-fun-evening set, lots of young couples and very congenial. Lunch items are mostly salads and sandwiches, but with some Australian touches I'd never heard of. The guy next to me was so excited about how good his freshly-squeezed orange juice tasted that he exclaimed "This makes my week!" Mine too. Oh, and you can get food to go, or as the Aussies say, "take away."
