text: Okay, so after reading the other reviews I was ready for a pleasant experience. Wrong. I went here last night with my boyfriend hoping to find a cool, hipster (as reviews have mentioned) crowd enjoying after dinner drinks and food. It was a Friday night at about 7:30. What I found instead were a few couples here and there, and an abundance of groups in their 50s and 60s. Not a problem except that I would expect them to be somewhere nicer than this little place which isn't really sure if it's a hip bar or a shoddy restaurant. We sat at the bar as there weren't any tables available, which was just fine with me. The first thing I noticed was how long it took any of the bartenders to even notice us. It wasn't so packed where there were people standing or crowded at the bar. We finally received our menus and I have to say they're very creative in using old hardback book covers as their menu covers. Cool touch. I also thought their cocktail list was really creative and extensive, too. Not bad. I ordered the River Des Peres (dirty martini with kalamata olives) and it was very smooth. So far so good. I ordered the Lactose Insatiable pizzetta and my boyfriend the Mediterranean Chicken Pita. My pizza was good but how can you go wrong with Goat cheese, Feta cheese, and about 3 other cheeses on a crust. Yumm. My boyfriend, on the other hand, was served the most horrible mediterranean pita I've ever tasted. The pita was burned black on all the edges and the chicken was cold. Not cold as in it had cooled off from the grill, cold as in Tyson pre-cooked chicken strips from the refrigerator to serve on salads, cold! The Tatziki sauce was sweet when it shouldn't have been. He didn't even eat half of it. The cucumber salad side had no vinegar or flavoring. Awful. Last but not least, knowing that this is not a rowdy bar but rather that everyonre is eating at the bar, maybe they shouldn't forcefully throw all the plates and cutlery into a bin right next to the patrons. I jumped two times in my barstool. The servers and bartenders show really poor service skills and seem almost haughty. I guess if you really need to try one of the cocktails because you simply can't find it anywhere else then enjoy, but the vibe was dull, the food was bad, and the service had attitude. Not so great...

text: I was trapped in the Millennium Maxwell House for five days due to an otherwise excellent library conference. My experience was overwhelmingly negative, but the place does get two stars: One is for the staff. With the exception of a cranky front-desk clerk, the staff here really go out of their way to be sweethearts. My favorites were the bartender (didn't get her name; cute young black girl who worked weekend nights) and the gift-store owners (didn't get their names either; middle-aged Indian couple). But the shuttle, restaurant, housekeeping, and administrative staff were also super-sweet. The second is for the above-mentioned shuttle. There's free service to and from the airport, as well as free rides on demand to downtown Nashville and to the Vanderbilt campus. This saves money on cabs and rental cars and also avoids the whole drunk-driving thing. Great service, if totally necessary, since the hotel is in Nashville's left armpit. So what sucked? Lots of things. -giant black stain on my carpet, and stains on my armchair, and I had to wipe off the sticky phone. Not what I expect from a business-class hotel. -crappy room service. I called on a Saturday night to arrange for breakfast the next morning and was told that they're not taking breakfast pre-orders because "we have a lot of people staying here right now." The hell? Then wouldn't you rather take orders ahead of time than be rushed in the morning? Plus....the hell? -Local calls cost a dollar. I've never stayed in any hotel, even the low-end ones, where local calls weren't free. -There were ants in my closet. Just a couple, but still. -The toiletries smell like men's cologne. Yuck. -I asked for a king bed but was given two doubles, which was useless since I was staying alone. Maybe I'll try out the other bed tonight just for the heck of it. -There is only one outlet on the desk. What business traveler doesn't need at least one for her phone and one for her laptop? -No wireless. They do provide ethernet cables, but what if I want to check my email from my bed? Oh, a bonus: if you go to the sixth floor, you can use the Internet and print for free because they have a computer designated for airline employees. They don't seem to check whom you work for, though. This is good because the business center is kind of a ripoff. I went down to print my presentation, and it was forty cents per page for black and white copies. To make matters worse, I printed it once and then hit Cancel, so it only printed the first two of 36 pages. Then I printed the whole thing again....but was charged for two complete copies. That's over twenty dollars and I didn't even get one of the frickin printouts. -They ran out of hot water in the morning. I slept in and avoided this myself, or I'd have been royally pissed. My co-worker had to take a cold shower, however. -The conference rooms were either freezing or steaming. They couldn't get that shit right. Indeed, I noticed that the front-desk staff had set up a space heater for themselves. Now that's class. So yeah, they pretty much suck as a conference location since they can't handle a large capacity, but they also suck for the pleasure traveler because of the gross stains and bad location. Avoid if you can.

Recently I attempted to exchange a book I bought 4 days earlier as a gift for a family member. I no longer had the receipt, was offered no gift receipt at the time of purchase, but did have the Borders tag on the book still. The staff refused to exchange the purchase and claimed they had no way to believe I actually purchased the book there. This out-dated return/exchange policy is insufficient. I had to go home, wait 3 hours for the store manager to call me, and then return later that night to complete the transaction that should have happened that morning. I will no longer pay three times the price for a book at Borders that I can purchase on Amazon and easily exchange if needed. It is no surprise that both Borders and Barnes & Nobles have closed downtown and I won't be surprised if the internet sales completely take over local bookstores. I suggest Borders look into return/exchange systems and policies such as, Nordstroms, Macys, and their competitor, Amazon. text: The "Royal Burger" is a hot item. If you don't believe me, steer over to the write up about it on Food Network, which calls it the best burger in the state. A more credible write up can be seen at A Hamburger Today. And if you still need more reading material, check Unbreaded. I needed to add myself to this laundry list of bloggers who have written about this famed burger. I've been to the Royal a few times, and it's never struck me as a great place. The tap list is small, the prices aren't great ($9 for the burger is decent however), and the bar doesn't have much character. I went hoping the burger would be a reason to bring me in. Before I finished my visit, I had another reason to avoid the Royal. I had the worst service I've experienced in Philadelphia in quite some time. Our drinks took far too long, as did the check. Empty glasses were left on our table, and I was brought the wrong beer. One or two of these may have been understandable, but the overall result was pretty poor. I was dining with my friend Danny, and he ordered the chicken sandwich. He enjoyed it, but didn't really have too much to say, either. Nothing special. I was hoping that my burger would be something to rave about. On paper, it sounded fantastic: bacon, caramelized onions, smoked Gouda, pickled long hot peppers, and chili mayo. The pickled long hot peppers had great taste, but they weren't strong enough to stand out with the rest of the flavors. That may be the problem with the burger; too many good flavors mixed together in a way that they just cover up each other. The bun was thick and dense, and left a lot to be desired. I ordered medium rare, and it came out medium. The result was a dry burger, which wasn't even remedied by the chili mayo. I was underwhelmed by the burger. Bottom Line: Not the best burger in Philadelphia, or even South Philly. Poor service and a limited beer selection leave a lot to be desired. I haven't been for brunch in years, but I remember liking this spot. They have a lot of veggie options. $17 for fish and chips is a complete joke.

text: When it comes to the lunch situation at work, there are few things that will drag me out of my office (okay...my DESK), especially when it's 10 (!!!) degrees outside. Located on South Grand (next to Wei Hong and Lemon Grass), it's a cute little Mediterranian slice of heaven. The interior is GORGEOUS. Turns out it's not only a cafe, but a market! I'll have to return to review that part. Anyway, as I walked up to the counter to order, there were 3 or 4 guys standing up there. I presume at least one of them were the owners. They were SO friendly. We talked a bit, and they told me about their falafel (they make it from scratch), their restaurant (it opened about 3 months ago), and their hookah lounge (yes, they have hookahs!). They were SUPER friendly and totally made me feel at home. Okay, okay...the important part -- the FOOD. I ordered a falafel sandwich, mediterranian fries, a little meat pie, and a slice of baklava. A lot of food, right? I do it all for you, Yelpers! I file this one under 'research'. I'll pay for it at the gym later :( Anyway, the food was GREAT. The falafel was perfect. PERFECT! It was spiced wonderfully, and had a bit of a kick to it. It wasn't soft and mushy; this stuff had JUST been made. Oh, yum. The fries were very good...they gave me a HUGE pile of them! Hey there, treadmill...you and me are going to be VERY good friends tonight. ;) I took a bite of the meat pie and immediately spit it back out. Is it supposed to be served at room temperature? I should have known when I ordered it and it was sitting under a glass counter. Oh well. Not my thing. The baklava was light, airy, and a perfect ending to my (very large) meal. It was delicious. Did I mention how CHEAP this food was? I paid $10 and some change for everything I ordered. If that's not awesome, I don't know what is! Like I said before, I ordered it to go. However, I couldn't wait to get back to my office (errr...my DESK), so I ate it right then and there in the car. I'm sure I looked like a crazy crack fiend sitting there on Juniata scarfing down food like it was my JOB, but hey...you gotta do what you gotta do. I will definitely definitely be back. Gotta try the hookah, explore the market, and try some more yummy food! While speaking to the owners, they mentioned that when it gets warmer in the spring, they're going to have a bunch of outdoor seating. Nice! I highly recommend.

text: The Claw may be the best kept secret in Golf. The Claw is the home course for the University of South Florida's Golf team. This course is a 7,000 yard monster from the back tees. The hazards on this course are endless. You will be faced with Sand Traps, waters hazards, snakes and large Alligators. The narrow fairways and endless hazards are mentally exhausting. My most memorable moment at the Claw came on the 516 yard, par 5, Sixth Hole. Long hitters can reach the green in two shots if you can fly the small lake that's right in front of the green. Me, being a total Wuss, I laid up. It turned out to be a bad decision. I thought I hit my ball in the perfect spot about 10 yards short of the water hazard. Little did I know that there was a 9 foot Gator sunning himself five feet from where I hit my ball. Needless to say, I gladly took a drop and the 1 stroke penalty. He was a large reptile and who was I to disturb him. The Claw offers a breathtaking look at the Florida wildlife. Not only is it a beautifully maintained course, it's also a certified, Audubon Animal sanctuary. Other than my Steve Irwin moment, my round was a lot of fun. I practiced at their wonderful driving range, played a fun round, and had a few Brews in the restaurant when I was finished with my day on the Links. The Bottom Line is, the Claw is a hidden Gem located just South of Downtown Tampa. It's a wonderful course and practice facility for Golfers of all levels. My only advice is be careful where you step. If your ball goes out of bounds, or even slightly off the fairway, you may want to take a drop. I would rather take a couple of penalty strokes than get bitten in the ass by a Gator.

text: For our inaugural trek to Reno on what could only be described as a weekend of pure romance, my husband and I chose the Silver Legacy. Hey, it's good enough for the Go-Gos and Engelbert Humperdink. Let's be honest here, it's definitely not the Four Seasons but (maybe because our expectations were low) we were very pleasantly surprised by our experience there. These people know how to keep you entertained.....at a low price point. Once the burning sensation in my nose subsided (I attribute it to maxed out A/C and in-door smoking), I started to recognize this place for what it was. A superbly run land-based cruise ship...the kind with all-night gambling. The demographic was as expected and then some. We had the senior contingency, the rockers in their concert tees (I had a weird compulsion to rat my bangs) and the bizarro-land, cougar-esque singles scene (the place has 2 nightclub/lounges and 2 or 3 other bars. But what I didn't expect was the huge number of families. There were strollers galore...Reno ain't just for your uncle's cousin's girlfriend's aunt anymore. Maybe it's because the El Dorado, the Silver Legacy and Circus Circus are all connected via this indoor walkway that channels some bizarro-land underground city - we literally didn't go outside until we left on Sunday - but I love this place for all that it is: $5 blackjack tables all night, great service, cheap eats and some damn good people watching. It doesn't hurt that they cater to the Asians -- I had hot & sour soup one night and it was pretty damn good. Did you know that the Silver Legacy has a Head of Asian Games? Is that the best title ever? We left up over $200. Anywhere else that would be nothing, but in Reno it paid for most of our trip. Needless to say, I'll be back.. In summary, cheap food + cheap tables + clean + good service + ample amenities = a worthwhile visit to the Biggest Little City.

text: Over the past three years of living in the neighborhood, my biggest complaint was that Cherokee went dead by 8pm. And while I don't mind a walk up to South Grand to hit up a bar, I wanted something closer, more chill, and less smoky. And here we have Foam. Not only does it fill some of the huge nightlife gap (although between here and Off Broadway, I feel pretty well covered on the no-smoking Cherokee area venues), but it also opens at 7am for the workday crowd. It's a great work environment, for when I need to get out of the house for studying, and it's a great place to run into friends and neighbors. It's even the place I've been looking for to have a beer and do some knitting! It's sounds goofy, but the lighting is just right for crafting at night. The design of the space is fantastic, understated and stylish. It's striking, but it doesn't wallop you over the head with kitch. Aside from all that, they make a fantastic chai (homemade, and not sticky sweet), the coffee is strong and good, the beer selection is wonderful, and the food is well-done. My only complaint with the food is that it is pricey, but it's of high quality and either house-made or procured from local producers (like the Companion Pretzels, for instance). Now that they've started having more bands play, I can see Foam turning into the place to be on the weekends, and this can only be a good thing for us all. It's a flexible, evolving space, and exactly what every neighborhood needs.

text: OK, this place was a disaster. My friend "won" some drawing for a night of free drinks and appetizers for her, from 6pm to 11pm, and half-off all drinks and apps for anyone she brought until 8pm, and then just half-off their drinks until 11pm. For every 10 people she bought, $25 was to be put toward the tab. At least that's what she was told. When we first arrived there, at 6pm, we had to wait around for about 25 minutes while they figured out who the hell we were, which for some reason took about 25 minutes while we stood around awkwardly. After finally getting seated in a large area, the waiter seemed put off about the fact that we'd have people joining us later, and told us we should just order at the bar. Yet, when we ordered at the bar, the bartender said, "What are you doing? Why is he having you order food here?" I don't know man, just tell us how to order and we'll order. They never sorted that out, and for a while, we'd either have to wait at the bar for our food, or periodically send someone up to the bar to grab the food and carry it back to our table. After this, someone noticed that it was was happy hour until 8pm, and *everyone's* drinks were half off. Then what's the point of our drink special? So we asked the bartender if we got half off the half off, to which he said, "Oh, yes, it's only 25%." After ordering more drinks, a different bartender says he thinks that's wrong, and then another one shoots it down all together, saying, "You're paying as much as everyone for their drinks, but everyone's special here." Which is, A) Lame; and B) We had been ordering drinks thinking they were at a hugely discounted price! We soon learned other contingencies of the "special." The free drinks that my friend had won did not include shots, and the half off was only on well drinks and house wine, and 8pm to 9pm was a dead zone in the night where none of these specials applied. Why were the rules suddenly changing so much? During this "dead zone" of 8pm-9pm, the half-off all drinks special went away, but select draft beers were $1. A bunch of us ordered these beers since we didn't have a special during this hour, but after ordering the beers the price was erased from the blackboard and changed to $2 - but then as soon as we paid for the beers we had ordered which suddenly cost us $2, the price was erased and changed back to $1. And then my friend was to get $50 put toward her tab there due to bringing in 20 friends, but they wouldn't give it to her that night, and weeks later she is having trouble getting the $50 because they are making her talk to a specific person there who is impossible to track down. All and all it was a bad experience, the bartenders and waitstaff kept changing the rules and seemed to hold some level of contempt for our party, the food was unpalatable, and aside from all that the aesthetic of the place was .... not good. Avoid.

text: Ok, before I get into my real review, I'll explain why subtracted a star from this place. It took me circling Maryland Plaza/Euclid/Kingshighway 3 separate times before I could find the flippin store! I was already in a bad mood, thus me venturing out to grab a cupcake, and this didn't help. Of course, I know I can't really base my review around location, especially when it's in the central west end, but the signage wasn't clear and it left me feeling extremely frustrated. I guess I'm just saying, don't expect this to be a very easy experience. Don't ever go into this part of the central west end in a hurry, wanting to just "pick something up really quick." Also, the woman behind the counter didn't even really greet me when I came in and when I was looking at the cupcakes questionably, waiting for some explanation of each, I got nothing. I would understand if she had a lot of other customers to take care of, but I was the only one in the place. No matter, I don't like to punish a good product too severely when that itself is fantastic. Onto the important stuff! I got the peanut butter cup cupcake and the red velvet. I was tempted to just stuff them into my mouth because I was so ready to eat them after my search for the shop, but I didn't think that would be the right thing to do. I knew these had to be savored. Aside from me scraping a bit of icing off each top and licking the divine goodness, I left them alone on my drive home. They aren't huge, but they aren't regular size cupcakes either, so I did cave and use a fork. The peanut butter cup was to die for!! I'm definitely not an icing person. I'm that guy who scrapes it off of every birthday/wedding cake or cupcake I've ever gotten and leave the pile on the edge of my plate like an unsatisfying-looking pile of sugar. HOWEVER, I'm sure I could have spread this peanut-butter icing on pizza and it STILL would have been delicious! It was like a whipped peanut butter, buttercream heaven. Not to mention, they sprinkle generous bits of reese's on top. I mean, cake is cake, but when you can top it with something like that, you get a masterpiece! I'm not sure I can be as enthusiastic about the red velvet, though still a wonderful cupcake! Very moist german chocolate cake with a smooth, whipped cream cheese icing. I didn't eat this one until later and split it with my husband. Maybe the reason I don't think of it like I do the peanut butter cup is because this cupcake was just a delightful dessert, not an escape from a horrible day. In any case, it was still wonderful. I still think I'm partial to the peanut butter. Overall, very tasty treats that I would love to go back for, but I think when I go back, I'd rather not drive myself.

Anyway, it was hot and I wanted to get out of there, away from the clutter, heat, and moldy/dusty book smell, but I had to wait until I caught the owner's attention to ask him about selling him my books before I could make a break for the door. Finally, I managed to ask my question, and I was told that they only trade store credit for people's books. That was disappointing, but I guess they really are just a book trader in the literal sense. text: This was HORRIBLE. I wanted to take my visiting parents on an airboat swamp tour. We made reservations for a small boat (4-6 people) two days prior. We arrived late because Jean Lafitte could not give us good directions, and all online directions (mapquest, google, etc) took us to a completely different location. Once we arrived they told us to follow them in our car to another airboat company location (Airboat Adventures) and pretty much just dropped us off. After standing around we finally discovered we had to go inside and stand in line to check in and get a colored ticket. Then we were told me would be called outside. After standing around with a bunch of people for 15 minutes, everyone just started walking outside to where the boats were. All the drivers were on the boats, but no one was giving directions. So we just stood there for a few minutes, and then people just started to get on the boats. After sitting on the boats for a few minutes, we realized that there were not enough seats per the reservations. Finally the management came outside and proceeded to make everyone get off the boats and do a "roll call" of who was on what boat. They made me and my parents get off the boat and said we had "big boat" tickets. I told her we did not. She said according to our color ticket, we did. I said, again, we had made a reservation for a small boat. She insisted and made us get off the boat. I said I wanted a refund for the difference between the boats. She said she no control over that, since we made the reservation through Jean Lafitte. I told her John Lafitte was gone for the day, and she said she couldn't help me. (Keep in mind this was all in front of 30 + people). After the roll call was finished (this took OVER 20 MINUTES), she finally figured out that there were enough seats, and we got to ride on the boat we had made the reservation for. However, the tour was amazingly disappointing. We saw two alligators at the beginning and watched the tour guide throw marshmallows at them. Then proceeded to drive to 4 different locations over the next hour, and just park in the middle of the swamp area and listen to him talk about his destitute life (not getting water on the job, the number of speeding tickets he has, his jail time, etc). The only enjoyment of the whole trip was the beauty of the swamp. Oh, and he failed to mention until halfway through the trip that people fall off the boat all the time and you need to hang on tight. (Thanks for the heads up, since I brought a nice camera to take pictures). I'm glad I paid for an hour and half of roll-count and mindless tour guide banter. This business is NOT professional and NOT recommended.

Frankly, that's unacceptable on two levels because not only is that crucial serving standard ignored but anyone who knows anything about pesce tacos knows that they ARE NOT fried. To top that off, our server mixed up our other friends burgers to the point where the one who wanted medium got well done and the one who wanted well got medium. Also - when we mentioned the mistake to her she apparently just wanted us to leave because she cleared all of our plates away without asking if we were finished - just because we hated the main portion doesn't mean we weren't going to eat the one mildly edible part (their frozen-from-the-bag-fries). To top it off, it took us two attempts to get our server to acknowledge our gift certificate. She was clearly not the brightest. The only super delicious part of the meal was the mac n cheese, which is honestly the only reason they are getting 2 stars. Get your shit together, Q BBQ. You have (in theory) an amazing menu but unfortunately you seem to not care about what you're serving. Also clean your lines in between kegs. You can advertise Great Lakes Christmas all you want but it seriously tasted and smelled like you just put it on a PBR line in hopes that no one would notice. text: I've been pretty impressed with this place. First things out of the way, I really don't care where a place is located or what it looks like unless it is clean and has delicious food. This place does have delicious food and got a 95 on their health inspection rating. So both criteria are met there. Now to the good stuff, the chicken. It is juicy and very flavorful. It is clear that they either put it in a spicy brine or marinade prior to cooking, and it makes all the difference. As for the style of the fried chicken, it comes out crisp with a spicy wet finish on the outside. I got the 400 degrees level and it was hot, but not enough to make me sweat. As a matter of fact, I didn't take the first sip of my soda until I was done. Given that I am spicy freak, this should be plenty hot enough for mortals (for reference, I can eat the spiciest thing Prince's has without batting an eye, I frequently consider using pepper spray as a condiment). But all in all, damn good fried chicken. For sides, they have spicy crinkle fries (hit the spot), baked beans (the way they are supposed to be made), cole slaw and potato salad. As well, they have a couple of random things like a burger(?) and they have fresh cookies for dessert. Another nice perk about this joint is the people that run it are friendly - great customer service. So there is another way they have Prince's beat. Their hours are a little wonky,. 11AM-3PM M-F and 11AM-1AM Saturday. As well, they only take cash, so make sure you come prepared or you'll be washing dishes. My wait time was very reasonable, a little less than 20 minutes, and they recommend you call in your order in advance.

text: My fiancee is throwing up her few bites of Liuzza's "sauteed" shrimp "remoulade" as I write this sad, sad review. Apparently Liuzza's is a beloved neighborhood institution, they seem like nice enough folks there, and the place was packed for dinner tonight. Oh, good. My fiancee has emerged from the bathroom alive, and is now describing her purge to me, Roseanne Roseannadanna-style. "Don't you hate when you throw up that soon after you eat, and..." Well. Look, I don't like it when people talk smack about my favorite restaurants, and it seems like lots of folks love this place, so I'm just going to get it over with. We sat down, ordered two Abita Ambers, and the waitress brings out the two coldest beers I've ever seen or tasted in my life. After a steamy 20 minute walk over, I can't tell you how awesome that was. It was definitely the highlight of the evening. A gentleman came to our table and said, "Alright, guys, wall of fame time," and pointed a camera at us. He took our sweaty picture, and then the sweaty pictures of everyone else who just walked in, and within minutes worked them into a photo slideshow that was displayed in the corner of the dining room. For the next 45 minutes, we all watched the same 25 picture loop of all the people who were right there in the room. Now that I think back on it, this was weird. We ordered the sauteed shrimp remoulade poboy and the crawfish telemachus, which was described on the menu as crawfish and pasta in a creamy sauce. Both were highly recommended in reviews we had read online. The dishes came out quickly. My crawfish telemachus was electric yellow, like ballpark nacho cheese. Her poboy was... I don't even know. What was intended to be remoulade sauce looked like straight-up mayonnaise, and there was tons of it, so the bread was soaked and the whole thing had to be eaten with a knife and fork. We had planned on splitting both dinners, as we often do, but that sandwich looked too unappetizing to even try. So I didn't. I was starving, and ended up eating a pretty good share of my pasta, which while edible, just tasted like butter. The crawfish tails were fine and cooked well, but the spaghetti was just about boiled to death. It was mush. The butter-flavored, neon sauce just had to be a mistake of some kind. It just had to be. With the crawfish picked out of my bowl and a couple bites or so of the poboy gone, we gave up our plates to the busboy and ended up waiting around for 20 minutes to get the check, during which time we got to contemplate working out our frustrations on Yelp and, were we total A-holes, just running out. In the end, of course, we forked over $45 for two plates of food we could only pick at and look upon with bewildered disgust. After we left, my fiancee told me that the shrimp on the poboy was totally stone cold. It was, however, cooked, and it was too cold to have simply not been cooked all the way through, so she assumed that it was supposed to be served that way. And maybe that's right. But I think a hot sandwich is pretty well implied if it has the word "sauteed" in the name. Anyway, she didn't send it back because, based on the way things were going, she didn't have high hopes about what would come back. Neither would have I. In the end, it didn't stay down. Maybe that's for the best. If I am someday so lucky as to have a head injury that causes me to forget that this evening ever took place, I may go back for one or two of those deliciously cold and huge beers at the bar. But to prepare for such an event, I'm going to leave little written reminders all over my apartment that I am not, under any circumstances, to order food, because they are into some truly nasty stuff back there in that kitchen.
label: NEG

text: Unfortunately, I'm giving FF two stars for overall experience even though the ice cream was fantastic. The service, not so much. A friend of mine and I arrived here late in the evening after a previous event in search of something refreshing on an overwhelmingly hot/humid night. We weren't expecting downright rude service from cranky staff members. I'm sorry your place of employment doesn't seem to have A/C and that you're probably suffering for minimum wage, but it's not my fault. I don't understand how a place that charges whopping fees for ice cream ONLY accepts cash. One could easily end up spending $50 or more for sundaes and the like for a family of 4. While I don't understand or like such a policy, I respect it. I don't respect, however, someone rudely pointing to a "We only take cash" sign with an exasperated expression as they sigh "No cards!" I also found it startling that the reply to my friend's request for a glass of water was a curt "We don't give out cups." It took several seconds of blank stares on our part before we were told we could go outside to the fountain where we could find cups. Except there were no cups until we asked again and another surly employee brought some out to us. All you have for customers is an outdoor water fountain? I'm pretty sure even soda fountains of yore provided water for their customers. After spending $16 on ice cream, you'd think we'd get some friendly service. I guess Old City hipsters feel they have better things to be doing than slinging milkshakes for tourists? Perhaps they'll reconsider their choice of employer in the future. I'll definitely go back and hope for a better experience. The ice cream itself was great - I had the mint chocolate chip which is made with real peppermint and super creamy. I had my scoops in a homemade waffle cone which was delicious if a little thick for my liking.

text: This is where I get my coffee almost every day while at work (I work on 3rd & Race in the TLA Entertainment offices.) So I have pretty regular experience with them, both purchasing drinks directly and individual drinks. The basic rundown is that the quality of the coffee beans are by far above average. And the iced coffee is a demonic broth that will make you feel like you just injected rocket fuel directly into your veins. (Your stomach may quickly alleviate you of that feeling, if you suffer from reflux.) After talking to one of the Barrista's about this - I suggested they were slipping crack cocaine in there - she said that the iced coffee is a mixture of all the roasts of the day, brewed double strength. So, there you go. Douse it with liquid sugar and a healthy amount of milk to cut the acid, and expect to get a lot of design and coding done before you crash and want to sleep under your desk for a week. They also have something called Balzac's blend here that is quite good. If you've ever read Balzac's humorous and incredibly verbose essay on the benefits of coffee, well... Yeah. It is well named. I wouldn't suggest going here for bulk tea though. Though the tea quality is fairly high it is apparent that they don't sell much of it- every time I've bought it it has been fairly stale. I suggest Remedy tea on Samson between 16th and 17th. Review of Remedy coming up in a bit.

text: OK, I'm very disappointed that I have to write a less than stellar review of a neighborhood venture. I just cant look past the fast that I paid over $12 dollars for a burger that I ended up throwing away. I decided to check it out one night while my wife was at work and I had the house to myself. Seeing all the positive feedback Sketch has been receiving and the fact that I live one street away had already formed a good opinion in my mind with out actually eating anything yet. I ordered the Kobe burger with pepperjack cheese and aioli sauce. I believe the total came to just below $13. First of all, that instantly takes it out of the family friendly category for me. I can't fathom spending $39.00 before drinks and tips for my wife and son, but then again, I'm middle class. Seems like there are many new to the hood, where this isn't an issue, I'm envious of you. Now I took my burger to go. I'm sitting at home, unwrapping the large sandwich, looking forward to my first bite. That's when I encounter my first problem and probably a personal preference, but it was an issue for me. The cheese was sliced way too thick. I had two quarter inch thick for a total of one half inch thick slice of cheese. They didn't melt at all and I like my cheese to some what melt. Maybe others like it this way, if that were my only problem, I'd give Sketch better review and make sure I tell the food prep person to slice thinner. My main issue and this is the deal sealer is that the burger was so salty it was gross. I could feel the salt crystals on my teeth when biting down. It was the nastiest taste. My best guess is that the slat shaker lid fell off when making this, I cant see how else this could happen. i was able to eat about a quarter or so before the taste was so bad I tossed it. If any of the Sketch people see this, please ditch the salt, leave it up to the individual eater to put salt/pepper on their own burger. I'm sure this was just a aberration since I didn't see anything in other reviews saying this, but it was enough for me.

text: The old Arbys has been transformed. It is now Chinese selling combo meals from as little as $5.99 to no more than $8.95. Cheap eats in sufficient quantity for a meal. No MSG. Free delivery in a limited area for a $10 minimum. The owners claim this is not just another Panda Express or "Americanized Chinese Food," but on my visit, it looked like standard Americanized Chinese food: Moo Goo Gai Pan; Orange Chicken; Sesame Pork; Mongolian Beef or Chicken; Fried Rice; Won Ton Soup; Egg Rolls and about 20 other predictable Americanized dishes. But if you stop and think, would we really eat authentic Chinese Food? Think, chicken heads and feet, fungus, dogs and cats. Yum yum! If you sold authentic Chinese food in the US, you'd be broke in a New York second. The only dishes that seemed that they might be authentic were the Keyone and Yazzyon Soups. I searched the net and no one has a record of such a soups, so they probably aren't Authentic Chinese. The "Y" soups are a pricy $7.50 per bowl. After tasting several of the dishes, this place earned only one star. The Mongolian Beef was horrible and a dish that I could not eat: spongy texture to the meat, and sickly sweet instead of spicy as promised. Two of the chicken dishes had better texture, but still too sweet and really lacking in flavor. The egg rolls were soggy, white steamed rice ok, shrimp fried rice was passible but bland. Too bad, no Brown Rice. Of six meals consumed, no one gave a rating better than two. I'm still a bit intrigued by the Y Soups, but afraid I'd be wasting my time and my money and still walk away hungry as I did when I left my Mongolian Beef. All in all, this is the second worst Asian food I've ever eaten. I'd rather have Panda Express any day. Or the Arbys it used to be. And I'm not a big fan of either.

text: As soon as I sat down, three different people came over, and welcomed me to the family (the "family" having something to do with some guy named Keven who owns this place, among other places.) Would my companion and I have some of the sweet tea? No, it was dinner and too late for me to have tea (plus I'm diabetic, okay?), so we asked for water. "Have you been here before? You are in for a treat!" said the server. Then the way, way, overly faux-ingratiating hostess lady came up and re-introduced us to the second guy who was "taking care of us" that evening, who had already introduced himself. She'll bring that sweet tea right over, she said, I guess doing a high- pressure upsell. "No," we had to make clear, again, that we did not want the sweet tea. I panicked and mentioned the diabetes. So, already, apologizing for not ordering food. Okay. This woman was a real personality plus. We were part of the family now, having sat down, and recieved the menus. After being called multiple pet names, she asked, "Have you been here before? You are in for a treat!" She told us about the specials, one of which was the chicken in a basket that she made clear was not on the menu, and some baked catfish. The server (second person to enter the scene) came back. I pointed to an option that said "Fried chicken with 2 sides, $13-16." I named my 2 sides and; he asked what size I wanted. Assuming the prices had to do with size, so I said "small." My companion ordered the baked catfish special. Then the hostess came over and asked what I wanted my fried chicken to be. She named a bunch of combinations very quickly and I wasn't sure what was going on, so i just said "The standard one," since I thought I'd already ordered a small, and she said, "Chicken in a basket," and left. I was not crazy about the atmosphere of this place. It was indeed very gleaming and clean (so clean that someone sprayed down the seats with some kind of cleaning solvent in front of us, which was, to say the least, unappetizing) and I know the contrast between the sleek, club-ish vibe and down-home food was intentional, but I didn't dig it. I don't like to eat fried chicken under a green lightbulb over a tiny, square white plate. And it was too dark to really read the menu, which brings me to... It turns out the chicken in the basket with the sides I'd ordered was $10 more total on the bill than the one I'd originally pointed to, because it was supposed to be coming with fries or something and included different pieces of meat. Also, my bf ended up with the fried catfish, not the special, but I don't know whose fault this was. I mentioned it to the hostess, that I was confused, and she was like, "Well, I'll take half the blame!" Then she went over to the original server, pointed to me, and said, "She didn't know what she was ordering!" Damn straight! Had I realized I was ordering a $24 meal, I would have returned it. I never said anything about replacing my side of fries! The pricing and menu was totally confusing, and none of the servers clarified things. (By the way, that half the blame comment certainly didn't mean she took anything off the price.) But what they did do was put on this huge show of how we were loved family members, beautiful, etc. The hostess went on and on about us getting a "friends and family" coupon, about how we should come to the Halloween thing they were throwing, and how the guy who said "Whasssssup!" in those commercials would be there (How many people did THAT draw in?) It was way uncomfortable. I understand soul food has a homemade appeal, and I'm all for it, and if the place was really run by some grandmotherly woman handing down her recipes I think I would appreciate some of the friendliness, if not the insanely high-pressure sales approach. I love restaurants where the cooks and waitresses treat you like family. It's great. The thing is, this felt like nothing but FAKE. There is no Aunt Tootsie. The place is slick, dark, and modern inside, with fancily-printed up menus and everything else, and its obviously run by some rich entreprenureal business guy, and they weren't trying to feed us, they were trying to sell stuff to us. As for the food, the fried chicken and sides were okay. I have had better and worse, but the quality was nothing special and not especially meaty. Totally not worth the price, but that never would have bothered me so much (despite the fact that I'm obviously a cheapskate) if I hadn't felt like I was being pressured to buy a timeshare during the entire meal. All in all, I would say ten to fifteen minutes of our meal was spent listening to this woman's pitch. So very unpleasant!

text: My fiancee and I had a horrible experience with 33 Jewels. We thought getting our engagement ring from a small company would be better than an impersonal big company, but that was totally wrong. Go to Blue Nile, or if you want palladium like we did, check out McGiverns (cheaper but you have to get insurance on your own). Even places like Fred Meyer or Ben Bridge are more worth the price you'll pay because they actually offer service and insurance in exchange for the markup. 33 Jewels was a total mistake! We ordered an engagement ring from Diane Garmendia, co-owner of 33 Jewels, who told us it'd arrive during our Winter break (it was my Christmas gift from my fiancée). She didn't tell us it was going to be delayed. She ruined our Christmas. It didn't arrive until the second week of January, and when it did, it was loose on my finger. Diane told me that it'd fit better when the weather got warmer. She also said we'd get the appraisal for the ring (so we could insure it, since the diamond wasn't certified) in a couple of weeks, so we took the ring and paid her for it. Fast forward to April. The ring was still way too big, and we still didn't have the appraisal. We finally went back to 33 Jewels to ask for the appraisal and check the ring's size. Turns out the ring was almost a size 7 (we ordered a 6.5), and on top of that Diane had done a bad sizing job the first time because after I made Diane go through all the ring sizers, she found I was actually a size 6.25. Either 33 Jewels never checked the size of the ring they delivered to us or they just didn't care. They said they'd fix it in under a week and get back to us, along with the appraisal. We had to call them to see when if was ready, and when I went back to get it, they still didn't have the appraisal. And on top of that, when I got home, I found out that the ring was damaged! There was a set of deep tool-marks on both sides of the ring (like from a vise) and filing marks all along the back, top, and bottom of the ring. It hadn't been polished at all. We got it sized, and found it was a 6.00 (which Diane had said would be too small). Diane had inspected the ring and checked its size before giving it to me, too, so she knew perfectly well what she was giving me, and didn't care at all about the shoddy workmanship. We took the ring back to 33 Jewels, and Diane said she'd fix it for us. She also said she'd email me a copy of the appraisal and took down my contact information. Another week passed and we didn't hear anything. At this point, we decided that we had had enough and just wanted my fiancee's money back. He called 33 Jewels to ask for a refund. Turns out that they don't give refunds, even though they never delivered on what we ordered (a correctly sized ring with an appraisal). Diane never told either of us that she had an "all sales final" policy. She claimed the ring was "custom", but really, we picked a stock design from a catalog, and the only "custom" part of it was the center stone ... which is no different from getting a semi-mount and stone at any jewelry store. We tried to get a chargeback through my fiancee's credit card company, but more than 60 days had passed so Chase wouldn't do it. After Diane heard we wanted a chargeback, she suddenly realized she had our contact information. She called multiple times to say that there was nothing wrong with the ring, and there had never been anything wrong with the ring (?!), and that we were being completely unreasonable in wanting his money back. She claimed she hadn't called him to say the ring was ready before because she had the wrong number on file, even though his number was correctly written on the receipt. She said what she put us through was "totally normal" according to her "experienced friends in the business", and that there was no way she'd even consider a refund because she didn't think she did anything wrong. Diane also insinuated that she thought the real problem was our relationship and she offered me counseling of all things. Diane's calls were getting progressively nastier, so my fiancee decided we should just pick up the ring and hold off on filing complaints about 33 Jewels before they did something else bad to us, like damaging the ring on purpose as revenge. When he finally went back to get it this last time, Diane finally gave him the appraisal. The appraisal was just a Word document with a picture of the ring on it. A 3rd grader could have made something that looked just as official. They managed to remove the deep tool-marks, but damaged the prongs, which may not be fixable. So now my fiancée and I are stuck with a damaged ring and an appraisal we don't trust. We're obviously pissed about the BS 33 Jewels put us through and don't want to be reminded of it, so I have not worn it since we got it back. We will be selling it and buying another ring elsewhere if we can't force a return. Avoid 33 Jewels at all costs!

text: To sum it up: Excellent service justifies the tiny tables that you barely have room to eat on. The ambiance and atmosphere is sexy and the wine to slide down with cheeses and strawberries is delicious. The veggie burger was great but the fries were too greased up. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ After a handful of visits to Vintage I finally decided to give this bar a review. It's easy to get to from the train so if you're looking to save on parking fees, it's a win-win for Jersey commuters. Since the location is in proximity of other delicious bars, restaurants, and snacks so there is always a back-up plan five steps away. Vintage offers outdoor seating but be weary since the sidewalk is uneven, you may be in store for the food landing on your lap and not in your mouth. I've seen this happen to someone next to us once. They laughed it off but who the hell wants to walk around with 'risotto crotch' for the next few hours. Vintage is perfect for a date but not so great with large crowds of +4 who want to be seated, unless you're okay with 2 standing and 2 sitting around a tiny table. Each time I go I get a Riesling wine flight of 3 sample glasses for $15. I love the option and it's a great way to test out other wines that you my not have otherwise chosen. I tasted the beer on tap and as a non-beer drinking, not bad. The guest who had the beer agreed that it was pretty tasty. The staff is very friendly and they are familiar faces. I love to see an establishment that keeps their employees consistent even months in between visits. I never have to wait long for a refill or to have my food appear...they are on top of things for damn sure. 5 stars on service. Last night I had the cheese plate ($12?) and the veggie burger--overall it was a low 4 star. The cheese plate had a great presentation, went well with the wines but I wouldn't say any cheese 'wow-ed' me. The bread and fruit was fresh and complimented my wines. The veggie burger had been changed up since I last had it and had raw onions, maybe a different topping this time. If you have never had a veggie burger or want to try something out of the realm of meat then this is the perfect opportunity. The side of fries were greasy and ruined the taste that could be a perfect fry underneath it all. I recommend Vintage and will be back again.

text: Yay for my 200th review, and a 5-star one to boot! We came here with our group of 10, Groupon in tow ($75 for 10 people, 2 hours of bowling, shoe rental, and 6 appetizers). They didn't treat us like crap just because we had already paid. In fact, service was VERY attentive and we had someone coming by every 20 minutes or so to make sure we had everything we needed. We had the following appetizers, and I think we all appreciated the fact that they waited for all of us to arrive-- food came out hot and fresh, not cold and rubbery because it was out too early. 1) crab and cheese dip 2) mac and cheese bites 3) loaded potato skins 4) buffalo chicken bites 5) artichoke and spinach dip 6) cheeseburger sliders I was able to try everything except the artichoke and spinach dip and the cheeseburger sliders. Very very good, although the buffalo chicken bites were a tad on the dry side. The loaded potato skins are to die for! You seriously do not get food this good at bowling alleys...I'm so used to buying a grease bomb at an overpriced stand. This was a pleasant surprise. I was particularly impressed by the look of the bowling alley. We pulled up, parked, and said something along the lines of "Oh man, I wonder if this is one of those old-fashioned bowling alleys." NOPE! It was absolutely gorgeous inside (did they renovate recently?). The shoes were brand new, or so they seemed, because they were still stiff and clean. The balls weren't all chipped and grimy, plus they had a good selection of weights and finger sizes. Bathrooms are spotless. Our entire group had so much fun and some friendly competition. Thank you, Pinsetter!

text: Upselling, high repair costs, and general douchebaggery are the hallmarks of this bike shop. My buddy and I are relatively serious riders, and we've gone to Breakaway a few times in the past, but only out of necessity, because it stays open later than the other bike shops west of Broad St. We have the knowledge and tools to fix the most common bike problems and many of the uncommon ones. Sometimes we need a new specialized tool and don't want to wait the time it would take to arrive from an online order, so one time we went here to see if they had a specific tool to disassemble a squeaky pedal (look axle tool). First of all, turns out that they didn't have the tool. Secondly, instead of just telling us that, we got total flak for even asking. "Why would you want that? Did you try this? Do you know it's not this? What about this? Let me just take a look at your bike..." Their strategy is to put your bike up in the stand, give it a quick look, then tell you all sorts of things that you could honestly fix on your own with a few simple steps and cheap tools, and then charge you an ass-load for it. Another time I came here looking for a spoke, a $0.50 part, to replace one that I had broken earlier that day on a ride. The dude gave me the "Let me just take a look at your bike" line, so I gave it to him, he puts it up on the bike stand, starts cranking away on the pedal, checking all sorts of things that I didn't ask him to look at, and then said he wanted to charge me $25... to replace one single broken spoke! A few occasions I've come in to the shop looking for specific accessories, like an extra bottle cage or new bike shorts, and although I was "helped" by one of the staff, they consistently tried to upsell me to a more expensive alternative that I don't want or need, or they'd suggest companion products that I neither asked for nor need (no, I don't want chamois butter. i guess my ass just doesn't chafe as much as yours) I understand that they are trying to run a business, and businesses have to make money, but it's my opinion that this place is taking advantage of many riders.

text: Thank you, Arturo!!! After being snubbed by some other Indy restaurants when trying to make a reservation, my stepfather advised me of this place Indy should be incredibly thankful for. For starters, while sipping on the presecco and decorating the bachelorette in her tiara for the evening, we had the calamari and artichoke. The calamari was lightly breaded with a marinara, very basic and simple but well done. The calamari wasn't drenched in batter so as to lose its taste but more of a light pan fry. The artichoke was the only average part of the meal--anywhere else it may have been a highlight. The orders for the table of 9 were a variety of main dishes, all of which received superb reviews--even from my younger sister who never finishes a meal ate every morsel of her penne pasta. I had the spaghetti and meatballs because I couldn't resist the description of homemade veal meatballs AND homemade pasta. I try to avoid ordering pasta at a restaurant but it was well worth it. The table also shared a couple of great, moderately priced wines. They had a nice selection. Before ordering our desserts, our waiter--who was one of the best serves I've ever had--leaned in to me and asked if we wanted a little time after the table cleared so the bride to be could finish opening her gifts. Service was prompt and friendly, Lauren I think her name was, really sweet; she offered to turn on the heater above us so I could enjoy the meal without cowering under my companion's jacket... Clam Chowder: Yuuum...it didn't even need any pepper, it was seasoned to perfection, just the right consistency. Lobster Bisque: Delicious as well, not overly salted like most. Soju Bloody Mary: My new favorite drink, I scoured SB the rest of the evening for this, and the "soju" mary we had with breakfast the next day tasted like watered down horseradish sauce/cocktail sauce. This, however, was perfection in a pint. Salted/peppered rim with limes and a celery stalk. Main Lobster: I finally fulfilled my fantasy of Daryl Hannah in "Splash" when she went to town on an entire lobster. It was however, split in half when it arrived, but I just wanted to say that I've had an entire lobster, not just the tails like most restaurants serve it. I've never used claw crackers before, but there's a first time for everything, and it was worth the non-work. I not only drenched all the edible meat in the melted butter tin they gave me, I also took the remaining precious liquid as an after dinner shot. Alaskan King Crab Legs: Fabulous, the meat by itself was buttery, but wouldn't you know that it came with it's own companion of melted butter heaven. Not to mention, kinda loved the coleslaw and onion rings....so wrong but so good. All in all, we were seated on the outside deck, facing the sunset, stuffing out faces with alcohol and butter sea goodness. It was an awesome ending to what might possibly be an incredible beginning.

text: I've been to a lot of post offices because I used to do a fair amount of eBay shipping. So, I in my old stomping grounds of Boston and Glastonbury, CT I knew the places which were good and bad. There's normally one person at a window and two others milling around making jokes or talking about someones grandchild and distracting the one teller that is actually attempting to re-enact something the rest of us call working. For a post office that resides so close to UPENN and Wharton, you'd think that some of the smarts would have rubbed off. Their flow of operations is terrible. Today their was an issue with a money order. So, three ladies sat around trying to read someones faded license... the line gradually grew longer until it was out the door. Hot Tip: If you hear someone in front of you say "passport application," "money order," or "international shipping," turn around and walk out the door unless you have 10-20 minutes to wait for that one person's needs. The only saving grace for this place is that they have a free tape dispenser for you to finish up wrapping your packages. Most post offices require you to buy tape from their merchandise rack at an extra $3.99. If you get them at a sleepy time of day, things will be just fine. I looked up the recipe online after trying it and noticed that this restaurant doesn't really use the real noodles in most recipes. They use instant noodles. Tastes great to me though! Also not bad is their shrimp & pineapple triangles appetizer. Other than the noodles, the rest of the dishes are actually quite small (~$11-12 each) so a little pricey. Don't have the sweet and sour fish because it was fishy-tasting. The curry was good. Tamarind chicken was meh. I didn't have any desserts but they looked interesting. Decor was good. Place was really clean. I think they just recently opened up. Service was good and food came out pretty quickly. Oh yeah, try the pineapple-coconut juice. It's really good! Apparently, they juice it fresh in the restaurant.

The soup was extra salty and the sandwich was seriously a piece of turkey between two tiny pieces of bread. Unfortunately, I didn't notice you could ask for mayo or mustard for a mere $.75 extra at the time I placed my order. Perhaps it's my own fault for assuming that a sandwich is more than meat and bread. The service was mediocre at best. The only reasons I might consider going back is because it's near my apartment and relatively cheap. If that ever happens I will definitely order something different. Sorry, but I'm far from impressed.

text: Planned a move with these guys after reading the great reviews on Yelp, and have to say I wasn't impressed. I've moved with professional movers before, and these guys just aren't it. The guys who showed up (half an hour late) were perfectly nice, but obviously had very little moving experience and also moved incredibly slowly. After it took TWO AND A HALF HOURS for them to load the first half of our stuff (and we just have a small one bedroom apartment), I finally gave up and started moving stuff too, because I was afraid we wouldn't get out of our building in time. I'm a pretty small female and I was able to move more stuff than they did, and that was in between me having to explain to them basic things about how to move (e.g. helping them figure out how to fit stuff through doors and into the elevators). My two favorite moments had to be: 1. Halfway through all three guys took a load of stuff down in the elevator (don't ask me why that required three people), and in the time it took them to come back I moved the entire rest of the contents of the apartment to the area in front of the elevator. When they finally got back, they seemed impressed and said, "wow, you're fast!" Thanks, but isn't that THEIR job? 2. At one point I saw one of them carrying a small table that has casters on it. I said, "You know you can push that, it has wheels," to which he replied "not anymore!" and showed me that he had somehow managed to snap off one of the casters. It ended up taking six hours to move about 30 blocks with these guys (compared to the seven hours it took when I moved to Philly from NYC with actual professionals). Again, they were perfectly nice, but you could get the same level of help by showing up at a college campus and offering free pizza to the first couple of kids you saw. If you want to pay for professional movers, use a company with actual professionals.
label: NEG

text: Many a hangover mornings have been spent at this place a block from my loft. This place is as close to a hipster SF restaurant as I have seen, but take that as a compliment. I love a place that uses local ingredients and they proudly do so. BELT and rooster slinger are always worth the price of admission. Not a big bloody mary fan (damn you Purdue homecoming '00), but their bloody mary list is as impressive as I have seen. Definitely a downtown treasure.
label: POS

text: It warms my cold, dark heart that so many other Yelpers have not-so great things to say about Marathon Grill. Yes, the menu sounds better than it actually is, and often - at least when you get delivery - they will mess up your order. I have a particular gift for really craving one particular thing - fruit salad, for example - and having that be the one thing that's never in the bag. So basically, it's overpriced and overhyped and what shows up is not what you expected. It's a lot like finding dates on match.com. They are pretty good about bringing what they inevitably forget later - but who wants to wait another 45 minutes for your tiny thing of cantaloupe and berries? Your overpriced omelette will get cold and gelatinous in that time, and not in a good way. Btw, this applies to Marathons across the city and not just this locale. They do have healthier options, so a lot of my friends order from them pretty often even though I roll my eyes and mildly tantrum if it's suggested.
label: NEG

text: I was in the mood for some cheap grease (sue me!) and ordered for take out a modestly priced appetizer sized shrimp basket. I received 4 jumboUNDERCOOKED shrimp. The staff is less than friendlky and the shrimp experience is only one of my run ins with PPG but def my last. I you want this kind of food take yourself and money to Chef Ken's on Germantown Ave but this place is a fail. Womp.

text: Another consistently good restaurant that I am so thankful is standing the test of time in Philadelphia. The chalkboard menu changes daily but not drastically. If the chicken pie is on it, I'm getting it, without fail. It's the perfect amount of food - a nice pillow of mostly shredded chicken with some gravy, carrots, onions, and maybe a few peas on a mixed green salad. I'm not a huge eater but I think this is a big meal and I still always clean my plate. Love it. I think one time I actually teared up when I got there and saw them erasing the chicken pie from the chalkboard because of a freak kitchen accident. The pulled pork sandwich is definitely a tasty and hearty second choice for me, but the pot pie and I have a relationship. If neither of those show up the duck salad is remarkable. A whole roasted duck leg on a hearty, mixed green salad, nice and lightly dressed. Dear lord, everything on this menu is exceptional. And there are plenty of veggie options too, like the beet salad, veggie chili or chick pea sandwich. I think the priciest thing on the menu is probably in the mid-twenties and even though I doubt I've had it because that generally exceeds my price range, I don't doubt that it's worth it though. The beer selection is proudly local: Sly Fox, PBC, Lancaster, Flying Fish, Troegs, Victory etc... Similarly, they support local farmers as well, typically buying all of their produce from Fishtown's Greensgrow Farms (when it's seasonally appropriate of course) and other 'Buy Fresh, Buy Local' contributors.
label: POS

text: This place is so close to home, and my friend -- who is pregnant with twins -- was quite hungry, so I wanted to love the place. No dice. The underwater murals on the walls were whimsical, the menu was ambitious and the lunch-special prices were great. That, however, is pretty much where it ends. We each started with the Tom Kha soup and salad. The salad was really tasty, but we can make a dressing of vinegar, sugar and fish sauce at home, and soup was sweet and quite bland - no heat and little to no galanga(l). I ordered the pad thai (often my first "baseline" dish at a new Thai place) and it too suffered from being overly sweet - no tamarind flavor and they served it with an orange wedge instead of lime; additionally, it was a bit oily and the chicken was like rubber. My friend, who loves fried rice, ordered the Thai fried rice only to discover that it had *frozen* peas, lima beans and carrot cubes in it. Service-wise, I have to say Thai Chef fell flat too. The two women working that afternoon were definitely uninterested in being there and in the customers' experience. They rushed all of the entrees to the table while diners were still eating the first courses: the woman behind us asked if they could keep the entree in an oven or something while so it wouldn't get cold while they ate their appetizers and the server replied that she could heat it in microwave. Egad! Otherwise, the servers pretty much kept to themselves - no refilling of water glasses or checking on how our meals were. Overall, the sort of dining experience that leaves one asking what happened and why.
label: NEG

text: There is not much I can say about Dim Sum Garden that hasn't been said before. Every time I go I get those phenomenal soup dumplings. (Or, if you want to sound smart and cultured, xiao long bao.) Absolutely out of this world, so tasty and fun to eat too. I'm glad I read how to eat them before visiting, though, or I imagine I'd be totally lost. The trick is to bit a small hole, suck out the soup, and then eat the dumpling. Even with this method I usually end up spilling a little. Just adds to the fun though! Of course, I can't ignore those scallion pancakes. Perfectly crisp and tasty and well complemented by the dipping sauces provided on the table. I have no idea what either of them are, but both are really good. I like sticking the dumplings in them after getting the soup out too. I like taking a friend or two to split these with otherwise I will seriously gorge myself. Not that I don't otherwise. So next time you maybe just got out of a show at the Troc or have a good twenty minutes until your train arrives at Market East but your tummy's grumbling, skip the toasted ravioli from WaWa (though that's good too) and stop by Dim Sum Garden. Probably the same price, too!
label: POS

text: I was hoping to try some local flavor on a recent visit. It's a nice local place with friendly staff. Everything was cooked pretty well - in an academic kind of way. I mean that it was cooked properly and correctly, but was uninspiring. There was no zing - nothing to rave about it. I split the sampler platter with my wife. The best was the pulled pork. It was juicy and flavorful. The ribs were somewhat tender but a little dry. The brisket was juicy. The chicken was dry. The problem with the ribs, brisket, and the chicken was the lack of flavor. You'll definitely need lots of sauce without flavor in the meat. We tried the "hot" and the 911 sauces. The hot was too sweet and no trace of pepper. The 911 was much better with visible pepper seeds and the right mix of slight sweetness, smokiness, and spice. If I were to go back I'd like to try a sausage and stick with the pulled pork sandwich or platter. I do agree with the other reviewer that the food temperature seemed strangely cold. We had a side of mac and cheese and potato salad. They both seemed homemade and had good flavor. My son had a bbq'd cheeseburger which he seemed to enjoy. It came with chips which were good too. Not sure if they were bagged or locally made.

text: I recently chose to use 'Tours by Isabelle' for a West Bank Plantation tour in New Orleans. I chose this particular company because they offer smaller group tours, which I find more personal, rather then big bus tours other companies offer. There was a total of eight people on our tour. We visited two plantations, Laura Plantation and Oak Valley. One of the nice things about this company is that they pick you up right at your hotel. Our driver was super friendly and a wealth of information regarding everything you could possibly know about New Orleans, from the cities history to alligator hunting. He encouraged us to ask questions on the drive and I can honestly say that I've never learned so much from a driver of a tour. The only thing that I had an issue with is the fact that when you sign up for a tour, its not confirmed until they have at least five people for the tour. Although I totally understand the reasoning of this, our tour wasn't confirmed until right before we left for our trip, this was after we were willing to change our first requested date. So if it would have been canceled, we would have had to find another company at the last minute. I would definetely use 'Tours by Isabelle' again!

text: I was in town for Tales of the Cocktail July 8-12th. The Hotel Monteleone where my conference was going to be at was already sold out, so I booked at the Ambassador. I was a little nervous that it would be a bad area, but walking to and from the French Quarter wasn't bad at all - a little bit of a hike in the hot weather, but the area was pretty safe. It's near Harrah's Casino and a lot of people are always walking around. The hotel itself wasn't bad either - yes it's old and no, there aren't any windows in the room, but it had beautiful high ceilings and was pretty updated as far as furniture and what not. I would never stay at the Ambassador again, though. First off, I booked my stay by calling in and found out about a "buy one night get the next night free" promotion. Awesome! So I was staying four nights and only paid for three - the promotion was only for weekdays, so I paid for one weekday and two weekend nights. Got to the hotel to check in and they only had me staying one night. The lady at the desk said "Not sure what you heard but you only here one night, sweetie, not three." Uh, ok. She then said "Wake up early and talk to the manager." Not an "I'll figure this out" or "Let me get your room number and have the manager talk to you," but more of a "Your problem, welcome to New Orleans." The next morning I talked to the lady at the front desk who told me that not everyone who works at The Ambassador knew about the buy one get one night free promotion yet. Turns out they had me checked in for the first night and the next night, the free night, was a manual check in that wasn't in the system - their system couldn't handle the promotion. Ok, fine. I was told the reservation was 4 nights as I originally asked for. Came back to the hotel at 5 pm and my room key didn't work. After walking 10 blocks in the New Orleans heat, I was frustrated. Front desk told me again that they couldn't find my reservation, so I had to explain that I actually had 3 different reservations because of THEIR promotion. They found the reservation and reactivated my key. This happened every day for the next three days - I had to reactivate my key and check back in, explaining why I had three reservations. Housekeeping was another issue, but the least of my worries there. I am now the owner of three new hair clips and got to smell three days of take out food... Last day, before checking out, I checked my credit card and saw that I in fact was charged for four days instead of the three. Went to check out and asked the guy at the front desk of The Ambassador New Orleans to print me out a receipt. He couldn't find my reservation and then said "Well, honey, we don't charge your credit card until you check out." I explained that I had been checked out three times already and he said, rudely, "Why did you check out already - how would I know to look for that?" I was mad by then and a manager stepped up and explained to him that it was a promotion that checked me out, not my mistake. There's still an extra room night charge on my credit card, though, four charges in total, one for each night they checked me out. End of story - stay at another hotel besides the Ambassador Hotel New Orleans. If you're on vacation and want to enjoy your stay, the staff at Ambassador Hotel will not make it enjoyable.
label: NEG

text: Is it just me, or five years ago, did this place have much better inventory than they do now? Initially, Beyond the Wall was more of a poster gallery who paid the electricity bill by peddling Belushi "College" prints, Dave Matthews Band black-light numbers, and all the Pulp Fiction you could take. But what was cool was the fact that they had all the '60s and '70s film posters, lots of replicas of French advertising art (before that too, became cliche), and even some terribly kitschy Tiger Beat-themed posters of former heart-throbs. (The Christian Slater "Gleaming the Cube" jawn I gave my boo in '02 outlasted me by a longshot) I recently ventured back into BtW, looking to upgrade my maxi-pad with some Paul Newman, Robert Redford, and Steve McQueen love on the walls (purely plutonic) and I've come to find that this place has moved entirely into the trite. Another one bites the dust. This place puts Spencer's Gifts and all the mallrat stores to shame, but I hate having to eBay all the cool crap that they used to carry. Bring it back.

text: Ok, here's the deal. The decor leaves little to be desired. I mean SO little that were it daytime I might consider wearing my sunglasses but at night I don't find that socially acceptable. The booths are dated, the artwork...well there isn't any, the walls are pink, the carpet is dingy, the place needs an Extreme Home Makeover Asian Restaurant edition! The food however, was pretty good! I was impressed given the few reviews and the spread of 1 to 5 stars. It sounds like it's definitely dependent on what you order, so let me break it down. I had vegetable egg foo young (soooo not good for you even though "vegetable" is in the name, but it reminds me of home, because my mom always ordered it), and chicken chow mein. I asked beforehand whether or not the chicken was white meat which I've found in Tucson is key. I also asked for light oil which my server seemed to understand. Both dishes came out relatively quick and were pretty darn enjoyable. The chicken chow mein was the better of the two, but the crispy noodles were kinda redic. I guess in Tucson you can't find those really thin ones like they sell in Asian supermarkets? Here they are wide and almost wonton-like...odd. In any case, I finished about 1/3 of each dish and was pretty satisfied after. The menu reads like the menu from a Chinese restaurant I frequented growing up. The servers speak VERY little English, but the place fit the bill. Oh, and the bill was cheap given the amount of food. I will surely be back to try more of the menu, and maybe they'll have painted by then?
label: POS

text: While Tijuana Taco Shop has been my fave Mexican restaurant in Wilmington for years on end, I can see El Diablo Burritos making their way into regular rotation when I'm fiending for good Mexican food. El Diablo Burritos does one thing: burritos and they do them quite well. Perhaps their biggest strength is that they don't overstuff their burritos, so as to make them unmanageable to eat with your hands. That said, their burritos remind me of Cali-style burritos, with substantial portions and rich flavor. They aren't quite as over-the-top as a Mission burrito or one of the beefy bombs from Benny's Burrito's NYC; they're almost a junior version of that. I had the pork burrito and the meat was tender and the pineapple salsa was very flavorful.
